5.12.e: Who, Agni, in alliance with thy foeman, what splendid helpers won for them their riches?  Agni, who guard the dwelling-place of falsehood? Who are protectors of the speech of liars?

5.12.d: सखायस ते विषुणा अग्न एते शिवासः सन्तो अशिवा अभूवन | अधूर्षत सवयम एते वचोभिर रजूयते वर्जिनानि बरुवन्तः ||
5.12.e: Agni, those friends of thine have turned them from thee: gracious of old, they have become ungracious.  They have deceived themselves by their own speeches, uttering wicked words against the righteous.

5.12.d: यस ते अग्ने नमसा यज्ञम ईट्ट रतं स पात्य अरुषस्य वर्ष्णः | तस्य कषयः पर्थुर आ साधुर एतु परसर्स्राणस्य नहुषस्य शेषः ||
5.12.e: He who pays sacrifice to thee with homage, O Agni, keeps the Red Steer's Law eternal;  Wide is his dwelling. May the noble offspring of Nahuṣa who wandered forth come hither.

5.13.d: अर्चन्तस तवा हवामहे ऽरचन्तः सम इधीमहि | अग्ने अर्चन्त ऊतये ||
5.13.e: WITH songs of praise we call on thee, we kindle thee with songs of praise,  Agni, with songs of praise, for help.

5.13.d: अग्ने सतोमम मनामहे सिध्रम अद्य दिविस्प्र्शः | देवस्य दरविणस्यवः ||
5.13.e: Eager for wealth, we meditate Agni's effectual praise to-day,  Praise of the God who touches heaven.

5.13.d: अग्निर जुषत नो गिरो होता यो मानुषेष्व आ | स यक्षद दैव्यं जनम ||
5.13.e: May Agni, Priest among mankind, take pleasure in our songs of praise,  And worship the Celestial Folk.

5.13.d: तवम अग्ने सप्रथा असि जुष्टो होता वरेण्यः | तवया यज्ञं वि तन्वते ||
5.13.e: Thou, Agni, art spread widely forth, Priest dear and excellent; through thee  Men make the sacrifice complete.

5.13.d: तवाम अग्ने वाजसातमं विप्रा वर्धन्ति सुष्टुतम | स नो रास्व सुवीर्यम ||
5.13.e: Singers exalt thee, Agni, well lauded, best giver of our strength:  So grant thou us heroic might.

5.13.d: अग्ने नेमिर अरां इव देवांस तवम परिभूर असि | आ राधश चित्रम रञ्जसे ||
5.13.e: Thou Agni, as the felly rings the spokes, encompassest the Gods.  I yearn for bounty manifold.

5.14.d: अग्निं सतोमेन बोधय समिधानो अमर्त्यम | हव्या देवेषु नो दधत ||
5.14.e: ENKINDLING the Immortal, wake Agni with song of praise: may he bear our oblations to the Gods.

5.14.d: तम अध्वरेष्व ईळते देवम मर्ता अमर्त्यम | यजिष्ठम मानुषे जने ||
5.14.e: At high solemnities mortal men glorify him the Immortal, best  At sacrifice among mankind.

5.14.d: तं हि शश्वन्त ईळते सरुचा देवं घर्तश्चुता | अग्निं हव्याय वोळ्हवे ||
5.14.e: That he may bear their gifts to heaven, all glorify him Agni, God,  With ladle that distilleth oil.

5.14.d: अग्निर जातो अरोचत घनन दस्यूञ जयोतिषा तमः | अविन्दद गा अपः सवः ||
5.14.e: Agni shone bright when born, with light killing the Dasyus and the dark:  He found the Kine, the Floods, the Sun.

5.14.d: अग्निम ईळेन्यं कविं घर्तप्र्ष्ठं सपर्यत | वेतु मे शर्णवद धवम ||
5.14.e: Serve Agni, God adorable, the Sage whose back is balmed with oil:  Let him approach, and hear my call.

5.14.d: अग्निं घर्तेन वाव्र्धु सतोमेभिर विश्वचर्षणिम | सवाधीभिर वचस्युभिः ||
5.14.e: They have exalted Agni, God of all mankind, with oil and hymns  Of praise, devout and eloquent.

5.15.d: पर वेधसे कवये वेद्याय गिरम भरे यशसे पूर्व्याय | घर्तप्रसत्तो असुरः सुशेवो रायो धर्ता धरुणो वस्वो अग्निः ||
5.15.e: To him, the far-renowned, the wise Ordainer, ancient and glorious, a song I offer.  Enthroned in oil, the Asura, bliss-giver, is Agni, firm support of noble, riches.

5.15.d: रतेन रतं धरुणं धारयन्त यज्ञस्य शाके परमे वयोमन | दिवो धर्मन धरुणे सेदुषो नञ्ञ जातैर अजातां अभि ये ननक्षुः ||
5.15.e: By holy Law they kept supporting Order, by help of sacrifice, in loftiest heaven,—  They who attained with born men to the unborn, men seated on that stay, heaven's firm sustainer.

5.15.d: अङहोयुवस तन्वस तन्वते वि वयो महद दुष्टरम पूर्व्याय | स संवतो नवजातस तुतुर्यात सिङहं न करुद्धम अभितः परि षठुः ||
5.15.e: Averting woe, they labour hard to bring him, the ancient, plenteous food as power resistless.  May he, born newly, conquer his assailants: round him they stand as round an angry lion.

5.15.d: मातेव यद भरसे पप्रथानो जनं-जनं धायसे चक्षसे च | वयो-वयो जरसे यद दधानः परि तमना विषुरूपो जिगासि ||
5.15.e: When, like a mother, spreading forth to nourish, to cherish and regard each man that liveth,—  Consuming all the strength that thou hast gotten, thou wanderest round, thyself, in varied fashion.

5.15.d: वाजो नु ते शवसस पात्व अन्तम उरुं दोघं धरुणं देव रायः | पदं न तायुर गुहा दधानो महो राये चितयन्न अत्रिम अस्पः ||
5.15.e: May strength preserve the compass of thy vigour, God! that broad stream of thine that beareth riches.  Thou, like a thief who keeps his refuge secret, hast holpen Atri to great wealth, by teaching.

5.16.d: बर्हद वयो हि भानवे ऽरचा देवायाग्नये | यम मित्रं न परशस्तिभिर मर्तासो दधिरे पुरः ||
5.16.e: GREAT power is in the beam of light, sing praise to, Agni, to the God  Whom men have set in foremost place like Mitra with their eulogies.

5.16.d: स हि दयुभिर जनानां होता दक्षस्य बाह्वोः | वि हव्यम अग्निर आनुषग भगो न वारम रण्वति ||
5.16.e: He by the splendour of his arms is Priest of every able man.  Agni conveys oblation straight, and deals, as Bhaga deals, his boons.

5.16.d: अस्य सतोमे मघोनः सख्ये वर्द्धशोचिषः | विश्वा यस्मिन तुविष्वणि सम अर्ये शुष्मम आदधुः ||
5.16.e: All rests upon the laud and love of him the rich, high-flaming God,  On whom, loud-roaring, men have laid great strength as on a faithful friend.

5.16.d: अधा हय अग्न एषां सुवीर्यस्य मंहना | तम इद यह्वं न रोदसी परि शरवो बभूवतुः ||
5.16.e: So, Agni, be the Friend of these with liberal gift of hero strength.  Yea, Heaven and Earth have not surpassed this Youthful One in glorious fame.

5.16.d: नू न एहि वार्यम अग्ने गर्णान आ भर | ये वयं ये च सूरयः सवस्ति धामहे सचोतैधि पर्त्सु नो वर्धे ||
5.16.e: O Agni, quickly come to us, and, glorified, bring precious wealth.  So we and these our princes will assemble for the good of all. Be near in fight to prosper us.

5.17.d: आ यज्ञैर देव मर्त्य इत्था तव्यांसम ऊतये | अग्निं कर्ते सवध्वरे पूरुर ईळीतावसे ||
5.17.e: GOD, may a mortal call the Strong hither, with solemn rites, to aid,  A man call Agni to protect when sacrifice is well prepared.

5.17.d: अस्य हि सवयशस्तर आसा विधर्मन मन्यसे | तं नाकं चित्रशोचिषम मन्द्रम परो मनीषया ||
5.17.e: Near him thou seemest mightier still in native glory, set to hold  Apart yon flame-hued vault of heaven, lovely beyond the thought of man.

5.17.d: अस्य वासा उ अर्चिषा य आयुक्त तुजा गिरा | दिवो न यस्य रेतसा बर्हच छोचन्त्य अर्चयः ||
5.17.e: Yea, this is by the light of him whom powerful song hath bound to act,  Whose beams of splendour flash on high as though they sprang from heavenly seed.

5.17.d: अस्य करत्वा विचेतसो दस्मस्य वसु रथ आ | अधा विश्वासु हव्यो ऽगनिर विक्षु पर शस्यते ||
5.17.e: Wealth loads the Wonder-Worker's car through his, the very wise One's power.  Then, meet to be invoked among all tribes, is Agni glorified.

5.17.d: नू न इद धि वार्यम आसा सचन्त सूरयः | ऊर्जो नपाद अभिष्टये पाहि शग्धि सवस्तय उतैधि पर्त्सु नो वर्धे ||
5.17.e: Now, too, the princes shall obtain excellent riches by our lips.  Protect us for our welfare: lend thy succour, O thou Son of Strength. Be near in fight to prosper us.

5.18.d: परातर अग्निः पुरुप्रियो विश सतवेतातिथिः | विश्वानि यो अमर्त्यो हव्या मर्तेषु रण्यति ||
5.18.e: AT dawn let Agni, much-beloved guest of the house, be glorified;  Immortal who delights in all oblations brought by mortal men.

5.18.d: दविताय मर्क्तवाहसे सवस्य दक्षस्य मंहना | इन्दुं स धत्त आनुषक सतोता चित ते अमर्त्य ||
5.18.e: For Dvita who receives through wealth of native strength maimed offerings,  Thy praiser even gains at once the Soma-drops, Immortal Gods!

5.18.d: तं वो दीर्घायुशोचिषं गिरा हुवे मघोनाम | अरिष्टो येषां रथो वय अश्वदावन्न ईयते ||
5.18.e: Nobles, with song I call that car of yours that shines with lengthened life,  For, God who givest steeds! that car hither and thither goes unharmed.

5.18.d: चित्रा वा येषु दीधितिर आसन्न उक्था पान्ति ये | सतीर्णम बर्हिः सवर्णरे शरवांसि दधिरे परि ||
5.18.e: They who have varied ways of thought, who guard the lauds within their lips,  And strew the grass before the light, have decked themselves with high renown.

5.18.d: ये मे पञ्चाशतं ददुर अश्वानां सधस्तुति | दयुमद अग्ने महि शरवो बर्हत कर्धि मघोनां नर्वद अम्र्त नर्णाम ||
5.18.e: Immortal Agni, give the chiefs, heroes who institute the rite,  Heroes’ illustrious, lofty fame, who at the synod met for praise presented me with fifty steeds.

5.19.d: अभ्य अवस्थाः पर जायन्ते पर वव्रेर वव्रिश चिकेत | उपस्थे मातुर वि चष्टे ||
5.19.e: ONE state begets another state: husk is made visible from husk:  Within his Mother's side he speaks.

5.19.d: जुहुरे वि चितयन्तो ऽनिमिषं नर्म्णम पान्ति | आ दर्ळ्हाम पुरं विविशुः ||
5.19.e: Discerning, have they offered gifts: they guard the strength that never wastes.  To a strong fort have they pressed in.

5.19.d: आ शवैत्रेयस्य जन्तवो दयुमद वर्धन्त कर्ष्टयः | निष्कग्रीवो बर्हदुक्थ एना मध्वा न वाजयुः ||
5.19.e: Śvaitreya's people, all his men, have gloriously increased in might.  A gold chain Bṛhaduktha wears, as, through this Soma, seeking spoil.

5.19.d: परियं दुग्धं न काम्यम अजामि जाम्योः सचा | घर्मो न वाजजठरो ऽदब्धः शश्वतो दभः ||
5.19.e: I bring, as ’twere, the longed-for milk, the dear milk of the Sister-Pair.  Like to a caldron filled with food is he, unconquered, conquering all.

5.19.d: करीळन नो रश्म आ भुवः सम भस्मना वायुना वेविदानः | ता अस्य सन धर्षजो न तिग्माः सुसंशिता वक्ष्यो वक्षणेस्थाः ||
5.19.e: Beam of light, come to us in sportive fashion, finding thyself close to the wind that fans thee.  These flames of his are wasting flames, like arrows keen-pointed, sharpened, on his breast.

5.20.d: यम अग्ने वाजसातम तवं चिन मन्यसे रयिम | तं नो गीर्भिः शरवाय्यं देवत्रा पनया युजम ||
5.20.e: AGNI, best winner of the spoil, cause us to praise before the Gods  As our associate meet for lauds, wealth which thou verily deemest wealth.

5.20.d: ये अग्ने नेरयन्ति ते वर्द्धा उग्रस्य शवसः | अप दवेषो अप हवरो ऽनयव्रतस्य सश्चिरे ||
5.20.e: Agni, the great who ward not off the anger of thy power and might  Stir up the wrath and hatred due to one who holds an alien creed.

5.20.d: होतारं तवा वर्णीमहे ऽगने दक्षस्य साधनम | यज्ञेषु पूर्व्यं गिरा परयस्वन्तो हवामहे ||
5.20.e: Thee, Agni, would we choose as Priest, the perfecter of strength and skill;  We who bring sacred food invoke with song thee Chief at holy rites.

5.20.d: इत्था यथा त ऊतये सहसावन दिवे-दिवे | राय रताय सुक्रतो गोभिः षयाम सधमादो वीरैः सयाम सधमादः ||
5.20.e: Here as is needful for thine aid we toil, O Conqueror, day by day,  For wealth, for Law. May we rejoice, Most Wise One! at the feast, with kine, rejoice, with heroes, at the feast.

5.21.d: मनुष्वत तवा नि धीमहि मनुष्वत सम इधीमहि | अग्ने मनुष्वद अङगिरो देवान देवयते यज ||
5.21.e: WE stablish thee as Manus used, as Manus used we kindle thee.  Like Manus, for the pious man , Aṅgiras, Agni, worship Gods.

5.21.d: तवं हि मानुषे जने ऽगने सुप्रीत इध्यसे | सरुचस तवा यन्त्य आनुषक सुजात सर्पिरासुते ||
5.21.e: For well, O Agni, art thou pleased when thou art kindled mid mankind.  Straight go the ladles unto thee, thou highborn God whose food is oil.

5.21.d: तवां विश्वे सजोषसो देवासो दूतम अक्रत | सपर्यन्तस तवा कवे यज्ञेषु देवम ईळते ||
5.21.e: Thee have all Gods of one accord established as their messenger.  Serving at sacrifices men adore thee as a God, O Sage.

5.21.d: देवं वो देवयज्ययाग्निम ईळीत मर्त्यः | समिद्धः शुक्र दीदिह्य रतस्य योनिम आसदः ससस्य योनिम आसदः ||
5.21.e: Let mortal man adore your God, Agni, with worship due to Gods.  Shine forth enkindled, Radiant One. Sit in the chamber of the Law, sit in the chamber of the food.

5.22.d: पर विश्वसामन्न अत्रिवद अर्चा पावकशोचिषे | यो अध्वरेष्व ईड्यो होता मन्द्रतमो विशि ||
5.22.e: LIKE Atri, Viśvasāman! sing to him of purifying light,  Who must be praised in holy rites, the Priest most welcome in the house.

5.22.d: नय अग्निं जातवेदसं दधाता देवम रत्विजम | पर यज्ञ एत्व आनुषग अद्या देवव्यचस्तमः ||
5.22.e: Set Jātavedas in his place, Agni the God and Minister.  Let sacrifice proceed to-day duly, comprising all the Gods.

5.22.d: चिकित्विन्मनसं तवा देवम मर्तास ऊतये | वरेण्यस्य ते ऽवस इयानासो अमन्महि ||
5.22.e: All mortals come to thee for aid, the God of most observant mind.  Of thine excelling favour we bethink us as we long for it.

5.22.d: अग्ने चिकिद्ध्य अस्य न इदं वचः सहस्य | तं तवा सुशिप्र दम्पते सतोमैर वर्धन्त्य अत्रयो गीर्भिः शुम्भन्त्य अत्रयः ||
5.22.e: Mark with attention this our speech, O Agni, thou victorious One.  Thee, Strong-jawed! as the homestead's Lord, the Atris with their lauds exalt, the Atris beautify with songs.

5.23.d: अग्ने सहन्तम आ भर दयुम्नस्य परासहा रयिम | विश्वा यश चर्षणीर अभ्य रसा वाजेषु सासहत ||
5.23.e: By thy fair splendour's mighty power, O Agni, bring victorious wealth,  Wealth that o’ercometh all mankind, and, near us, conquereth in fight.

5.23.d: तम अग्ने पर्तनाषहं रयिं सहस्व आ भर | तवं हि सत्यो अद्भुतो दाता वाजस्य गोमतः ||
5.23.e: Victorious Agni, bring to us the wealth that vanquisheth in war;  For thou art wonderful and true, giver of strength in herds of kine.

5.23.d: विश्वे हि तवा सजोषसो जनासो वर्क्तबर्हिषः | होतारं सद्मसु परियं वयन्ति वार्या पुरु ||
5.23.e: For all the folk with one accord, whose sacred grass is trimmed and strewn,  Invite thee to their worship-halls, as a dear Priest, for choicest wealth.

5.23.d: स हि षमा विश्वचर्षणिर अभिमाति सहो दधे | अग्न एषु कषयेष्व आ रेवन नः शुक्र दीदिहि दयुमत पावक दीदिहि ||
5.23.e: For he, the God of all men, hath gotten him might that quelleth foes.  O Agni, in these homes shine forth, bright God! for our prosperity, shine, Purifier! splendidly.

5.24.d: अग्ने तवं नो अन्तम उत तराता शिवो भवा वरूथ्यः ||
5.24.e: O AGNI, be our nearest Friend, be thou a kind deliverer and a gracious Friend.

5.24.d: वसुर अग्निर वसुश्रवा अछा नक्षि दयुमत्तमं रयिं दाः ||
5.24.e: Excellent Agni, come thou nigh to us, and give us wealth most splendidly renowned.

5.24.d: स नो बोधि शरुधी हवम उरुष्या णो अघायतः समस्मात ||
5.24.e: So hear us, listen to this call of ours, and keep us far from every sinful man.

5.24.d: तं तवा शोचिष्ठ दीदिवः सुम्नाय नूनम ईमहे सखिभ्यः ||
5.24.e: To thee then, O Most Bright, O Radiant God, we come with prayer for happiness for our friends.

5.25.d: अछा वो अग्निम अवसे देवं गासि स नो वसुः | रासत पुत्र रषूणाम रतावा पर्षति दविषः ||
5.25.e: I WILL sing near, for grace, your God Agni, for he is good to us.  Son of the Brands, may he give gifts, and, righteous, save us from the foe.

5.25.d: स हि सत्यो यम पूर्वे चिद देवासश चिद यम ईधिरे | होतारम मन्द्रजिह्वम इत सुदीतिभिर विभावसुम ||
5.25.e: For he is true, whom men of old enkindled, and the Gods themselves,  The Priest with the delicious tongue, rich with the light of glorious beams.

5.25.d: स नो धीती वरिष्ठया शरेष्ठया च सुमत्या | अग्ने रायो दिदीहि नः सुव्र्क्तिभिर वरेण्य ||
5.25.e: With wisdom that surpasseth all, with gracious will most excellent,  O Agni, worthy of our choice, shine wealth on us through hymns of praise.

5.25.d: अग्निर देवेषु राजत्य अग्निर मर्तेष्व आविशन | अग्निर नो हव्यवाहनो ऽगनिं धीभिः सपर्यत ||
5.25.e: Agni is King, for he extends to mortals and to Gods alike.  Agni is bearer of our gifts. Worship ye Agni with your thoughts.

5.25.d: अग्निस तुविश्रवस्तमं तुविब्रह्माणम उत्तमम | अतूर्तं शरावयत्पतिम पुत्रं ददाति दाशुषे ||
5.25.e: Agni gives to the worshipper a son, the best, of mightiest fame,  Of deep devotion, ne’er subdued, bringer of glory to his sire.

5.25.d: अग्निर ददाति सत्पतिं सासाह यो युधा नर्भिः | अग्निर अत्यं रघुष्यदं जेतारम अपराजितम ||
5.25.e: Agni bestows the hero-lord who conquers with the men in fight.  Agni bestows the fleet-foot steed, the victor never overcome.

5.25.d: यद वाहिष्ठं तद अग्नये बर्हद अर्च विभावसो | महिषीव तवद रयिस तवद वाजा उद ईरते ||
5.25.e: The mightiest song is Agni's: shine on high, thou who art rich in light.  Like the Chief Consort of a King, riches and strength proceed from thee.

5.25.d: तव दयुमन्तो अर्चयो गरावेवोच्यते बर्हत | उतो ते तन्यतुर यथा सवानो अर्त तमना दिवः ||
5.25.e: Resplendent are thy rays of light: loud is thy voice like pressing-stones.  Yea, of itself thy thunder goes forth like the roaring of the heaven.

5.25.d: एवां अग्निं वसूयवः सहसानं ववन्दिम | स नो विश्वा अति दविषः पर्षन नावेव सुक्रतुः ||
5.25.e: Thus, seeking riches, have we paid homage to Agni Conqueror.  May he, most wise, as with a ship, carry us over all our foes.

5.26.d: अग्ने पावक रोचिषा मन्द्रया देव जिह्वया | आ देवान वक्षि यक्षि च ||
5.26.e: O AGNI, Holy and Divine, with splendour and thy pleasant tongue  Bring hither and adore the Gods.

5.26.d: तं तवा घर्तस्नव ईमहे चित्रभानो सवर्द्र्शम | देवां आ वीतये वह ||
5.26.e: We pray thee, thou who droppest oil, bright-rayed! who lookest on the Sun,  Bring the Gods hither to the feast.

5.26.d: वीतिहोत्रं तवा कवे दयुमन्तं सम इधीमहि | अग्ने बर्हन्तम अध्वरे ||
5.26.e: We have enkindled thee, O Sage, bright caller of the Gods to feast.  O Agni, great in Sacrifice.

5.26.d: अग्ने विश्वेभिर आ गहि देवेभिर हव्यदातये | होतारं तवा वर्णीमहे ||
5.26.e: O Agni, come with all the Gods, come to our sacrificial gift:  We choose thee as Invoking Priest.

5.26.d: यजमानाय सुन्वत आग्ने सुवीर्यं वह | देवैर आ सत्सि बर्हिषि ||
5.26.e: Bring, Agni, to the worshipper who pours the juice, heroic strength:  Sit with the Gods upon the grass.

5.26.d: समिधानः सहस्रजिद अग्ने धर्माणि पुष्यसि | देवानां दूत उक्थ्यः ||
5.26.e: Victor of thousands, Agni, thou, enkindled, cherishest the laws,  Laud-worthy, envoy of the Gods.

5.26.d: नय अग्निं जातवेदसं होत्रवाहं यविष्ठ्यम | दधाता देवम रत्विजम ||
5.26.e: Set Agni Jātavedas down, the bearer of our sacred gifts,  MostYouthful, God and Minister.

5.26.d: पर यज्ञ एत्व आनुषग अद्या देवव्यचस्तमः | सत्र्णीत बर्हिर आसदे ||
5.26.e: Duly proceed our sacrifice, comprising all the Gods, to-day:  Strew holy grass to be their seat.

5.26.d: एदम मरुतो अश्विना मित्रः सीदन्तु वरुणः | देवासः सर्वया विशा ||
5.26.e: So may the Maruts sit thereon, the Aśvins, Mitra, Varuṇa:  The Gods with all their company.

5.27.d: अनस्वन्ता सत्पतिर मामहे मे गावा चेतिष्ठो असुरो मघोनः | तरैव्र्ष्णो अग्ने दशभिः सहस्रैर वैश्वानर तर्यरुणश चिकेत ||
5.27.e: THE Godlike hero, famousest of nobles, hath granted me two oxen with a wagon.  Trvrsan's son Tryaruna hath distinguished himself, Vaiśvānara Agni! with ten thousands.

5.27.d: यो मे शता च विंशतिं च गोनां हरी च युक्ता सुधुरा ददाति | वैश्वानर सुष्टुतो वाव्र्धानो ऽगने यछ तर्यरुणाय शर्म ||
5.27.e: Protect Tryaruna, as thou art waxing strong and art highly praised, Vaiśvānara Agni!  Who granteth me a hundred kine and twenty, and two bay horses, good at draught, and harnessed.

5.27.d: एवा ते अग्ने सुमतिं चकानो नविष्ठाय नवमं तरसदस्युः | यो मे गिरस तुविजातस्य पूर्वीर युक्तेनाभि तर्यरुणो गर्णाति ||
5.27.e: So Trasadasyu served thee, God Most Youthful, craving thy favour for the ninth time, Agni;  Tryaruya who with attentive spirit accepteth many a song from me the mighty.

5.27.d: यो म इति परवोचत्य अश्वमेधाय सूरये | ददद रचा सनिं यते ददन मेधाम रतायते ||
5.27.e: He who declares his wish to me, to Asvamedha, to the Prince,  Pays him who with his verse seeks gain, gives power to him who keeps the Law.

5.27.d: यस्य मा परुषाः शतम उद्धर्षयन्त्य उक्षणः | अश्वमेधस्य दानाः सोमा इव तर्य्र्शिरः ||
5.27.e: From whom a hundred oxen, all of speckled hue, delight my heart,  The gifts of Asvamedha, like thrice-mingled draughts of Soma juice.

5.27.d: इन्द्राग्नी शतदाव्न्य अश्वमेधे सुवीर्यम | कषत्रं धारयतम बर्हद दिवि सूर्यम इवाजरम ||
5.27.e: To Asvamedha who bestows a hundred gifts grant hero power,  O Indra-Agni! lofty rule like the unwasting Sun in heaven.

5.28.d: समिद्धो अग्निर दिवि शोचिर अश्रेत परत्यङङ उषसम उर्विया वि भाति | एति पराची विश्ववारा नमोभिर देवां ईळाना हविषा घर्ताची ||
5.28.e: AGNI inflamed hath sent to heaven his lustre: he shines forth widely turning unto Morning.  Eastward the ladle goes that brings all blessing, praising the Godswith homage and oblation.

5.28.d: समिध्यमानो अम्र्तस्य राजसि हविष कर्ण्वन्तं सचसे सवस्तये | विश्वं स धत्ते दरविणं यम इन्वस्य आतिथ्यम अग्ने नि च धत्त इत पुरः ||
5.28.e: Enkindled, thou art King of the immortal world: him who brings offerings thou attendest for his weal.  He whom thou urgest on makes all possessions his: he sets before thee, Agni, gifts that guests may claim.

5.28.d: अग्ने शर्ध महते सौभगाय तव दयुम्नान्य उत्तमानि सन्तु | सं जास्पत्यं सुयमम आ कर्णुष्व शत्रूयताम अभि तिष्ठा महांसि ||
5.28.e: Show thyself strong for mighty bliss, O Agni, most excellent be thine effulgent splendours.  Make easy to maintain our household lordship, and overcome the might of those who hate us.

5.28.d: समिद्धस्य परमहसो ऽगने वन्दे तव शरियम | वर्षभो दयुम्नवां असि सम अध्वरेष्व इध्यसे ||
5.28.e: Thy glory, Agni, I adore, kindled, exalted in thy strength.  A Steer of brilliant splendour, thou art lighted well at sacred rites.

5.28.d: समिद्धो अग्न आहुत देवान यक्षि सवध्वर | तवं हि हव्यवाळ असि ||
5.28.e: Agni, invoked and kindled, serve the Gods, thou skilled in sacrifice:  For thou art bearer of our gifts.

5.28.d: आ जुहोता दुवस्यताग्निम परयत्य अध्वरे | वर्णीध्वं हव्यवाहनम ||
5.28.e: Invoke and worship Agni while the sacrificial rite proceeds:  For offering-bearer choose ye him.

5.29.d: तर्य अर्यमा मनुषो देवताता तरी रोचना दिव्या धारयन्त | अर्चन्ति तवा मरुतः पूतदक्षास तवम एषाम रषिर इन्द्रासि धीरः ||
5.29.e: MAN'S worship of the Gods hath three great lustres, and three celestial lights have they established  The Maruts gifted with pure strength adore thee, for thou, O Indra, art their sapient Ṛṣi.

5.29.d: अनु यद ईम मरुतो मन्दसानम आर्चन्न इन्द्रम पपिवांसं सुतस्य | आदत्त वज्रम अभि यद अहिं हन्न अपो यह्वीर अस्र्जत सर्तवा उ ||
5.29.e: What time the Maruts sang their song to Indra, joyous when he had drunk of Soma juices,  He grasped his thunderbolt to slay the Dragon, and loosed, that they might flow, the youthful Waters.

5.29.d: उत बरह्माणो मरुतो मे अस्येन्द्रः सोमस्य सुषुतस्य पेयाः | तद धि हव्यम मनुषे गा अविन्दद अहन्न अहिम पपिवां इन्द्रो अस्य ||
5.29.e: And, O ye Brahmans, Maruts, so may Indra drink draughts of this my carefully pressed Soma;  For this oblation found for man the cattle, and Indra, having quaffed it, slew the Dragon.

5.29.d: आद रोदसी वितरं वि षकभायत संविव्यानश चिद भियसे मर्गं कः | जिगर्तिम इन्द्रो अपजर्गुराणः परति शवसन्तम अव दानवं हन ||
5.29.e: Then heaven and earth he sundered and supported: wrapped even in these he struck the Beast with terror.  So Indra forced the Engulfer to disgorgement, and slew the Dānava. panting against him.

5.29.d: अध करत्वा मघवन तुभ्यं देवा अनु विश्वे अददुः सोमपेयम | यत सूर्यस्य हरितः पतन्तीः पुरः सतीर उपरा एतशे कः ||
5.29.e: Thus all the Gods, O Maghavan, delivered to thee of their free will the draught of Soma;  When thou for Etaśa didst cause to tarry the flying mares of Sūrya racing forward.

5.29.d: नव यद अस्य नवतिं च भोगान साकं वज्रेण मघवा विव्र्श्चत | अर्चन्तीन्द्रम मरुतः सधस्थे तरैष्टुभेन वचसा बाधत दयाम ||
5.29.e: When Maghavan with the thunderbolt demolished his nine-and-ninety castles all together,  The Maruts, where they met, glorified Indra: ye with the Tṛṣṭup hymn obstructed heaven.

5.29.d: सखा सख्ये अपचत तूयम अग्निर अस्य करत्वा महिषा तरी शतानि | तरी साकम इन्द्रो मनुषः सरांसि सुतम पिबद वर्त्रहत्याय सोमम ||
5.29.e: As friend to aid a friend, Agni dressed quickly three hundred buffaloes, even as he willed it.  And Indra, from man's gift, for Vṛtra's slaughter, drank ofr at once three lakes of pressed-out Soma.

5.29.d: तरी यच छता महिषाणाम अघो मास तरी सरांसि मघवा सोम्यापाः | कारं न विश्वे अह्वन्त देवा भरम इन्द्राय यद अहिं जघान ||
5.29.e: When thou three hundred buffaloes' flesh hadst eaten, and drunk, as Maghavan, three lakes of Soma,  All the Gods raised as ’twere a shout of triumph to Indra praise because he slew the Dragon.

5.29.d: उशना यत सहस्यैर अयातं गर्हम इन्द्र जूजुवानेभिर अश्वैः | वन्वानो अत्र सरथं ययाथ कुत्सेन देवैर अवनोर ह शुष्णम ||
5.29.e: What time ye came with strong steeds swiftly speeding, O Uśanā and Indra, to the dwelling,  Thou camest thither -conquering together with Kutsa and the Gods: thou slewest Śuṣṇa.

5.29.d: परान्यच चक्रम अव्र्हः सूर्यस्य कुत्सायान्यद वरिवो यातवे ऽकः | अनासो दस्यूंर अम्र्णो वधेन नि दुर्योण आव्र्णङ मर्ध्रवाचः ||
5.29.e: One car-wheel of the Sun thou rolledst forward, and one thou settest free to move for Kutsa.  Thou slewest noseless Dasyus with thy weapon, and in their home o’erthrewest hostile speakers.

5.29.d: सतोमासस तवा गौरिवीतेर अवर्धन्न अरन्धयो वैदथिनाय पिप्रुम | आ तवाम रजिश्वा सख्याय चक्रे पचन पक्तीर अपिबः सोमम अस्य ||
5.29.e: The lauds of Gauriviti made thee mighty to Vidathin's son, as prey, thou gavest Pipru.  Rjisivan drew thee into friendship dressing the sacred food, and thou hast drunk his Soma.

5.29.d: नवग्वासः सुतसोमास इन्द्रं दशग्वासो अभ्य अर्चन्त्य अर्कैः | गव्यं चिद ऊर्वम अपिधानवन्तं तं चिन नरः शशमाना अप वरन ||
5.29.e: Navagvas and Dasgvas with libations of Soma juice sing hymns of praise to Indra.  Labouring at their task the men laid open the stall of Kine though firmly closed and fastened.

5.29.d: कथो नु ते परि चराणि विद्वान वीर्य्र मघवन या चकर्थ | या चो नु नव्या कर्णवः शविष्ठ परेद उ ता ते विदथेषु बरवाम ||
5.29.e: How shall I serve thee, Maghavan, though knowing full well what hero deeds thou hast accomplished?  And the fresh deeds which thou wilt do, Most Mighty! these, too, will we tell forth in sacred synods.

5.29.d: एता विश्वा चक्र्वां इन्द्र भूर्य अपरीतो जनुषा वीर्येण | या चिन नु वज्रिन कर्णवो दध्र्ष्वान न ते वर्ता तविष्या अस्ति तस्याः ||
5.29.e: Resistless from of old through hero courage, thou hast done all these many acts, O Indra.  What thou wilt do in bravery, Thunder-wielder! none is there who may hinder this thy prowess.

5.29.d: इन्द्र बरह्म करियमाणा जुषस्व या ते शविष्ठ नव्या अकर्म | वस्त्रेव भद्रा सुक्र्ता वसूयू रथं न धीरः सवपा अतक्षम ||
5.29.e: Indra, accept the prayers which now are offered, accept the new prayers, Mightiest! which we utter.  Like fair and well-made robes, I, seeking riches, as a deft craftsman makes a car, have wrought them.

5.30.d: कव सय वीरः को अपश्यद इन्द्रं सुखरथम ईयमानं हरिभ्याम | यो राया वज्री सुतसोमम इछन तद ओको गन्ता पुरुहूत ऊती ||
5.30.e: WHERE is that Hero? Who hath looked on Indra borne on light-rolling car by Tawny Coursers,  Who, Thunderer, seeks with wealth the Soma-presser, and to his house goes, much-invoked, to aid him?

5.30.d: अवाचचक्षम पदम अस्य सस्वर उग्रं निधातुर अन्व आयम इछन | अप्र्छम अन्यां उत ते म आहुर इन्द्रं नरो बुबुधाना अशेम ||
5.30.e: I have beheld his strong and secret dwelling, longing have sought the Founder's habitation.  I asked of others, and they said in answer, May we, awakened men, attain to Indra.

5.30.d: पर नु वयं सुते या ते कर्तानीन्द्र बरवाम यानि नो जुजोषः | वेदद अविद्वाञ छर्णवच च विद्वान वहते ऽयम मघवा सर्वसेनः ||
5.30.e: We will tell, Indra, when we pour libation, what mighty deeds thou hast performed to please us.  Let him who knows not learn, who knows them listen: hither rides Maghavan with all his army.

5.30.d: सथिरम मनश चक्र्षे जात इन्द्र वेषीद एको युधये भूयसश चित | अश्मानं चिच छवसा दिद्युतो वि विदो गवाम ऊर्वम उस्रियाणाम ||
5.30.e: Indra, when born, thou madest firm thy spirit: alone thou seekest war to fight with many.  With might thou clavest e’en the rock asunder, and foundest out the stable of the Milch-kine.

5.30.d: परो यत तवम परम आजनिष्ठाः परावति शरुत्यं नाम बिभ्रत | अतश चिद इन्द्राद अभयन्त देवा विश्वा अपो अजयद दासपत्नीः ||
5.30.e: When thou wast born supremest at a distance, bearing a name renowned in far-off regions,  Since then e’en Gods have been afraid of Indra: he conquered all the floods which served the Dāsa.

5.30.d: तुभ्येद एते मरुतः सुशेवा अर्चन्त्य अर्कं सुन्वन्त्य अन्धः | अहिम ओहानम अप आशयानम पर मायाभिर मायिनं सक्षद इन्द्रः ||
5.30.e: These blissful Maruts sing their psalm to praise thee, and pour to thee libation of the Soma.  Indra with wondrous powers subdued the Dragon, the guileful lurker who beset the waters.

5.30.d: वि षू मर्धो जनुषा दानम इन्वन्न अहन गवा मघवन संचकानः | अत्रा दासस्य नमुचेः शिरो यद अवर्तयो मनवे गातुम इछन ||
5.30.e: Thou, Maghavan, from the first didst scatter foemen, speeding, while joying in the milk, the Giver.  There, seeking man's prosperity, thou torest away the head of Namuci the Dāsa.

5.30.d: युजं हि माम अक्र्था आद इद इन्द्र शिरो दासस्य नमुचेर मथायन | अश्मानं चित सवर्यं वर्तमानम पर चक्रियेव रोदसी मरुद्भ्यः ||
5.30.e: Pounding the head of Namuci the Dāsa, me, too thou madest thine associate, Indra!  Yea, and the rolling stone that is in heaven both worlds, as on a car, brought to the Maruts.

5.30.d: सत्रियो हि दास आयुधानि चक्रे किम मा करन्न अबला अस्य सेनाः | अन्तर हय अख्यद उभे अस्य धेने अथोप परैद युधये दस्युम इन्द्रः ||
5.30.e: Women for weapons hath the Dāsa taken, What injury can his feeble armies To me?  Well he distinguished his two different voices, and Indra then advanced to fight the Dasyu.

5.30.d: सम अत्र गावो ऽभितो ऽनवन्तेहेह वत्सैर वियुता यद आसन | सं ता इन्द्रो अस्र्जद अस्य शाकैर यद ईं सोमासः सुषुता अमन्दन ||
5.30.e: Divided from their calves the Cows went lowing around, on every side, hither and thither.  These Indra re-united with his helpers, what time the well-pressed Soma made him joyful.

5.30.d: यद ईं सोमा बभ्रुधूता अमन्दन्न अरोरवीद वर्षभः सादनेषु | पुरंदरः पपिवां इन्द्रो अस्य पुनर गवाम अददाद उस्रियाणाम ||
5.30.e: What time the Somas mixed by Babhru cheered him, loud the Steer bellowed in his habitations.  So Indra drank thereof, the Fort-destroyer, and gave him guerdon, in return, of milch-kine.

5.30.d: भद्रम इदं रुशमा अग्ने अक्रन गवां चत्वारि ददतः सहस्रा | रणंचयस्य परयता मघानि परत्य अग्रभीष्म नर्तमस्य नर्णाम ||
5.30.e: This good deed have the Rusamas done, Agni! that they have granted me four thousand cattle.  We have received Rnancaya's wealth, of heroes the most heroic, which was freely offered.

5.30.d: सुपेशसम माव सर्जन्त्य अस्तं गवां सहस्रै रुशमासो अग्ने | तीव्रा इन्द्रम अममन्दुः सुतासो ऽकतोर वयुष्टौ परितक्म्यायाः ||
5.30.e: The Rusamas, O Agni, sent me homeward with fair adornment and with kine in thousands.  The strong libations have made Indra joyful, when night, whose course was ending, changed to morning.

5.30.d: औछत सा रात्री परितक्म्या यां रणंचये राजनि रुशमानाम | अत्यो न वाजी रघुर अज्यमानो बभ्रुश चत्वार्य असनत सहस्रा ||
5.30.e: Night, well-nigh ended, at Rnancaya's coming, King of the Rusamas, was changed to morning.  Like a strong courser, fleet of foot, urged onward, Babhru hath gained four thousand as his guerdon.

5.30.d: चतुःसहस्रं गव्यस्य पश्वः परत्य अग्रभीष्म रुशमेष्व अग्ने | घर्मश चित तप्तः परव्र्जे य आसीद अयस्मयस तं व आदाम विप्राः ||
5.30.e: We have received four thousand head of cattle presented by the Rusamas, O Agni.  And we, the singers, have received the caldron of metal which was heated for Pravargya.

5.31.d: इन्द्रो रथाय परवतं कर्णोति यम अध्यस्थान मघवा वाजयन्तम | यूथेव पश्वो वय उनोति गोपा अरिष्टो याति परथमः सिषासन ||
5.31.e: MAGHAVAN Indra turns his chariot downward, the strength-displaying car which he hath mounted.  Even as a herdsman driveth forth his cattle, he goeth, first, uninjured, fain for treasure.

5.31.d: आ पर दरव हरिवो मा वि वेनः पिशङगराते अभि नः सचस्व | नहि तवद इन्द्र वस्यो अन्यद अस्त्य अमेनांश चिज जनिवतश चकर्थ ||
5.31.e: Haste to us, Lord of Bays; be not ungracious: visit us, lover of gold-hued oblation.  There is naught else better than thou art, Indra: e’en to the wifeless hast thou given spouses.

5.31.d: उद यत सहः सहस आजनिष्ट देदिष्ट इन्द्र इन्द्रियाणि विश्वा | पराचोदयत सुदुघा वव्रे अन्तर वि जयोतिषा संवव्र्त्वत तमो ऽवः ||
5.31.e: When out of strength arose the strength that conquers, Indra displayed all powers that he possesses.  Forth from the cave he drove the milky mothers, and with the light laid bare investing darkness.

5.31.d: अनवस ते रथम अश्वाय तक्षन तवष्टा वज्रम पुरुहूत दयुमन्तम | बरह्माण इन्द्रम महयन्तो अर्कैर अवर्धयन्न अहये हन्तवा उ ||
5.31.e: Anus have wrought a chariot for thy Courser, and Tvaṣṭar, Much-invoked! thy bolt that glitters.  The Brahmans with their songs exalting Indra increased his strength that he might slaughter Ahi.

5.31.d: वर्ष्णे यत ते वर्षणो अर्कम अर्चान इन्द्र गरावाणो अदितिः सजोषाः | अनश्वासो ये पवयो ऽरथा इन्द्रेषिता अभ्य अवर्तन्त दस्यून ||
5.31.e: When heroes sang their laud to thee the Hero, Indra! and stones and Aditi accordant,  Without or steed or chariot were the fellies which, sped by Indra, rolled upon the Dasytis.

5.31.d: पर ते पूर्वाणि करणानि वोचम पर नूतना मघवन या चकर्थ | शक्तीवो यद विभरा रोदसी उभे जयन्न अपो मनवे दानुचित्राः ||
5.31.e: I will declare thine exploits wrought aforetime, and, Maghavan, thy deeds of late achievement,  When, Lord of Might, thou sunderedst earth and heaven, winning for man the moistly-gleaming waters.

5.31.d: तद इन नु ते करणं दस्म विप्राहिं यद घनन्न ओजो अत्रामिमीथाः | शुष्णस्य चित परि माया अग्र्भ्णाः परपित्वं यन्न अप दस्यूंर असेधः ||
5.31.e: This is thy deed, e’en this, Wonderful! Singer! that, slaying Ahi, here thy strength thou showedst,  Didst check and stay e’en gusna's wiles and magic, and, drawing nigh, didst chase away the Dasytis.

5.31.d: तवम अपो यदवे तुर्वशायारमयः सुदुघाः पार इन्द्र | उग्रम अयातम अवहो ह कुत्सं सं ह यद वाम उशनारन्त देवाः ||
5.31.e: Thou, Indra, on the farther bank forYadu and Turvaga didst stay the gushing waters.  Ye both assailed the fierce: thou barest Kutsa: when Gods and Uśanā came to you together.

5.31.d: इन्द्राकुत्सा वहमाना रथेना वाम अत्या अपि कर्णे वहन्तु | निः षीम अद्भ्यो धमथो निः षधस्थान मघोनो हर्दो वरथस तमांसि ||
5.31.e: Let the steeds bring you both, Indra and Kutsa, borne on the chariot within hearing-distance.  Ye blew him from the waters, from his dwelling, and chased the darkness from the noble's spirit.

5.31.d: वातस्य युक्तान सुयुजश चिद अश्वान कविश चिद एषो अजगन्न अवस्युः | विश्वे ते अत्र मरुतः सखाय इन्द्र बरह्माणि तविषीम अवर्धन ||
5.31.e: Even this sage hath come looking for succour even to Vāta's docile harnessed horses.  Here are the Maruts, all, thy dear companions: prayers have increased thy power and might, O Indra.

5.31.d: सूरश चिद रथम परितक्म्यायाम पूर्वं करद उपरं जूजुवांसम | भरच चक्रम एतशः सं रिणाति पुरो दधत सनिष्यति करतुं नः ||
5.31.e: When night was near its close he carried forward e’en the Sun's chariot backward in its running.  Etaga brought his wheel and firmly stays it: setting it eastward he shall give us courage.

5.31.d: आयं जना अभिचक्षे जगामेन्द्रः सखायं सुतसोमम इछन | वदन गरावाव वेदिम भरियाते यस्य जीरम अध्वर्यवश चरन्ति ||
5.31.e: This Indra, O ye men, hath come to see you, seeking a friend who hath expressed the Soma.  The creaking stone is laid upon the altar, and the Adhvaryus come to turn it quickly.

5.31.d: ये चाकनन्त चाकनन्त नू ते मर्ता अम्र्त मो ते अंह आरन | वावन्धि यज्यूंर उत तेषु धेह्य ओजो जनेषु येषु ते सयाम ||
5.31.e: Let mortals who were happy still be happy; let them not come to sorrow, O Immortal.  Love thou the pious, and to these thy people-with whom may we be numbered-give thou vigour.

5.32.d: अदर्दर उत्सम अस्र्जो वि खानि तवम अर्णवान बद्बधानां अरम्णाः | महान्तम इन्द्र पर्वतं वि यद वः सर्जो वि धारा अव दानवं हन ||
5.32.e: 1ṬHE well thou clavest, settest free the fountains, and gavest rest to floods that were obstructed.  Thou, Indra, laying the great mountain open, slaying the Dānava, didst loose the torrents.

5.32.d: तवम उत्सां रतुभिर बद्बधानां अरंह ऊधः पर्वतस्य वज्रिन | अहिं चिद उग्र परयुतं शयानं जघन्वां इन्द्र तविषीम अधत्थाः ||
5.32.e: The fountain-depths obstructed in their seasons, thou, Thunderer! madest flow, the mountain's udder.  Strong Indra, thou by slaying e’en the Dragon that lay extended there hast shown thy vigour.

5.32.d: तयस्य चिन महतो निर मर्गस्य वधर जघान तविषीभिर इन्द्रः | य एक इद अप्रतिर मन्यमान आद अस्माद अन्यो अजनिष्ट तव्यान ||
5.32.e: Indra with violence smote down the weapon,  yea, even of that wild and mighty creature.  Although he deemed himself alone unequalled, another had been born e’en yet more potent.

5.32.d: तयं चिद एषां सवधया मदन्तम मिहो नपातं सुव्र्धं तमोगाम | वर्षप्रभर्मा दानवस्य भामं वज्रेण वज्री नि जघान शुष्णम ||
5.32.e: Him, whom the heavenly food of these delighted, child of the mist, strong waxing, couched in darkness,  Him the bolt-hurling Thunderer with his lightning smote down and slew, the Dānava's wrath-fire, Śuṣṇa.

5.32.d: तयं चिद अस्य करतुभिर निषत्तम अमर्मणो विदद इद अस्य मर्म | यद ईं सुक्षत्र परभ्र्ता मदस्य युयुत्सन्तं तमसि हर्म्ये धाः ||
5.32.e: Though he might ne’er be wounded still his vitals felt that, the God's bolt, which his powers supported,  When, after offered draughts, Strong Lord, thou laidest him, fain to battle, in the pit in darkness.

5.32.d: तयं चिद इत्था कत्पयं शयानम असूर्ये तमसि वाव्र्धानम | तं चिन मन्दानो वर्षभः सुतस्योच्चैर इन्द्रो अपगूर्या जघान ||
5.32.e: Him as he lay there huge in length extended, still waxing in the gloom which no sun lightened,  Him, after loud-voiced threats, the Hero Indra, rejoicing in the poured libation, slaughtered.

5.32.d: उद यद इन्द्रो महते दानवाय वधर यमिष्ट सहो अप्रतीतम | यद ईं वज्रस्य परभ्र्तौ ददाभ विश्वस्य जन्तोर अधमं चकार ||
5.32.e: When 'gainst the mighty Dānava his weapon Indra uplifted, power which none could combat,  When at the hurling of his bolt he smote him, he made him lower than all living creatures.

5.32.d: तयं चिद अर्णम मधुपं शयानम असिन्वं वव्रम मह्य आदद उग्रः | अपादम अत्रम महता वधेन नि दुर्योण आव्र्णङ मर्ध्रवाचम ||
5.32.e: The fierce God seized that huge and restless coiler, insatiate, drinker of the sweets, recumbent,  And with his mighty weapon in his dwelling smote down the footless evil-speaking ogre.

5.32.d: को अस्य शुष्मं तविषीं वरात एको धना भरते अप्रतीतः | इमे चिद अस्य जरयसो नु देवी इन्द्रस्यौजसो भियसा जिहाते ||
5.32.e: Who may arrest his strength or cheek his vigour? Alone, resistless, he bears off all riches.  Even these Twain, these Goddesses, through terror of Indra's might, retire from his dominion.

5.32.d: नय अस्मै देवी सवधितिर जिहीत इन्द्राय गातुर उशतीव येमे | सं यद ओजो युवते विश्वम आभिर अनु सवधाव्ने कषितयो नमन्त ||
5.32.e: E’en the Celestial Axe bows down before him, and the Earth, lover-like, gives way to Indra.  As he imparts all vigour to these people, straightway the folk bend them to him the Godlike.

5.32.d: एकं नु तवा सत्पतिम पाञ्चजन्यं जातं शर्णोमि यशसं जनेषु | तम मे जग्र्भ्र आशसो नविष्ठं दोषा वस्तोर हवमानास इन्द्रम ||
5.32.e: I hear that thou wast born sole Lord of heroes of the Five Races, famed among the people.  As such my wishes have most lately grasped him, invoking Indra both at eve and morning.

5.32.d: एवा हि तवाम रतुथा यातयन्तम मघा विप्रेभ्यो ददतं शर्णोमि | किं ते बरह्माणो गर्हते सखायो ये तवाया निदधुः कामम इन्द्र ||
5.32.e: So, too, I hear of thee as in due season urging to action and enriching singers.  What have thy friends received from thee, the Brahmans who, faithful, rest their hopes on thee, O Indra?

5.33.d: महि महे तवसे दीध्ये नॄन इन्द्रायेत्था तवसे अतव्यान | यो अस्मै सुमतिं वाजसातौ सतुतो जने समर्यश चिकेत ||
5.33.e: GREAT praise to Indra, great and strong mid heroes, I ponder thus, the feeble to the Mighty,  Who with his band shows favour to this people, when lauded, in the fight where spoil is gathered.

5.33.d: स तवं न इन्द्र धियसानो अर्कैर हरीणां वर्षन योक्त्रम अश्रेः | या इत्था मघवन्न अनु जोषं वक्षो अभि परार्यः सक्षि जनान ||
5.33.e: So made attentive by our hymns, Steer! Indra! thou fastenedst the girth of thy Bay Coursers,  Which, Maghavan, at thy will thou drivest hither. With these subdue for us the men who hate us.

5.33.d: न ते त इन्द्राभ्य अस्मद रष्वायुक्तासो अब्रह्मता यद असन | तिष्ठा रथम अधि तं वज्रहस्ता रश्मिं देव यमसे सवश्वः ||
5.33.e: They were not turned to us-wtrd, lofty Indra! while yet through lack of prayer they stood unharnessed.  Ascend this chariot, thou whose hand wields thunder, and draw the rein, O Lord of noble horses.

5.33.d: पुरू यत त इन्द्र सन्त्य उक्था गवे चकर्थोर्वरासु युध्यन | ततक्षे सूर्याय चिद ओकसि सवे वर्षा समत्सु दासस्य नाम चित ||
5.33.e: Thou, because many lauds are thine, O Indra, wast active warring in the fields  for cattle.  For Sūrya in his own abode thou, Hero, formedst in fights even a Dāsa's nature.

5.33.d: वयं ते त इन्द्र ये च नरः शर्धो जज्ञाना याताश च रथाः | आस्माञ जगम्याद अहिशुष्म सत्वा भगो न हव्यः परभ्र्थेषु चारुः ||
5.33.e: Thine are we, Indra; thine are all these people, conscious of might, whose cars are set in motion.  Some hero come to us, O Strong as Ahi beauteous in war, to be invoked like Bhaga.

5.33.d: पप्र्क्षेण्यम इन्द्र तवे हय ओजो नर्म्णानि च नर्तमानो अमर्तः | स न एनीं वसवानो रयिं दाः परार्य सतुषे तुविमघस्य दानम ||
5.33.e: Strength much to be desired is in thee, Indra: the Immortal dances forth his hero exploits.  Such, Lord of Treasure, give us splendid riches. I praise the Friend's gift, his whose wealth is mighty.

5.33.d: एवा न इन्द्रोतिभिर अव पाहि गर्णतः शूर कारून | उत तवचं ददतो वाजसातौ पिप्रीहि मध्वः सुषुतस्य चारोः ||
5.33.e: Thus favour us, O Indra, with ihy succour; Hero, protect the bards who sing thy praises.  Be friendly in the fray to those who offer the skin of beautiful and well-pressed Soma.

5.33.d: उत तये मा पौरुकुत्स्यस्य सूरेस तरसदस्योर हिरणिनो रराणाः | वहन्तु मा दश शयेतासो अस्य गैरिक्षितस्य करतुभिर नु सश्चे ||
5.33.e: And these ten steeds which Trasadasyu gives me, the goldrich chief, the son of Purukutsa,  Resplendent in their brightness shall convey me. Gairiksita willed it and so came I hither.

5.33.d: उत तये मा मारुताश्वस्य शोणाः करत्वामघासो विदथस्य रातौ | सहस्रा मे चयवतानो ददान आनूकम अर्यो वपुषे नार्चत ||
5.33.e: And these, bestowed as sacrificial guerdon, the powerful tawny steeds of Marutasva;  And thousands which kind Cyavatana gave me, abundantly bestowed for my adornment.

5.33.d: उत तये मा धवन्यस्य जुष्टा लक्ष्मण्यस्य सुरुचो यतानाः | मह्ना रायः संवरणस्य रषेर वरजं न गावः परयता अपि गमन ||
5.33.e: And these commended horses, bright and active, by Dhvanya son of Laksmana presented,  Came unto me, as cows into the Ṛṣi Samvarana's stall, with magnitude of riches.

5.34.d: अजातशत्रुम अजरा सवर्वत्य अनु सवधामिता दस्मम ईयते | सुनोतन पचत बरह्मवाहसे पुरुष्टुताय परतरं दधातन ||
5.34.e: BOUNDLESS and wasting not, the heavenly food of Gods goes to the foeless One, doer of wondrous deeds.  Press out, make ready, offer gifts with special zeal to him whom many laud, accepter of the prayer.

5.34.d: आ यः सोमेन जठरम अपिप्रतामन्दत मघवा मध्वो अन्धसः | यद ईम मर्गाय हन्तवे महावधः सहस्रभ्र्ष्टिम उशना वधं यमत ||
5.34.e: He who filled full his belly with the Soma's juice, Maghavan, was delighted with the meath's sweet draught,  When Uśanā, that he might slay the monstrous beast, gave him the mighty weapon with a thousand points.

5.34.d: यो अस्मै घरंस उत वा य ऊधनि सोमं सुनोति भवति दयुमां अह | अपाप शक्रस ततनुष्टिम ऊहति तनूशुभ्रम मघवा यः कवासखः ||
5.34.e: Illustrious is the man whoever presseth out Soma for him in sunshine or in cloud and rain.  The mighty Maghavan who is the sage's Friend advanceth more and more his beauteous progeny.

5.34.d: यस्यावधीत पितरं यस्य मातरं यस्य शक्रो भरातरं नात ईषते | वेतीद व अस्य परयता यतंकरो न किल्बिषाद ईषते वस्व आकरः ||
5.34.e: The Strong God doth not flee away from him whose sire, whose mother or whose brother he hath done to death.  He, the Avenger, seeketh this man's offered gifts: this God, the source of riches, doth not flee from sin.

5.34.d: न पञ्चभिर दशभिर वष्ट्य आरभं नासुन्वता सचते पुष्यता चन | जिनाति वेद अमुया हन्ति वा धुनिर आ देवयुम भजति गोमति वरजे ||
5.34.e: He seeks no enterprise with five or ten to aid, nor stays with him who pours no juice though prospering well.  The Shaker conquers or slays in this way or that, and to the pious gives a stable full of kine.

5.34.d: वित्वक्षणः सम्र्तौ चक्रमासजो ऽसुन्वतो विषुणः सुन्वतो वर्धः | इन्द्रो विश्वस्य दमिता विभीषणो यथावशं नयति दासम आर्यः ||
5.34.e: Exceeding strong in war he stays the chariot wheel, and, hating him who pours not, prospers him who pours.  Indra the terrible, tamer of every man, as Ārya leads away the Dāsa at his will.

5.34.d: सम ईम पणेर अजति भोजनम मुषे वि दाशुषे भजति सूनरं वसु | दुर्गे चन धरियते विश्व आ पुरु जनो यो अस्य तविषीम अचुक्रुधत ||
5.34.e: He gathers up for plunder all the niggard’s gear: excellent wealth he gives to him who offers gifts.  Not even in wide stronghold may all the folk stand firm who have provoked to anger his surpassing might.

5.34.d: सं यज जनौ सुधनौ विश्वशर्धसाव अवेद इन्द्रो मघवा गोषु शुभ्रिषु | युजं हय अन्यम अक्र्त परवेपन्य उद ईं गव्यं सर्जते सत्वभिर धुनिः ||
5.34.e: When Indra Maghavan hath marked two wealthy men fighting for beauteous cows with all their followers,  He who stirs all things takes one as his close ally, and, Shaker, with his Heroes, sends the kine to him.

5.34.d: सहस्रसाम आग्निवेशिं गर्णीषे शत्रिम अग्न उपमां केतुम अर्यः | तस्मा आपः संयतः पीपयन्त तस्मिन कषत्रम अमवत तवेषम अस्तु ||
5.34.e: Agni! I laud the liberal Agnivesi, Satri the type and standard of the pious.  May the collected waters yield him plenty, and his be powerful and bright dominion.

5.35.d: यस ते साधिष्ठो ऽवस इन्द्र करतुष टम आ भर | अस्मभ्यं चर्षणीसहं सस्निं वाजेषु दुष्टरम ||
5.35.e: INDRA, for our assistance bring that most effectual power of thine,  Which conquers men for us, and wins the spoil, invincible in fight.

5.35.d: यद इन्द्र ते चतस्रो यच छूर सन्ति तिस्रः | यद वा पञ्च कषितीनाम अवस तत सु न आ भर ||
5.35.e: Indra, whatever aids be thine, four be they, or, O Hero, three,  Or those of the Five Tribes of men, bring quickly all that help to us.

5.35.d: आ ते ऽवो वरेण्यं वर्षन्तमस्य हूमहे | वर्षजूतिर हि जज्ञिष आभूभिर इन्द्र तुर्वणिः ||
5.35.e: The aid most excellent of thee the Mightiest hitherward we call,  For thou wast born with hero might, conquering, Indra, with the Strong.

5.35.d: वर्षा हय असि राधसे जज्ञिषे वर्ष्णि ते शवः | सवक्षत्रं ते धर्षन मनः सत्राहम इन्द्र पौंस्यम ||
5.35.e: Mighty to prosper us wast thou born, and mighty is the strength thou hast.  In native power thy soul is firm: thy valour, Indra, slays a host.

5.35.d: तवं तम इन्द्र मर्त्यम अमित्रयन्तम अद्रिवः | सर्वरथा शतक्रतो नि याहि शवसस पते ||
5.35.e: O Śatakratu, Lord of Strength, O Indra, Caster of the Stone.  With all thy chariot's force assail the man who shows himself thy foe.

5.35.d: तवाम इद वर्त्रहन्तम जनासो वर्क्तबर्हिषः | उग्रम पूर्वीषु पूर्व्यं हवन्ते वाजसातये ||
5.35.e: For, Mightiest Vṛtra-slayer, thee, fierce, foremost among many, folk  Whose sacred grass is trimmed invite to battle where the spoil is won.

5.35.d: अस्माकम इन्द्र दुष्टरम पुरोयावानम आजिषु | सयावानं धने-धने वाजयन्तम अवा रथम ||
5.35.e: Indra, do thou protect our car that mingles foremost in the fights,  That bears its part in every fray, invincible and seeking spoil.

5.35.d: अस्माकम इन्द्रेहि नो रथम अवा पुरंध्या | वयं शविष्ठ वार्यं दिवि शरवो दधीमहि दिवि सतोमम मनामहे ||
5.35.e: Come to us, Indra, and protect our car with thine intelligence.  May we, O Mightiest One, obtain excellent fame at break of day, and meditate our hymn at dawn.

5.36.d: स आ गमद इन्द्रो यो वसूनां चिकेतद दातुं दामनो रयीणाम | धन्वचरो न वंसगस तर्षाणश चकमानः पिबतु दुग्धम अंशुम ||
5.36.e: MAY Indra come to us, he who knows rightly to give forth treasures from his store of riches.  Even as a thirsty steer who roams the deserts may he drink eagerly the milked-out Soma.

5.36.d: आ ते हनू हरिवः शूर शिप्रे रुहत सोमो न पर्वतस्य पर्ष्ठे | अनु तवा राजन्न अर्वतो न हिन्वन गीर्भिर मदेम पुरुहूत विश्वे ||
5.36.e: Lord of Bay Horses, Hero, may the Soma rise to thy cheeks and jaws like mountain-ridges.  May we, O King, as he who driveth coursers, all joy in thee with hymns, invoked of many!

5.36.d: चक्रं न वर्त्तम पुरुहूत वेपते मनो भिया मे अमतेर इद अद्रिवः | रथाद अधि तवा जरिता सदाव्र्ध कुविन नु सतोषन मघवन पुरूवसुः ||
5.36.e: Invoked of many, Caster of the Stone my heart quakes like a rolling wheel for fear of penury.  Shall not Puruvasu the singer give thee praise, O ever-prospering Maghavan, mounted on thy car?

5.36.d: एष गरावेव जरिता त इन्द्रेयर्ति वाचम बर्हद आशुषाणः | पर सव्येन मघवन यंसि रायः पर दक्षिणिद धरिवो मा वि वेनः ||
5.36.e: Like the press-stone is this thy praiser, Indra. Loudly he lifts his voice with strong endeavour.  With thy left hand, O Maghavan, give us riches: with thy right, Lord of Bays, be not reluctant.

5.36.d: वर्षा तवा वर्षणं वर्धतु दयौर वर्षा वर्षभ्यां वहसे हरिभ्याम | स नो वर्षा वर्षरथः सुशिप्र वर्षक्रतो वर्षा वज्रिन भरे धाः ||
5.36.e: May the strong Heaven make thee the Strong wax stronger: Strong, thou art borne by thy two strong Bay Horses.  So, fair of cheek, with mighty chariot, mighty, uphold us, strong-willed, thunderarmed, in battle.

5.36.d: यो रोहितौ वाजिनौ वाजिनीवान तरिभिः शतैः सचमानाव अदिष्ट | यूने सम अस्मै कषितयो नमन्तां शरुतरथाय मरुतो दुवोया ||
5.36.e: Maruts, let all the people in obeisance bow down before this youthful Srutaratha,  Who, rich in steeds, gave me two dark red horses together with three hundred head of cattle.

5.37.d: सम भानुना यतते सूर्यस्याजुह्वानो घर्तप्र्ष्ठः सवञ्चाः | तस्मा अम्र्ध्रा उषसो वय उछान य इन्द्राय सुनवामेत्य आह ||
5.37.e: BEDEWED with holy oil and meetly worshipped, the Swift One vies with Sūrya's beam in splendour.  For him may mornings dawn without cessation who saith, Let us press Soma out for Indra.

5.37.d: समिद्धाग्निर वनवत सतीर्णबर्हिर युक्तग्रावा सुतसोमो जराते | गरावाणो यस्येषिरं वदन्त्य अयद अध्वर्युर हविषाव सिन्धुम ||
5.37.e: With kindled fire and strewn grass let him worship, and, Soma-presser, sing with stones adjusted:  And let the priest whose press-stones ring forth loudly, go down with his oblation to the river.

5.37.d: वधूर इयम पतिम इछन्त्य एति य ईं वहाते महिषीम इषिराम | आस्य शरवस्याद रथ आ च घोषात पुरू सहस्रा परि वर्तयाते ||
5.37.e: This wife is coming near who loves her husband who carries to his home a vigorous consort.  Here may his car seek fame, here loudly thunder, and his wheel make a thousand revolutions.

5.37.d: न स राजा वयथते यस्मिन्न इन्द्रस तीव्रं सोमम पिबति गोसखायम | आ सत्वनैर अजति हन्ति वर्त्रं कषेति कषितीः सुभगो नाम पुष्यन ||
5.37.e: No troubles vex that King in whose home Indra drinks the sharp Soma juice with milk commingled.  With heroes he drives near, he slays the foeman: Blest, cherishing that name, he guards his people.

5.37.d: पुष्यात कषेमे अभि योगे भवात्य उभे वर्तौ संयती सं जयाति | परियः सूर्ये परियो अग्ना भवाति य इन्द्राय सुतसोमो ददाशत ||
5.37.e: May he support in peace and win in battle: he masters both the hosts that meet together.  Dear shall he be to Sūrya, dear to Agni, who with pressed Soma offers gifts to India.

5.38.d: उरोष ट इन्द्र राधसो विभ्वी रातिः शतक्रतो | अधा नो विश्वचर्षणे दयुम्ना सुक्षत्र मंहय ||
5.38.e: WIDE, Indra Śatakratu, spreads the bounty of thine ample grace:  So, Lord of fair dominion, Friend of all men, give us splendid wealth.

5.38.d: यद ईम इन्द्र शरवाय्यम इषं शविष्ठ दधिषे | पप्रथे दीर्घश्रुत्तमं हिरण्यवर्ण दुष्टरम ||
5.38.e: The food which, Mightiest Indra, thou possessest worthy of renown  Is bruited as most widely famed, invincible, O Golden-hued!

5.38.d: शुष्मासो ये ते अद्रिवो मेहना केतसापः | उभा देवाव अभिष्टये दिवश च गमश च राजथः ||
5.38.e: O Darter of the Stone, the powers which readily obey thy will,—  Divinities, both thou and they, ye rule, to guard them, earth and heaven.

5.38.d: उतो नो अस्य कस्य चिद दक्षस्य तव वर्त्रहन | अस्मभ्यं नर्म्णम आ भरास्मभ्यं नर्मणस्यसे ||
5.38.e: And from whatever power of thine, O Vṛtra-slayer, it may be,  Bring thou to us heroic strength: thou hast a man's regard for us.

5.38.d: नू त आभिर अभिष्टिभिस तव शर्मञ छतक्रतो | इन्द्र सयाम सुगोपाः शूर सयाम सुगोपाः ||
5.38.e: In thy protection, with these aids of thine, O Lord of Hundred Powers,  Indra, may we be guarded well, Hero, may we be guarded well.

5.39.d: यद इन्द्र चित्र मेहनास्ति तवादातम अद्रिवः | राधस तन नो विदद्वस उभयाहस्त्य आ भर ||
5.39.e: STONE-DARTING Indra. Wondrous One, what wealth is richly given from thee,  That bounty, Treasure-Finder! bring filling both thy hands, to us.

5.39.d: यन मन्यसे वरेण्यम इन्द्र दयुक्षं तद आ भर | विद्याम तस्य ते वयम अकूपारस्य दावने ||
5.39.e: Bring what thou deemest worth the wish, O Indra, that which is in heaven.  So may we know thee as thou art, boundless in thy munificence.

5.39.d: यत ते दित्सु परराध्यम मनो अस्ति शरुतम बर्हत | तेन दर्ळ्हा चिद अद्रिव आ वाजं दर्षि सातये ||
5.39.e: Thy lofty spirit, far-renowned as fain to give and prompt to win,—  With this thou rendest e’en the firm, Stone-Darter! so to gain thee strength.

5.39.d: मंहिष्ठं वो मघोनां राजानं चर्षणीनाम | इन्द्रम उप परशस्तये पूर्वीभिर जुजुषे गिरः ||
5.39.e: Singers with many songs have made Indra propitious to their fame,  Him who is King of human kind, most liberal of your wealthy ones.

5.39.d: अस्मा इत काव्यं वच उक्थम इन्द्राय शंस्यम | तस्मा उ बरह्मवाहसे गिरो वर्धन्त्य अत्रयो गिरः शुम्भन्त्य अत्रयः ||
5.39.e: To him, to Indra must be sung the poet's word, the hymn of praise.  To him, accepter of the prayer, the Atris raise their songs on high, the Atris beautify their songs.

5.40.d: आ याह्य अद्रिभिः सुतं सोमं सोमपते पिब | वर्षन्न इन्द्र वर्षभिर वर्त्रहन्तम ||
5.40.e: COME thou to what the stones have pressed, drink Soma, O thou Soma's Lord,  Indra best Vṛtra-slayer Strong One, with the Strong.

5.40.d: वर्षा गरावा वर्षा मदो वर्षा सोमो अयं सुतः | वर्षन्न इन्द्र वर्षभिर वर्त्रहन्तम ||
5.40.e: Strong is the stone, the draught is strong, strong is this Soma that is pressed,  Indra, best Vṛtra-slayer, Strong One with the Strong.

5.40.d: वर्षा तवा वर्षणं हुवे वज्रिञ चित्राभिर ऊतिभिः | वर्षन्न इन्द्र वर्षभिर वर्त्रहन्तम ||
5.40.e: As strong I call on thee the Strong, O Thunder-armed, with various aids,  Indra, best Vṛtra-slayer, Strong One with the Strong.

5.40.d: रजीषी वज्री वर्षभस तुराषाट छुष्मी राजा वर्त्रहा सोमपावा | युक्त्वा हरिभ्याम उप यासद अर्वाङ माध्यंदिने सवने मत्सद इन्द्रः ||
5.40.e: Impetuous, Thunderer, Strong, quelling the mighty, King, potent, Vṛtra-slayer, Soma-drinker,  May he come hither with his yoked Bay Horses; may Indra gladden him at the noon libation.

5.40.d: यत तवा सूर्य सवर्भानुस तमसाविध्यद आसुरः | अक्षेत्रविद यथा मुग्धो भुवनान्य अदीधयुः ||
5.40.e: O Sūrya, when the Asura's descendant Svarbhanu, pierced thee through and through with darkness,  All creatures looked like one who is bewildered, who knoweth not the place where he is standing.

5.40.d: सवर्भानोर अध यद इन्द्र माया अवो दिवो वर्तमाना अवाहन | गूळ्हं सूर्यं तमसापव्रतेन तुरीयेण बरह्मणाविन्दद अत्रिः ||
5.40.e: What time thou smotest down Svarbhanu's magic that spread itself beneath the sky, O Indra,  By his fourth sacred prayer Atri disoovered Sūrya concealed in gloom that stayed his function.

5.40.d: मा माम इमं तव सन्तम अत्र इरस्या दरुग्धो भियसा नि गारीत | तवम मित्रो असि सत्यराधास तौ मेहावतं वरुणश च राजा ||
5.40.e: Let not the oppressor with this dread, through anger swallow me up, for I am thine, O Atri.  Mitra art thou, the sender of true blessings: thou and King Varuṇa be both my helpers.

5.40.d: गराव्णो बरह्मा युयुजानः सपर्यन कीरिणा देवान नमसोपशिक्षन | अत्रिः सूर्यस्य दिवि चक्षुर आधात सवर्भानोर अप माया अघुक्षत ||
5.40.e: The Brahman Atri, as he set the press-stones, serving the Gods with praise and adoration,  Established in the heaven the eye of Sūrya, and caused Svarbhanu's magic arts to vanish.

5.40.d: यं वै सूर्यं सवर्भानुस तमसाविध्यद आसुरः | अत्रयस तम अन्व अविन्दन नह्य अन्ये अशक्नुवन ||
5.40.e: The Atris found the Sun again, him whom Svarbhanu of the brood  Of Asuras had pierced with gloom. This none besides had power to do.

5.41.d: को नु वाम मित्रावरुणाव रतायन दिवो वा महः पार्थिवस्य वा दे | रतस्य वा सदसि तरासीथां नो यज्ञायते वा पशुषो न वाजान ||
5.41.e: WHO, Mitra-Varuṇa, is your pious servant to give you gifts from earth or mighty heaven?  Preserve us in the seat of holy Order, and give the offerer power that winneth cattle.

5.41.d: ते नो मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमायुर इन्द्र रभुक्षा मरुतो जुषन्त | नमोभिर वा ये दधते सुव्र्क्तिं सतोमं रुद्राय मीळ्हुषे सजोषाः ||
5.41.e: May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, and Āyu, Indra Ṛbhukṣan, and the Maruts, love us,  And they who of one mind with bounteous Rudra accept the hymn and laud with adorations.

5.41.d: आ वां येष्ठाश्विना हुवध्यै वातस्य पत्मन रथ्यस्य पुष्टौ | उत वा दिवो असुराय मन्म परान्धांसीव यज्यवे भरध्वम ||
5.41.e: You will I call to feed the car-horse, Aśvins, with the wind's flight swiftest of those who travel:  Or also to the Asura of heaven, Worshipful, bring a hymn as ’twere libation.

5.41.d: पर सक्षणो दिव्यः कण्वहोता तरितो दिवः सजोषा वातो अग्निः | पूषा भगः परभ्र्थे विश्वभोजा आजिं न जग्मुर आश्वश्वतमाः ||
5.41.e: The heavenly Victor, he whose priest is Kaṇva, Tṛta with Dyaus accordant, Vāta, Agni,  All-feeding Pūṣan, Bhaga sought the oblation, as they whose steeds are fleetest seek the contest.

5.41.d: पर वो रयिं युक्ताश्वम भरध्वं राय एषे ऽवसे दधीत धीः | सुशेव एवैर औशिजस्य होता ये व एवा मरुतस तुराणाम ||
5.41.e: Bring ye your riches forward borne on horses: let thought be framed for help and gain of treasure.  Blest he the priest of Auśija through courses, the courses which are yours the fleet, O Maruts.

5.41.d: पर वो वायुं रथयुजं कर्णुध्वम पर देवं विप्रम पनितारम अर्कैः | इषुध्यव रतसापः पुरंधीर वस्वीर नो अत्र पत्नीर आ धिये धुः ||
5.41.e: Bring hither him who yokes the car, your Vāyu, who praises with his songs, the God and Singer;  And, praying and devout, noble and prudent, may the Gods’ Spouses in their thoughts retain us.

5.41.d: उप व एषे वन्द्येभिः शूषैः पर यह्वी दिवश चितयद्भिर अर्कैः | उषासानक्ता विदुषीव विश्वम आ हा वहतो मर्त्याय यज्ञम ||
5.41.e: I speed to you with powers that should be honoured, with songs distinguishing Heaven's mighty Daughters,  Morning and Night, the Two, as ’twere all-knowing: these bring the sacrifice unto the mortal.

5.41.d: अभि वो अर्चे पोष्यावतो नॄन वास्तोष पतिं तवष्टारं रराणः | धन्या सजोषा धिषणा नमोभिर वनस्पतींर ओषधी राय एषे ||
5.41.e: You I extol, the nourishers of heroes bringing you gifts, Vastospati and Tvaṣṭar-  Rich Dhiṣaṇā accords through our obeisance - andTrees and Plants, for the swift gain of riches.

5.41.d: तुजे नस तने पर्वताः सन्तु सवैतवो ये वसवो न वीराः | पनित आप्त्यो यजतः सदा नो वर्धान नः शंसं नर्यो अभिष्टौ ||
5.41.e: Ours be the Parvatas, even they, for offspring, free-moving, who are Heroes like the Vasus.  May holy Āptya, Friend of man, exalted, strengthen our word for ever and be near us.

5.41.d: वर्ष्णो अस्तोषि भूम्यस्य गर्भं तरितो नपातम अपां सुव्र्क्ति | गर्णीते अग्निर एतरी न शूषैः शोचिष्केशो नि रिणाति वना ||
5.41.e: Tṛta praised him, germ of the earthly hero, with pure songs him the Offspring of the Waters.  Agn; with might neighs loudly like a charger: he of the flaming hair destroys the forests.

5.41.d: कथा महे रुद्रियाय बरवाम कद राये चिकितुषे भगाय | आप ओषधीर उत नो ऽवन्तु दयौर वना गिरयो वर्क्षकेशाः ||
5.41.e: How shall we speak to the great might of Rudra? How speak to Bhaga who takes thought for riches?  May Plants, the Waters, and the Sky preserve us, and Woods and Mountains with their trees for tresses.

5.41.d: शर्णोतु न ऊर्जाम पतिर गिरः स नभस तरीयां इषिरः परिज्मा | शर्ण्वन्त्व आपः पुरो न शुभ्राः परि सरुचो बब्र्हाणस्याद्रेः ||
5.41.e: May the swift Wanderer, Lord of refreshments listen to our songs, who speeds throuih cloudy heaven:  And may the Waters, bright like castles, hear us, as they flow onward from the cloven mountain.

5.41.d: विदा चिन नु महान्तो ये व एवा बरवाम दस्मा वार्यं दधानाः | वयश चन सुभ्व आव यन्ति कषुभा मर्तम अनुयतं वधस्नैः ||
5.41.e: We know your ways, ye Mighty Ones receiving choice meed, ye Wonderful, we will proclaim it.  Even strong birds descend not to the mortal who strives to reach them with swift blow and weapons.

5.41.d: आ दैव्यानि पार्थिवानि जन्मापश चाछा सुमखाय वोचम | वर्धन्तां दयावो गिरश चन्द्राग्रा उदा वर्धन्ताम अभिषाता अर्णाः ||
5.41.e: Celestial and terrestrial generations, and Waters will I summon to the feasting.  May days with bright dawns cause my songs to prosper, and may the conquered streams increase their waters.

5.41.d: पदे-पदे मे जरिमा नि धायि वरूत्री वा शक्रा या पायुभिश च | सिषक्तु माता मही रसा नः समत सूरिभिर रजुहस्त रजुवनिः ||
5.41.e: Duly to each one hath my laud been offered. Strong be Varūtrī with her powers to succour.  May the great Mother Rasā here befriend us, straight-handed, with the princes, striving forward.

5.41.d: कथा दाशेम नमसा सुदानून एवया मरुतो अछोक्तौ परश्रवसो मरुतो अछोक्तौ | मा नो ऽहिर बुध्न्यो रिषे धाद अस्माकम भूद उपमातिवनिः ||
5.41.e: How may we serve the Liberal Ones with worship, the Maruts swift of course in invocation, the Maruts far-renowned in invocation?  Let not the Dragon of the Deep annoy us, and gladly may he welcome our addresses.

5.41.d: इति चिन नु परजायै पशुमत्यै देवासो वनते मर्त्यो व आ देवासो वनते मर्त्यो वः | अत्रा शिवां तन्वो धासिम अस्या जरां चिन मे निर्र्तिर जग्रसीत ||
5.41.e: Thus thinking, O ye Gods, the mortal wins you to give him increase of his herds of cattle: the mortal wins him, O ye Gods, your favour.  Here he wins wholesome food to feed this body: as for mine old age, Nirrti consume it

5.41.d: तां वो देवाः सुमतिम ऊर्जयन्तीम इषम अश्याम वसवः शसा गोः | सा नः सुदानुर मर्ळयन्ती देवी परति दरवन्ती सुविताय गम्याः ||
5.41.e: O Gods, may we obtain from you this favour, strengthening food through the Cow's praise, ye Vasus.  May she who gives good gifts, the gracious Goddes. s, come speeding nigh to us for our well-being.

5.41.d: अभि न इळा यूथस्य माता समन नदीभिर उर्वशी वा गर्णातु | उर्वशी वा बर्हद्दिवा गर्णानाभ्यूर्ण्वाना परभ्र्थस्यायोः ||
5.41.e: May Iḷā, Mother of the herds of cattle, and Urvasi with all the streams accept us;  May Urvasi in lofty heaven accepting, as she partakes the oblation of the living,

5.41.d: सिषक्तु न ऊर्जव्यस्य पुष्टेः ||
5.41.e: Visit us while she shares Urjavya's food.

5.42.d: पर शंतमा वरुणं दीधिती गीर मित्रम भगम अदितिं नूनम अश्याः | पर्षद्योनिः पञ्चहोता शर्णोत्व अतूर्तपन्था असुरो मयोभुः ||
5.42.e: Now may our sweetest song with deep devotion reach Varuṇa, Mitra, Aditi, and Bhaga.  May the Five Priests' Lord, dwelling in oblations, bliss-giving Asura, hear, whose paths are open.

5.42.d: परति मे सतोमम अदितिर जग्र्भ्यात सूनुं न माता हर्द्यं सुशेवम | बरह्म परियं देवहितं यद अस्त्य अहम मित्रे वरुणे यन मयोभु ||
5.42.e: May Aditi welcome, even as a mother her dear heart-gladdening son, my song that lauds her.  The prayer they love, bliss-giving, God-appointed, I offer unto Varuṇa and Mitra.

5.42.d: उद ईरय कवितमं कवीनाम उनत्तैनम अभि मध्वा घर्तेन | स नो वसूनि परयता हितानि चन्द्राणि देवः सविता सुवाति ||
5.42.e: In spirit him, the Sagest of the Sages; with sacrificial oil and meath bedew him  So then let him, God Savitar, provide us excellent, ready, and resplendent treasures.

5.42.d: सम इन्द्र णो मनसा नेषि गोभिः सं सूरिभिर हरिवः सं सवस्ति | सम बरह्मणा देवहितं यद अस्ति सं देवानां सुमत्या यज्ञियानाम ||
5.42.e: With willing mind, Indra, vouchsafe us cattle, prosperity, Lord of Bays! and pious patrons;  And, with the sacred prayer by Gods appointed, give us the holy Deities' lovingkindness.

5.42.d: देवो भगः सविता रायो अंश इन्द्रो वर्त्रस्य संजितो धनानाम | रभुक्षा वाज उत वा पुरंधिर अवन्तु नो अम्र्तासस तुरासः ||
5.42.e: God Bhaga, Savitar who deals forth riches, Indra, and they who conquer Vṛtra's treasures,  And Vāja and Ṛbhukṣan and Purandhi, the Mighty and Immortal Ones, protect us!

5.42.d: मरुत्वतो अप्रतीतस्य जिष्णोर अजूर्यतः पर बरवामा कर्तानि | न ते पूर्वे मघवन नापरासो न वीर्यं नूतनः कश चनाप ||
5.42.e: Let us declare his deeds, the undecaying unrivalled Victor whom the Maruts follow.  None of old times, O Maghavan, nor later, none of these days hath reached thy hero prowess.

5.42.d: उप सतुहि परथमं रत्नधेयम बर्हस्पतिं सनितारं धनानाम | यः शंसते सतुवते शम्भविष्ठः पुरूवसुर आगमज जोहुवानम ||
5.42.e: Praise him the Chief who gives the boon of riches, Bṛhaspati distributor of treasures,  Who, blessing most the man who sings and praises, comes with abundant wealth to his invoker.

5.42.d: तवोतिभिः सचमाना अरिष्टा बर्हस्पते मघवानः सुवीराः | ये अश्वदा उत वा सन्ति गोदा ये वस्त्रदाः सुभगास तेषु रायः ||
5.42.e: Tended, Bṛhaspati, with thy protections, the princes are unharmed and girt by heroes.  Wealth that brings bliss is found among the givers of horses and of cattle and of raiment.

5.42.d: विसर्माणं कर्णुहि वित्तम एषां ये भुञ्जते अप्र्णन्तो न उक्थैः | अपव्रतान परसवे वाव्र्धानान बरह्मद्विषः सूर्याद यावयस्व ||
5.42.e: Make their wealth flee who, through our hymns enjoying their riches, yield us not an ample guerdon.  Far from the sun keep those who hate devotion, the godless, prospering in their vocation.

5.42.d: य ओहते रक्षसो देववीताव अचक्रेभिस तम मरुतो नि यात | यो वः शमीं शशमानस्य निन्दात तुछ्यान कामान करते सिष्विदानः ||
5.42.e: With wheelless chariots drive down him, O Maruts, who at the feasts of Gods regards the demons.  May he, though bathed in sweat, form empty wishes, who blames his sacred rite who toils to serve you.

5.42.d: तम उ षटुहि यः सविषुः सुधन्वा यो विश्वस्य कषयति भेषजस्य | यक्ष्वा महे सौमनसाय रुद्रं नमोभिर देवम असुरं दुवस्य ||
5.42.e: Praise him whose bow is strong and sure his arrow, him who is Lord of every balm that bealeth.  Worship thou Rudra for his great good favour: adore the Asura, God, with salutations.

5.42.d: दमूनसो अपसो ये सुहस्ता वर्ष्णः पत्नीर नद्यो विभ्वतष्टाः | सरस्वती बर्हद्दिवोत राका दशस्यन्तीर वरिवस्यन्तु शुभ्राः ||
5.42.e: May the House-friends, the cunning-handed Artists, may the Steer's Wives, the streams carved out by Vibhvan,  And may the fair Ones honour and befriend us, Sarasvatī, Brhaddiva, and Rākā.

5.42.d: पर सू महे सुशरणाय मेधां गिरम भरे नव्यसीं जायमानाम | य आहना दुहितुर वक्षणासु रूपा मिनानो अक्र्णोद इदं नः ||
5.42.e: My newest song, thought that now springs within me, I offer to the Great, the Sure Protector,  Who made for us this All, in fond love laying each varied form within his Daughter's bosom.

5.42.d: पर सुष्टुति सतनयन्तं रुवन्तम इळस पतिं जरितर नूनम अश्याः | यो अब्दिमां उदनिमां इयर्ति पर विद्युता रोदसी उक्षमाणः ||
5.42.e: Now, even now, may thy fair praise, O Singer, attain Idaspati who roars and thunders,  Who, rich in clouds and waters with his lightning speeds forth bedewing both the earth and heaven.

5.42.d: एष सतोमो मारुतं शर्धो अछा रुद्रस्य सूनूंर युवन्यूंर उद अश्याः | कामो राये हवते मा सवस्त्य उप सतुहि पर्षदश्वां अयासः ||
5.42.e: May this my laud attain the troop of Maruts, those who are youths in act, the Sons of Rudra.  The wish calls me to riches and well-being: praise the unwearied Ones whose steeds are dappled.

5.42.d: परैष सतोमः पर्थिवीम अन्तरिक्षं वनस्पतींर ओषधी राये अश्याः | देवो-देवः सुहवो भूतु मह्यम मा नो माता पर्थिवी दुर्मतौ धात ||
5.42.e: May this my laud reach earth and air's mid-region, and forest trees and plants to win me riches.  May every Deity be swift to listen, and Mother Earth with no ill thought regard me.

5.42.d: उरौ देवा अनिबाधे सयाम | सम अश्विनोर अवसा नूतनेन मयोभुवा सुप्रणीती गमेम | आ नो रयिं वहतम ओत वीरान आ विश्वान्य अम्र्ता सौभगानि ||
5.42.e: Gods, may we dwell in free untroubled bliss.

5.43.d: आ धेनवः पयसा तूर्ण्यर्था अमर्धन्तीर उप नो यन्तु मध्वा | महो राये बर्हतीः सप्त विप्रो मयोभुवो जरिता जोहवीति ||
5.43.e: MAY the Milch-cows who hasten to their object come harmless unto us with liquid sweetness.  The Singer, lauding, calls, for ample riches, the Seven Mighty Ones who bring enjoyment.

5.43.d: आ सुष्टुती नमसा वर्तयध्यै दयावा वाजाय पर्थिवी अम्र्ध्रे | पिता माता मधुवचाः सुहस्ता भरे-भरे नो यशसाव अविष्टाम ||
5.43.e: With reverence and fair praise will I bring hither, for sake of strength, exhaustless Earth and Heaven.  Father and Mother, sweetof speech, fairhanded, may they, far-famed, in every fight protect us.

5.43.d: अध्वर्यवश चक्र्वांसो मधूनि पर वायवे भरत चारु शुक्रम | होतेव नः परथमः पाह्य अस्य देव मध्वो ररिमा ते मदाय ||
5.43.e: Adhvaryus, make the sweet libations ready, and bring the beautiful bright juice to Vāyu.  God, as our Priest, be thou the first to drink it: we give thee of the mead to make thee joyful.

5.43.d: दश कषिपो युञ्जते बाहू अद्रिं सोमस्य या शमितारा सुहस्ता | मध्वो रसं सुगभस्तिर गिरिष्ठां चनिश्चदद दुदुहे शुक्रम अंशुः ||
5.43.e: Two arms-the Soma's dexterous immo. lators-and the ten fingers set and fix the press-stone.  The stalk hath poured, fair with its spreading branches, the mead's bright glittering juice that dwells on mountains.

5.43.d: असावि ते जुजुषाणाय सोमः करत्वे दक्षाय बर्हते मदाय | हरी रथे सुधुरा योगे अर्वाग इन्द्र परिया कर्णुहि हूयमानः ||
5.43.e: The Soma hath been pressed for thee, its lover, to give thee power and might and high enjoyment.  Invoked, turn hither in thy car, O Indra, at need, thy two well-trained and dear Bay Horses.

5.43.d: आ नो महीम अरमतिं सजोषा गनां देवीं नमसा रातहव्याम | मधोर मदाय बर्हतीम रतज्ञाम आग्ने वह पथिभिर देवयानैः ||
5.43.e: Bring by God-traversed paths, accordant, Agni, the great Aramati, Celestial Lady,  Exalted, worshipped with our gifts and homage, who knoweth holy Law, to drink sweet Soma.

5.43.d: अञ्जन्ति यम परथयन्तो न विप्रा वपावन्तं नाग्निना तपन्तः | पितुर न पुत्र उपसि परेष्ठ आ घर्मो अग्निम रतयन्न असादि ||
5.43.e: As on his father's lap the son, the darling, so on the fire is set the sacred caldron,  Which holy singers deck, as if extending and heating that which holds the fatty membrane.

5.43.d: अछा मही बर्हती शंतमा गीर दूतो न गन्त्व अश्विना हुवध्यै | मयोभुवा सरथा यातम अर्वाग गन्तं निधिं धुरम आणिर न नाभिम ||
5.43.e: Hither, as herald to invite the Aśvins, come the great lofty song, most sweet and pleasant!  Come in one car, joy-givers! to the banquet, like the bolt binding pole and nave, come hither.

5.43.d: पर तव्यसो नमक्तिं तुरस्याहम पूष्ण उत वायोर अदिक्षि | या राधसा चोदितारा मतीनां या वाजस्य दरविणोदा उत तमन ||
5.43.e: I have declared this speech of adoration to mightiest Pūṣan and victorious Vāyu,  Who by their bounty are the hymns' inspirers, and of themselves give power as a possession.

5.43.d: आ नामभिर मरुतो वक्षि विश्वान आ रूपेभिर जातवेदो हुवानः | यज्ञं गिरो जरितुः सुष्टुतिं च विश्वे गन्त मरुतो विश्व ऊती ||
5.43.e: Invoked by us bring hither, jatavedas the Maruts all under their names and figures.  Come to the sacrifice with aid all Maruts, all to the songs and praises of the singer!

5.43.d: आ नो दिवो बर्हतः पर्वताद आ सरस्वती यजता गन्तु यज्ञम | हवं देवी जुजुषाणा घर्ताची शग्मां नो वाचम उशती शर्णोतु ||
5.43.e: From high heaven may Sarasvatī the Holy visit our sacrifice, and from the mountain.  Eager, propitious, may the balmy Goddess hear our effectual speech, our invocation.

5.43.d: आ वेधसं नीलप्र्ष्ठम बर्हन्तम बर्हस्पतिं सदने सादयध्वम | सादद्योनिं दम आ दीदिवांसं हिरण्यवर्णम अरुषं सपेम ||
5.43.e: Set in his seat the God whose back is dusky, Bṛhaspati the lofty, the Disposer.  Him let us worship, set within the dwelling, the red, the golden-hued, the allresplendent.

5.43.d: आ धर्णसिर बर्हद्दिवो रराणो विश्वेभिर गन्त्व ओमभिर हुवानः | गना वसान ओषधीर अम्र्ध्रस तरिधातुश्र्ङगो वर्षभो वयोधाः ||
5.43.e: May the Sustainer, high in heaven, come hither, the Bounteous One, invoked, with all his favours,  Dweller with Dames divine, with plants, unwearied, the Steer with triple horn, the life-bestower.

5.43.d: मातुष पदे परमे शुक्र आयोर विपन्यवो रास्पिरासो अग्मन | सुशेव्यं नमसा रातहव्याः शिशुम मर्जन्त्य आयवो न वासे ||
5.43.e: The tuneful eloquent priests of him who liveth have sought the Mother's bright and loftiest station.  As living men, with offered gifts and homage they deck the most auspicious Child to clothe him.

5.43.d: बर्हद वयो बर्हते तुभ्यम अग्ने धियाजुरो मिथुनासः सचन्त | देवो-देवः सुहवो भूतु मह्यम मा नो माता पर्थिवी दुर्मतौ धात ||
5.43.e: Agni, great vital power is thine, the mighty: pairs waxing old in their devotion seek thee.  May every Deity be swift to listen, and Mother Earth with no ill thought regard me.

5.43.d: उरौ देवा अनिबाधे सयाम | सम अश्विनोर अवसा नूतनेन मयोभुवा सुप्रणीती गमेम | आ नो रयिं वहतम ओत वीरान आ विश्वान्य अम्र्ता सौभगानि ||
5.43.e: Gods, may we dwell in free untroubled bliss.

5.44.d: तम परत्नथा पूर्वथा विश्वथेमथा जयेष्ठतातिम बर्हिषदं सवर्विदम | परतीचीनं वर्जनं दोहसे गिराशुं जयन्तम अनु यासु वर्धसे ||
5.44.e: As in the first old times, as all were wont, as now, he draweth forth the power turned hitherward with song,  The Princedom throned on holy grass, who findeth light, swift, conquering in the' plants wherein he waxeth strong.

5.44.d: शरिये सुद्र्शीर उपरस्य याः सवर विरोचमानः ककुभाम अचोदते | सुगोपा असि न दभाय सुक्रतो परो मायाभिर रत आस नाम ते ||
5.44.e: Shining to him who leaves heaven's regions undisturbed, which to his sheen who is beneath show fair in light,  Good guardian art thou, not to be deceived, Most Wise! Far from deceits thy name dwelleth in holy Law.

5.44.d: अत्यं हविः सचते सच च धातु चारिष्टगातुः स होता सहोभरिः | परसर्स्राणो अनु बर्हिर वर्षा शिशुर मध्ये युवाजरो विस्रुहा हितः ||
5.44.e: Truth waits upon oblation present and to come: naught checks him in his way, this vic tory- bringing Priest:  The Mighty Child who glides along the sacred grass, the undecaying Youth set in the midst of plants.

5.44.d: पर व एते सुयुजो यामन्न इष्टये नीचीर अमुष्मै यम्य रताव्र्धः | सुयन्तुभिः सर्वशासैर अभीशुभिः करिविर नामानि परवणे मुषायति ||
5.44.e: These come, well-yoked, to you for furtherance in the rite: down come the twinborn strengtheners of Law for him,  With reins easily guided and commanding all. In the deep fall the hide stealeth away their names.

5.44.d: संजर्भुराणस तरुभिः सुतेग्र्भं वयाकिनं चित्तगर्भासु सुस्वरुः | धारवाकेष्व रजुगाथ शोभसे वर्धस्व पत्नीर अभि जीवो अध्वरे ||
5.44.e: Thou, moving beauteously in visibly pregnant ones, snatching with trees the branching plant that grasps the juice,  Shinest, true Singer! mid the upholders of the voice. Increase thy Consorts thou, lively at sacrifice.

5.44.d: याद्र्ग एव दद्र्शे ताद्र्ग उच्यते सं छायया दधिरे सिध्रयाप्स्व आ | महीम अस्मभ्यम उरुषाम उरु जरयो बर्हत सुवीरम अनपच्युतं सहः ||
5.44.e: Like as he is beheld such is he said to be.  They with effectual splendour in the floods have made  Earth yield us room enough and amply wide extent, great might invincible, with store of hero sons.

5.44.d: वेत्य अग्रुर जनिवान वा अति सप्र्धः समर्यता मनसा सूर्यः कविः | घरंसं रक्षन्तम परि विश्वतो गयम अस्माकं शर्म वनवत सवावसुः ||
5.44.e: Sūrya the Sage, as if unwedded, with a Spouse, in battle-loving spirit moveth o’er the foes.  May he, self-excellent, grant us a sheltering home, a house that wards the fierce heat off on every side.

5.44.d: जयायांसम अस्य यतुनस्य केतुन रषिस्वरं चरति यासु नाम ते | याद्र्श्मिन धायि तम अपस्यया विदद य उ सवयं वहते सो अरं करत ||
5.44.e: Thy name, sung forth by Ṛṣis in these hymns of ours, goes to the loftier One with this swift mover's light.  By skill he wins the boon whereon his heart is set: he who bestirs himself shall bring the thing to pass.

5.44.d: समुद्रम आसाम अव तस्थे अग्रिमा न रिष्यति सवनं यस्मिन्न आयता | अत्रा न हार्दि करवणस्य रेजते यत्रा मतिर विद्यते पूतबन्धनी ||
5.44.e: The chief and best of these abideth in the sea, nor doth libation fail wherein it is prolonged.  The heart of him who praiseth trembleth not in fear there where the hymn is found connected with the pure.

5.44.d: स हि कषत्रस्य मनसस्य चित्तिभिर एवावदस्य यजतस्य सध्रेः | अवत्सारस्य सप्र्णवाम रण्वभिः शविष्ठं वाजं विदुषा चिद अर्ध्यम ||
5.44.e: For it is he: with though to of Ksatra, Manasa, of Yajata, and Sadhri, and Evavada,  With Avatsara's sweet songs will we strive to win the mightiest strength which even he who knows should gain.

5.44.d: शयेन आसाम अदितिः कक्ष्यो मदो विश्ववारस्य यजतस्य मायिनः | सम अन्यम-अन्यम अर्थयन्त्य एतवे विदुर विषाणम परिपानम अन्ति ते ||
5.44.e: The Hawk is their full source, girth-stretching rapturous drink of Visvavara, of Mayin, and Yajata.  They ever seek a fresh draught so that they may come, know when thy time to halt and drink thy fill is near.

5.44.d: सदाप्र्णो यजतो वि दविषो वधीद बाहुव्र्क्तः शरुतवित तर्यो वः सचा | उभा स वरा परत्य एति भाति च यद ईं गणम भजते सुप्रयावभिः ||
5.44.e: Sadaprna the holy, Tarya, Srutavit, and Bahuvrkta, joined with you, have slain the foes.  He gains his wish in both the worlds and brightly shines-when he adores the host with well-advancing steeds.

5.44.d: सुतम्भरो यजमानस्य सत्पतिर विश्वासाम ऊधः स धियाम उदञ्चनः | भरद धेनू रसवच छिश्रिये पयो ऽनुब्रुवाणो अध्य एति न सवपन ||
5.44.e: The worshipper's defender is Sutambhara, producer and uplifter of all holy thoughts.  The milch-cow brought, sweet-flavoured milk was dealt around. Who speaks the bidding text knows this, not he who sleeps.

5.44.d: यो जागार तम रचः कामयन्ते यो जागार तम उ सामानि यन्ति | यो जागार तम अयं सोम आह तवाहम अस्मि सख्ये नयोकाः ||
5.44.e: The sacred hymns love him who wakes and watches: to him who watches come the Sāma verses.  This Soma saith unto the man who watches, I rest and have my dwelling in thy friendship.

5.44.d: अग्निर जागार तम रचः कामयन्ते ऽगनिर जागार तम उ सामानि यन्ति | अग्निर जागार तम अयं सोम आह तवाहम अस्मि सख्ये नयोकाः ||
5.44.e: Agni is watchful, and the gcas love him; Agni is watchful, Sāma verses seek him.  Agni is watchful, to him saith this Soma, I rest and have my dwelling in thy friendship.

5.45.d: विदा दिवो विष्यन्न अद्रिम उक्थैर आयत्या उषसो अर्चिनो गुः | अपाव्र्त वरजिनीर उत सवर गाद वि दुरो मानुषीर देव आवः ||
5.45.e: BARDS of approaching Dawn who know the heavens are come with hymns to throw the mountain open.  The Sun hath risen and oped the stable portals: the doors of men, too, hath the God thrown open.

5.45.d: वि सूर्यो अमतिं न शरियं साद ओर्वाद गवाम माता जानती गात | धन्वर्णसो नद्यः खादोर्णा सथूणेव सुमिता दरंहत दयौः ||
5.45.e: Sūrya hath spread his light as splendour: hither came the Cows' Mother, conscious, from the stable,  To streams that flow with biting waves to deserts; and heaven is stablished like a firm-set pillar.

5.45.d: अस्मा उक्थाय पर्वतस्य गर्भो महीनां जनुषे पूर्व्याय | वि पर्वतो जिहीत साधत दयौर आविवासन्तो दसयन्त भूम ||
5.45.e: This laud hath won the burden of the mountain. To aid the ancient birth of mighty waters  The mountain parted, Heaven performed his office. The worshippers were worn with constant serving.

5.45.d: सूक्तेभिर वो वचोभिर देवजुष्टैर इन्द्रा नव अग्नी अवसे हुवध्यै | उक्थेभिर हि षमा कवयः सुयज्ञा आविवासन्तो मरुतो यजन्ति ||
5.45.e: With hymns and God-loved words will I invoke you, Indra and Agni, to obtain your favour,  For verily sages, skilled in sacrificing, worship the Maruts and with lauds invite them.

5.45.d: एतो नव अद्य सुध्यो भवाम पर दुछुना मिनवामा वरीयः | आरे दवेषांसि सनुतर दधामायाम पराञ्चो यजमानम अछ ||
5.45.e: This day approach us: may our thoughts be holy, far from us let us cast away misfortune.  Let us keep those who hate us at a distance, and haste to meet the man who sacrifices.

5.45.d: एता धियं कर्णवामा सखायो ऽप या मातां रणुत वरजं गोः | यया मनुर विशिशिप्रं जिगाय यया वणिग वङकुर आपा पुरीषम ||
5.45.e: Come, let us carry out, O friends, the purpose wherewith the Mother threw the Cow's stall open,  That wherewith Manu conquered Visisipra, wherewith the wandering merchant gained heaven's water.

5.45.d: अनूनोद अत्र हस्तयतो अद्रिर आर्चन येन दश मासो नवग्वाः | रतं यती सरमा गा अविन्दद विश्वानि सत्याङगिराश चकार ||
5.45.e: Here, urged by hands, loudly hath rung the press-stone wherewith Navagvas through ten months sang praises.  Saramā went aright and found the cattle. Aṅgiras gave effect to all their labours.

5.45.d: विश्वे अस्या वयुषि माहिनायाः सं यद गोभिर अङगिरसो नवन्त | उत्स आसाम परमे सधस्थ रतस्य पथा सरमा विदद गाः ||
5.45.e: When at the dawning of this mighty Goddess, Aṅgirases all sang forth with the cattle,—  Their spring is in the loftiest place of meeting,—Saramā found the kine by Order's pathway.

5.45.d: आ सूर्यो यातु सप्ताश्वः कषेत्रं यद अस्योर्विया दीर्घयाथे | रघुः शयेनः पतयद अन्धो अछा युवा कविर दीदयद गोषु गछन ||
5.45.e: Borne by his Coursers Seven may Sūrya visit the field that spreadeth wide for his long journey.  Down on the Soma swooped the rapid Falcon. Bright was the young Sage moving mid his cattle.

5.45.d: आ सूर्यो अरुहच छुक्रम अर्णो ऽयुक्त यद धरितो वीतप्र्ष्ठाः | उद्ना न नावम अनयन्त धीरा आश्र्ण्वतीर आपो अर्वाग अतिष्ठन ||
5.45.e: Sūrya hath mounted to the shining ocean when he hath yoked his fair-backed Tawny Horses.  The wise have drawn him like a ship through water: the floods obedient have descended hither.

5.45.d: धियं वो अप्सु दधिषे सवर्षां ययातरन दश मासो नवग्वाः | अया धिया सयाम देवगोपा अया धिया तुतुर्यामात्य अंहः ||
5.45.e: I lay upon the Floods your hymn, lightwinning, wherewith Navagvas their ten months completed.  Through this our hymn may we have Gods to guard us: through this our hymn pass safe beyond affliction.

5.46.d: हयो न विद्वां अयुजि सवयं धुरि तां वहामि परतरणीम अवस्युवम | नास्या वश्मि विमुचं नाव्र्तम पुनर विद्वान पथः पुरेत रजु नेषति ||
