5.46.e: WELL knowing I have bound me, horselike, to the pole: I carry that which bears as on and gives us help.  I seek for no release, no turning back therefrom. May he who knows the way, the Leader, guide me straight.

5.46.d: अग्न इन्द्र वरुण मित्र देवाः शर्धः पर यन्त मारुतोत विष्णो | उभा नासत्या रुद्रो अध गनाः पूषा भगः सरस्वती जुषन्त ||
5.46.e: O Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, and Mitra, give, O ye Gods, and Marut host, and Viṣṇu.  May both Nāsatyas, Rudra, heavenly Matrons, Pūṣan, Sarasvatī, Bhaga, accept us.

5.46.d: इन्द्राग्नी मित्रावरुणादितिं सवः पर्थिवीं दयाम मरुतः पर्वतां अपः | हुवे विष्णुम पूषणम बरह्मणस पतिम भगं नु शंसं सवितारम ऊतये ||
5.46.e: Indra and Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the Waters, Mountains, Maruts, Sky, and Earth and Heaven,  Viṣṇu I call, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati, and Bhaga, Samsa, Savitar that they may help.

5.46.d: उत नो विष्णुर उत वातो अस्रिधो दरविणोदा उत सोमो मयस करत | उत रभव उत राये नो अश्विनोत तवष्टोत विभ्वानु मंसते ||
5.46.e: May Viṣṇu also and Vāta who injures none, and Soma granter of possessions give us joy;  And may the Ṛbhus and the Aśvins, Tvaṣṭar and Vibhvan remember us so that we may have wealth.

5.46.d: उत तयन नो मारुतं शर्ध आ गमद दिविक्षयं यजतम बर्हिर आसदे | बर्हस्पतिः शर्म पूषोत नो यमद वरूथ्यं वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा ||
5.46.e: So may the band of Maruts dwelling in the sky, the holy, come to us to sit on sacred grass;  Bṛhaspati and Pūṣan grant us sure defence, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman guard and shelter us.

5.46.d: उत तये नः पर्वतासः सुशस्तयः सुदीतयो नद्यस तरामणे भुवन | भगो विभक्ता शवसावसा गमद उरुव्यचा अदितिः शरोतु मे हवम ||
5.46.e: And may the Mountains famed in noble eulogies, and the fair-gleaming Rivers keep us safe from harm.  May Bhaga the Dispenser come with power and grace, and far-pervading Aditi listen to my call.

5.46.d: देवानाम पत्नीर उशतीर अवन्तु नः परावन्तु नस तुजये वाजसातये | याः पार्थिवासो या अपाम अपि वरते ता नो देवीः सुहवाः शर्म यछत ||
5.46.e: May the Gods’ Spouses aid us of their own freewill, aid us to offspring and the winning of the spoil.  Grant us protection, O ye gracious Goddesses, ye who are on the earth or in the waters' realm.

5.46.d: उत गना वयन्तु देवपत्नीर इन्द्राण्य अग्नाय्य अश्विनी राट | आ रोदसी वरुणानी शर्णोतु वयन्तु देवीर य रतुर जनीनाम ||
5.46.e: May the Dames, wives of Gods, enjoy our presents, Rat, Aśvini, Agnāyī, and Indrāṇī.  May Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us, and Goddesses come at the Matrons' season.

5.47.d: परयुञ्जती दिव एति बरुवाणा मही माता दुहितुर बोधयन्ती | आविवासन्ती युवतिर मनीषा पित्र्भ्य आ सदने जोहुवाना ||
5.47.e: URGING to toil and making proclamation, seeking Heaven's Daughter comes the Mighty Mother:  She comes, the youthful Hymn, unto the Fathers, inviting to her home and loudly calling.

5.47.d: अजिरासस तदप ईयमाना आतस्थिवांसो अम्र्तस्य नाभिम | अनन्तास उरवो विश्वतः सीम परि दयावाप्र्थिवी यन्ति पन्थाः ||
5.47.e: Swift in their motion, hasting to their duty, reaching the central point of life immortal,  On every side about the earth and heaven go forth the spacious paths without a limit.

5.47.d: उक्षा समुद्रो अरुषः सुपर्णः पूर्वस्य योनिम पितुर आ विवेश | मध्ये दिवो निहितः पर्श्निर अश्मा वि चक्रमे रजसस पात्य अन्तौ ||
5.47.e: Steer, Sea, Red Bird with strong wings, he hath entered the dwelling-place of the Primeval Father.  A gay-hued Stone set in the midst of heaven, he hath gone forth and guards mid-air's two limits.

5.47.d: चत्वार ईम बिभ्रति कषेमयन्तो दश गर्भं चरसे धापयन्ते | तरिधातवः परमा अस्य गावो दिवश चरन्ति परि सद्यो अन्तान ||
5.47.e: Four bear him up and give him rest and quiet, and ten invigorate the Babe for travel.  His kine most excellent, of threefold nature, pass swiftly round the boundaries of heaven.

5.47.d: इदं वपुर निवचनं जनासश चरन्ति यन नद्यस तस्थुर आपः | दवे यद ईम बिभ्र्तो मातुर अन्ये इहेह जाते यम्य्र सबन्धू ||
5.47.e: Wondrous, O people, is the mystic knowledge that while the waters stand the streams are flowing:  That, separate from his Mother, Two support him, closely-united, twins, here made apparent.

5.47.d: वि तन्वते धियो अस्मा अपांसि वस्त्रा पुत्राय मातरो वयन्ति | उपप्रक्षे वर्षणो मोदमाना दिवस पथा वध्वो यन्त्य अछ ||
5.47.e: For him they lenghten prayers and acts of worship: the Mothers weave garments for him their offspring.  Rejoicing, for the Steer's impregning contact, his Spouses move on paths or heaven to meet him.

5.47.d: तद अस्तु मित्रावरुणा तद अग्ने शं योर अस्मभ्यम इदम अस्तु शस्तम | अशीमहि गाधम उत परतिष्ठां नमो दिवे बर्हते सादनाय ||
5.47.e: Be this our praise, O Varuṇa and Mitra may this be health and force to us, O Agni.  May we obtain firm ground and room for resting: Glory to Heaven, the lofty habitation!

5.48.d: कद उ परियाय धाम्ने मनामहे सवक्षत्राय सवयशसे महे वयम | आमेन्यस्य रजसो यद अभ्र आं अपो वर्णाना वितनोति मायिनी ||
5.48.e: WHAT may we meditate for the beloved Power, mighty in native strength and glorious in itself,  Which as a magic energy seeking waters spreads even to theimmeasurable middle region's cloud?

5.48.d: ता अत्नत वयुनं वीरवक्षणं समान्या वर्तया विश्वम आ रजः | अपो अपाचीर अपरा अपेजते पर पूर्वाभिस तिरते देवयुर जनः ||
5.48.e: O'er all the region with their uniform advance these have spread out the lore that giveth heroes strength.  Back, with their course reversed, the others pass away: the pious lengthens life with those that are before.

5.48.d: आ गरावभिर अहन्येभिर अक्तुभिर वरिष्ठं वज्रम आ जिघर्ति मायिनि | शतं वा यस्य परचरन सवे दमे संवर्तयन्तो वि च वर्तयन्न अहा ||
5.48.e: With pressing-stones and with the bright beams of the day he hurls his broadest bolt against the Guileful One.  Even he whose hundred wander in his own abode, driving the days afar and bringing them again.

5.48.d: ताम अस्य रीतिम परशोर इव परत्य अनीकम अख्यम भुजे अस्य वर्पसः | सचा यदि पितुमन्तम इव कषयं रत्नं दधाति भरहूतये विशे ||
5.48.e: I, to enjoy the beauty of his form, behold that rapid rush of his as ’twere an axe's edge,  What time he gives the man who calls on him in fight wealth like a dwelling-house filled full with store of food.

5.48.d: स जिह्वया चतुरनीक रञ्जते चारु वसानो वरुणो यतन्न अरिम | न तस्य विद्म पुरुषत्वता वयं यतो भगः सविता दाति वार्यम ||
5.48.e: Four-faced and nobly clad, Varuṇa, urging on the pious to his task, stirs himself with the tongue.  Naught by our human nature do we know of him, him from whom Bhaga Savitar bestows the boon.

5.49.d: देवं वो अद्य सवितारम एषे भगं च रत्नं विभजन्तम आयोः | आ वां नरा पुरुभुजा वव्र्त्यां दिवे-दिवे चिद अश्विना सखीयन ||
5.49.e: THIS day I bring God Savitar to meet you, and Bhaga who allots the wealth of mortals.  You, Aśvins, Heroes rich in treasures, daily seeking your friendship fain would I turn hither.

5.49.d: परति परयाणम असुरस्य विद्वान सूक्तैर देवं सवितारं दुवस्य | उप बरुवीत नमसा विजानञ जयेष्ठं च रत्नं विभजन्तम आयोः ||
5.49.e: Knowing full well the Asura's time of coming, worship God Savitar with hymns and praises.  Let him who rightly knoweth speak with homage to him who dealeth out man's noblest treasure.

5.49.d: अदत्रया दयते वार्याणि पूषा भगो अदितिर वस्त उस्रः | इन्द्रो विष्णुर वरुणो मित्रो अग्निर अहानि भद्रा जनयन्त दस्माः ||
5.49.e: Not for reward doth Pūṣan send his blessings, Bhaga, or Aditi: his garb is splendour.  May Indra, Visniu, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni produce auspicious days, the Wonder-Workers.

5.49.d: तन नो अनर्वा सविता वरूथं तत सिन्धव इषयन्तो अनु गमन | उप यद वोचे अध्वरस्य होता रायः सयाम पतयो वाजरत्नाः ||
5.49.e: Sending the shelter which we ask, the foeless Savitar and the Rivers shall approach us.  When I, the sacrifice's priest, invite them, may we he lords of wealth and rich possessions.

5.49.d: पर ये वसुभ्य ईवद आ नमो दुर ये मित्रे वरुणे सूक्तवाचः | अवैत्व अभ्वं कर्णुता वरीयो दिवस्प्र्थिव्योर अवसा मदेम ||
5.49.e: They who devote such worship to the Vasus, singing their hymns to Varuṇa and Mitra,  Vouchsafe them ample room, far off be danger. Through grace of Heaven and Earth may we be happy.

5.50.d: विश्वो देवस्य नेतुर मर्तो वुरीत सख्यम | विश्वो राय इषुध्यति दयुम्नं वर्णीत पुष्यसे ||
5.50.e: LET every mortal man elect the friendship of the guiding God.  Each one solicits him for wealth and seeks renown to prosper him.

5.50.d: ते ते देव नेतर ये चेमां अनुशसे | ते राया ते हय रप्र्चे सचेमहि सचथ्यः ||
5.50.e: These, leading God, are thine, and these here ready to speak after us.  As such may we attain to wealth and wait with services on thee.

5.50.d: अतो न आ नञ्न अतिथीन अतः पत्नीर दशस्यत | आरे विश्वम पथेष्ठां दविषो युयोतु यूयुविः ||
5.50.e: So further honour as our guests the Hero Gods and then the Dames.  May he remove and keep afar our foes and all who block our path.

5.50.d: यत्र वह्निर अभिहितो दुद्रवद दरोण्यः पशुः | नर्मणा वीरपस्त्यो ऽरणा धीरेव सनिता ||
5.50.e: Where fire is set, and swiftly runs the victim dwelling in the trough,  He wins, with heroes in his home, friendly to man, like constant streams.

5.50.d: एष ते देव नेता रथस्पतिः शं रयिः | शं राये शं सवस्तय इषस्तुतो मनामहे देवस्तुतो मनामहे ||
5.50.e: May these thy riches, Leader God! that rule the car, be blest to us,  Yea, blest to us for wealth and weal. This will we ponder praising strength, this ponder as we praise the God.

5.51.d: अग्ने सुतस्य पीतये विश्वैर ऊमेभिर आ गहि | देवेभिर हव्यदातये ||
5.51.e: WITH all assistants, Agni, come hither to drink the Soma-juice;  With Gods unto our sacred gifts.

5.51.d: रतधीतय आ गत सत्यधर्माणो अध्वरम | अग्नेः पिबत जिह्वया ||
5.51.e: Come to the sacrifice, O ye whose ways are right, whose laws are true,  And drink the draught with Agni's tongue.

5.51.d: विप्रेभिर विप्र सन्त्य परातर्यावभिर आ गहि | देवेभिः सोमपीतये ||
5.51.e: O Singer, with the singers, O Gracious, with those who move at dawn,  Come to the Soma-draught with Gods.

5.51.d: अयं सोमश चमू सुतो ऽमत्रे परि षिच्यते | परिय इन्द्राय वायवे ||
5.51.e: To Indra and to Vāyu dear, this Soma, by the mortar pressed,  Is now poured forth to fill the jar.

5.51.d: वायव आ याहि वीतये जुषाणो हव्यदातये | पिबा सुतस्यान्धसो अभि परयः ||
5.51.e: Vāyu, come hither to the feast, wellpleased unto our sacred gifts:  Drink of the Soma juice effused come to the food.

5.51.d: इन्द्रश च वायव एषां सुतानाम पीतिम अर्हथः | ताञ जुषेथाम अरेपसाव अभि परयः ||
5.51.e: Ye, Indra, Vāyu, well deserve to drink the juices pressed by us.  Gladly accept them, spotless Pair come to the food.

5.51.d: सुता इन्द्राय वायवे सोमासो दध्याशिरः | निम्नं न यन्ति सिन्धवो ऽभि परयः ||
5.51.e: For Indra and for Vāyu pressed are Soma juices blent with curd,  As rivers to the lowland flow: come to the food.

5.51.d: सजूर विश्वेभिर देवेभिर अश्विभ्याम उषसा सजूः | आ याह्य अग्ने अत्रिवत सुते रण ||
5.51.e: Associate with all the Gods, come, with the Aśvins and with Dawn,  Agni, as erst with Atri, so enjoy the juice.

5.51.d: सजूर मित्रावरुणाभ्यां सजूः सोमेन विष्णुना | आ याह्य अग्ने अत्रिवत सुते रण ||
5.51.e: Associate with Varuṇa, with Mitra, Soma, Viṣṇu, come,  Agni, as erstwith Atri, so enjoy the juice.

5.51.d: सजूर आदित्यैर वसुभिः सजूर इन्द्रेण वायुना | आ याह्य अग्ने अत्रिवत सुते रण ||
5.51.e: Associate with Vasus, with Ādityas, Indra, Viyu, come, Agni as erst with Atri, so enjoy the juice.

5.51.d: सवस्ति नो मिमीताम अश्विना भगः सवस्ति देव्य अदितिर अनर्वणः | सवस्ति पूषा असुरो दधातु नः सवस्ति दयावाप्र्थिवी सुचेतुना ||
5.51.e: May Bhaga and the Aśvins grant us health and wealth, and Goddess Adid and he whom none resist.  The Asura Pūṣan grant us all prosperity, and Heaven and Earth most wise vouchsafe us happiness.

5.51.d: सवस्तये वायुम उप बरवामहै सोमं सवस्ति भुवनस्य यस पतिः | बर्हस्पतिं सर्वगणं सवस्तये सवस्तय आदित्यासो भवन्तु नः ||
5.51.e: Let us solicit Vāyu for prosperity, and Soma who is Lord of all the world for weal;  For weal Bṛhaspati with all his company. May the Ādityas bring us health and happiness.

5.51.d: विश्वे देवा नो अद्या सवस्तये वैश्वानरो वसुर अग्निः सवस्तये | देवा अवन्त्व रभवः सवस्तये सवस्ति नो रुद्रः पात्व अंहसः ||
5.51.e: May all the Gods, may Agni the beneficent, God of all men, this day be with us for our weal.  Help us the Ṛbhus, the Divine Ones, for our good. May Rudra bless and keep us from calamity.

5.51.d: सवस्ति मित्रावरुणा सवस्ति पथ्ये रेवति | सवस्ति न इन्द्रश चाग्निश च सवस्ति नो अदिते कर्धि ||
5.51.e: Prosper us, Mitra, Varuṇa. O wealthy Pathya, prosper us.  Indra and Agni, prosper us; prosper us thou, O Aditi.

5.51.d: सवस्ति पन्थाम अनु चरेम सूर्याचन्द्रमसाव इव | पुनर ददताघ्नता जानता सं गमेमहि ||
5.51.e: Like Sun and Moon may we pursue in full prosperity our path,  And meet with one who gives again, -who knows us well and slays us not.

5.52.d: पर शयावाश्व धर्ष्णुयार्चा मरुद्भिर रक्वभिः | ये अद्रोघम अनुष्वधं शरवो मदन्ति यज्ञियाः ||
5.52.e: SING boldly forth, Śyāvāśva, with the Maruts who are loud in song,  Who, holy, as their wont is, joy in glory that is free from guile.

5.52.d: ते हि सथिरस्य शवसः सखायः सन्ति धर्ष्णुया | ते यामन्न आ धर्षद्विनस तमना पान्ति शश्वतः ||
5.52.e: For in their boldness they are friends of firm and sure heroic strength.  They in their course, bold-spirited, guard all men of their own accord.

5.52.d: ते सयन्द्रासो नोक्षणो ऽति षकन्दन्ति शर्वरीः | मरुताम अधा महो दिवि कषमा च मन्महे ||
5.52.e: Like steers in rapid motion they advance and overtake the nights;  And thus the Maruts’ power in heaven and on the earth we celebrate.

5.52.d: मरुत्सु वो दधीमहि सतोमं यज्ञं च धर्ष्णुया | विश्वे ये मानुषा युगा पान्ति मर्त्यं रिषः ||
5.52.e: With boldness to your Maruts let us offer laud and sacrifice:  Who all, through ages of mankind, guard mortal man from injury.

5.52.d: अर्हन्तो ये सुदानवो नरो असामिशवसः | पर यज्ञं यज्ञियेभ्यो दिवो अर्चा मरुद्भ्यः ||
5.52.e: Praiseworthy, givers of good gifts, Heroes with full and perfect strength -  To Maruts, Holy Ones of heaven, will I extol the sacrifice.

5.52.d: आ रुक्मैर आ युधा नर रष्वा रष्टीर अस्र्क्षत | अन्व एनां अह विद्युतो मरुतो जज्झतीर इव भानुर अर्त तमना दिवः ||
5.52.e: The lofty Heroes cast their spears and weapons bright with gleaming gold.  After these Maruts followed close, like laughing lightning from the sky, a splendour of its own accord.

5.52.d: ये वाव्र्धन्त पार्थिवा य उराव अन्तरिक्ष आ | वर्जने वा नदीनां सधस्थे वा महो दिवः ||
5.52.e: They who waxed mighty, of the earth, they who are in the wide mid-air,  Or in the rivers’ compass, or in the abode of ample heaven.

5.52.d: शर्धो मारुतम उच छंस सत्यशवसम रभ्वसम | उत सम ते शुभे नरः पर सयन्द्रा युजत तमना ||
5.52.e: Praise thou the Maruts’ company, the valorous and truly strong,  The Heroes, hasting, by themselves have yoked their deer for victory.

5.52.d: उत सम ते परुष्ण्याम ऊर्णा वसत शुन्ध्यवः | उत पव्या रथानाम अद्रिम भिन्दन्त्य ओजसा ||
5.52.e: Fair-gleaming, on Paruṣṇī they have clothed themselves in robes of wool,  And with their chariot tires they cleave the rock asunder in their might.

5.52.d: आपथयो विपथयो ऽनतस्पथा अनुपथाः | एतेभिर मह्यं नामभिर यज्ञं विष्टार ओहते ||
5.52.e: Whether as wanderers from the way or speeders on or to the path,  Under these names the spreading band tend well the sacrifice for me.

5.52.d: अधा नरो नय ओहते ऽधा नियुत ओहते | अधा पारावता इति चित्रा रूपाणि दर्श्या ||
5.52.e: To this the Heroes well attend, well do their teams attend to this.  Visible are their varied forms. Behold, they are Paravatas.

5.52.d: छन्दस्तुभः कुभन्यव उत्सम आ कीरिणो नर्तुः | ते मे के चिन न तायव ऊमा आसन दर्शि तविषे ||
5.52.e: Hymn-singing, seeking water, they, praising, have danced about the spring.  What are they unto me? No thieves, but helpers, splendid to behold.

5.52.d: य रष्वा रष्टिविद्युतः कवयः सन्ति वेधसः | तम रषे मारुतं गणं नमस्या रमया गिरा ||
5.52.e: Sublime, with lightnings for their spears, Sages and Orderers are they.  Ṛṣi, adore that Marut host, and make them happy with thy song.

5.52.d: अछ रषे मारुतं गणं दाना मित्रं न योषणा | दिवो वा धर्ष्णव ओजसा सतुता धीभिर इषण्यत ||
5.52.e: Ṛṣi, invite the Marut band with offerings, as a maid her friend.  From heaven, too, Bold Ones, in your might haste hither glorified with songs.

5.52.d: नू मन्वान एषां देवां अछा न वक्षणा | दाना सचेत सूरिभिर यामश्रुतेभिर अञ्जिभिः ||
5.52.e: Thinking of these now let him come, as with the escort of the Gods,  And with the splendid Princes, famed for rapid courses, to the gifts.

5.52.d: पर ये मे बन्ध्वेषे गां वोचन्त सूरयः पर्श्निं वोचन्त मातरम | अधा पितरम इष्मिणं रुद्रं वोचन्त शिक्वसः ||
5.52.e: Princes, who, when I asked their kin, named Pṛśni as their Mother-cow,  And the impetuous Rudra they, the Mighty Ones, declared their Sire.

5.52.d: सप्त मे सप्त शाकिन एकम-एका शता ददुः | यमुनायाम अधि शरुतम उद राधो गव्यम मर्जे नि राधो अश्व्यम मर्जे ||
5.52.e: The mighty ones, the seven times seven, have singly given me hundred gifts.  I have obtained on Yamuna famed wealth in kine and wealth in steeds.

5.53.d: को वेद जानम एषां को वा पुरा सुम्नेष्व आस मरुताम | यद युयुज्रे किलास्यः ||
5.53.e: Who knows the birth of these, or who lived in the Maruts’ favour in the days of old  What time their spotted deer were yoked?

5.53.d: ऐतान रथेषु तस्थुषः कः शुश्राव कथा ययुः | कस्मै सस्रुः सुदासे अन्व आपय इळाभिर वर्ष्टयः सह ||
5.53.e: Who, when they stood upon their cars, hath heard them tell the way they went?  Who was the bounteous man to whom their kindred rains flowed down with food of sacrifice?

5.53.d: ते म आहुर य आययुर उप दयुभिर विभिर मदे | नरो मर्या अरेपस इमान पश्यन्न इति षटुहि ||
5.53.e: To me they told it, and they came with winged steeds radiant to the draught,  Youths, Heroes free from spot or stain: Behold us here and praise thou us;

5.53.d: ये अञ्जिषु ये वाशीषु सवभानवः सरक्षु रुक्मेषु खादिषु | शराया रथेषु धन्वसु ||
5.53.e: Who shine self-luminous with ornaments and swords, with breastplates, armlets, and with wreaths,  Arrayed on chariots and with bows.

5.53.d: युष्माकं समा रथां अनु मुदे दधे मरुतो जीरदानवः | वर्ष्टी दयावो यतीर इव ||
5.53.e: O swift to pour your bounties down, ye Maruts, with delight I look upon your cars,  Like splendours coming through the rain.

5.53.d: आ यं नरः सुदानवो ददाशुषे दिवः कोशम अचुच्यवुः | वि पर्जन्यं सर्जन्ति रोदसी अनु धन्वना यन्ति वर्ष्टयः ||
5.53.e: Munificent Heroes, they have cast heaven's treasury down for the worshipper's behoof:  They set the storm-cloud free to stream through both the worlds, and rainfloods flow o’er desert spots.

5.53.d: तत्र्दानाः सिन्धवः कषोदसा रजः पर सस्रुर धेनवो यथा | सयन्ना अश्वा इवाध्वनो विमोचने वि यद वर्तन्त एन्यः ||
5.53.e: The bursting streams m billowy flood have spread abroad, like milch-kine, o’er the firmament.  Like swift steeds hasting to their journey's resting-place, to every side run glittering brooks.

5.53.d: आ यात मरुतो दिव आन्तरिक्षाद अमाद उत | माव सथात परावतः ||
5.53.e: Hither, O Maruts, come from heaven, from mid-air, or from near at hand  Tarry not far away from us.

5.53.d: मा वो रसानितभा कुभा करुमुर मा वः सिन्धुर नि रीरमत | मा वः परि षठात सरयुः पुरीषिण्य अस्मे ईत सुम्नम अस्तु वः ||
5.53.e: So let not Rasā, Krumu, or Anitabha, Kubha, or Sindhu hold you back.  Let not the watery Sarayti obstruct your way. With us be all the bliss ye give.

5.53.d: तं वः शर्धं रथानां तवेषं गणम मारुतं नव्यसीनाम | अनु पर यन्ति वर्ष्टयः ||
5.53.e: That brilliant gathering of your cars, the company of Maruts, of the Youthful Ones,  The rain-showers, speeding on, attend.

5.53.d: शर्धं-शर्धं व एषां वरातं-वरातं गणं-गणं सुशस्तिभिः | अनु करामेम धीतिभिः ||
5.53.e: With eulogies and hymns may we follow your army, troop by troop, and band by band,  And company by company.

5.53.d: कस्मा अद्य सुजाताय रातहव्याय पर ययुः | एना यामेन मरुतः ||
5.53.e: To what oblation-giver, sprung of noble ancestry, have sped  The Maruts on this course to-day?

5.53.d: येन तोकाय तनयाय धान्यम बीजं वहध्वे अक्षितम | अस्मभ्यं तद धत्तन यद व ईमहे राधो विश्वायु सौभगम ||
5.53.e: Vouchsafe to us the bounty, that which we implore, through which, for child and progeny,  Ye give the seed of corn that wasteth not away, and bliss that reacheth to all life.

5.53.d: अतीयाम निदस तिरः सवस्तिभिर हित्वावद्यम अरातीः | वर्ष्ट्वी शं योर आप उस्रि भेषजं सयाम मरुतः सह ||
5.53.e: May we in safety pass by those who slander us, leaving behind disgrace and hate.  Maruts, may we be there when ye, at dawn, in rest and toil, rain waters down and balm.

5.53.d: सुदेवः समहासति सुवीरो नरो मरुतः स मर्त्यः | यं तरायध्वे सयाम ते ||
5.53.e: Favoured by Gods shall he the man, O Heroes, Marutr! and possessed of noble sons,  Whom ye protect. Such may we be.

5.53.d: सतुहि भोजान सतुवतो अस्य यामनि रणन गावो न यवसे | यतः पूर्वां इव सखींर अनु हवय गिरा गर्णीहि कामिनः ||
5.53.e: Praise the Free-givers. At this liberal patron's rite they joy like cattle in the mead.  So call thou unto them who come as ancient Friends: hymn those who love thee with a song.

5.54.d: पर शर्धाय मारुताय सवभानव इमां वाचम अनजा पर्वतच्युते | घर्मस्तुभे दिव आ पर्ष्ठयज्वने दयुम्नश्रवसे महि नर्म्णम अर्चत ||
5.54.e: THIS hymn will I make for the Marut host who bright in native splendour cast the mountains down.  Sing the great strength of those illustrious in renown, who stay the heat, who sacrifice on heights of heaven.

5.54.d: पर वो मरुतस तविषा उदन्यवो वयोव्र्धो अश्वयुजः परिज्रयः | सं विद्युता दधति वाशति तरितः सवरन्त्य आपो ऽवना परिज्रयः ||
5.54.e: O Maruts, rich in water, strengtheners of life are your strong bands with harnessed steeds, that wander far.  Trita roars out at him who aims the lightning-flash. The waters sweeping round are thundering on their way.

5.54.d: विद्युन्महसो नरो अश्मदिद्यवो वातत्विषो मरुतः पर्वतच्युतः | अब्दया चिन मुहुर आ हरादुनीव्र्त सतनयदमा रभसा उदोजसः ||
5.54.e: They gleam with lightning, Heroes, Casters of the Stone, wind-rapid Maruts, overthrowers of the bills,  Oft through desire to rain coming with storm of hail, roaring in onset, violent and exceeding strong.

5.54.d: वय अक्तून रुद्रा वय अहानि शिक्वसो वय अन्तरिक्षं वि रजांसि धूतयः | वि यद अज्रां अजथ नाव ईं यथा वि दुर्गाणि मरुतो नाह रिष्यथ ||
5.54.e: When, mighty Rudras, through the nights and through the days, when through the sky and realms of air, shakers of all,  When over the broad fields ye drive along like ships, e’en to strongholds ye come, Maruts, but are not harmed.

5.54.d: तद वीर्यं वो मरुतो महित्वनं दीर्घं ततान सूर्यो न योजनम | एता न यामे अग्र्भीतशोचिषो ऽनश्वदां यन नय अयातना गिरिम ||
5.54.e: Maruts, this hero strength and majesty of yours hath, like the Sun, extended o’er a lengthened way,  When in your course like deer with splendour unsubdued ye bowed the hill that gives imperishable rain.

5.54.d: अभ्राजि शर्धो मरुतो यद अर्णसम मोषथा वर्क्षं कपनेव वेधसः | अध समा नो अरमतिं सजोषसश चक्षुर इव यन्तम अनु नेषथा सुगम ||
5.54.e: Bright shone your host, ye Sages, Maruts, when ye smote the waving tree as when the worm consumeth it.  Accordant, as the eye guides him who walks, have ye led our devotion onward by an easy path.

5.54.d: न स जीयते मरुतो न हन्यते न सरेधति न वयथते न रिष्यति | नास्य राय उप दस्यन्ति नोतय रषिं वा यं राजानं वा सुषूदथ ||
5.54.e: Never is he, O Maruts, slain or overcome, never doth he decay ne’er is distressed or harmed;  His treasures, his resources, never waste away, whom. whether he be prince or Ṛṣi, ye direct.

5.54.d: नियुत्वन्तो गरामजितो यथा नरो ऽरयमणो न मरुतः कबन्धिनः | पिन्वन्त्य उत्सं यद इनासो अस्वरन वय उन्दन्ति पर्थिवीम मध्वो अन्धसा ||
5.54.e: With harnessed team like heroes overcoming troops, the friendly Maruts, laden with their water-casks,  Let the spring flow, and when impetuous' they roar they inundate the earth with floods of pleasant meath.

5.54.d: परवत्वतीयम पर्थिवी मरुद्भ्यः परवत्वती दयौर भवति परयद्भ्यः | परवत्वतीः पथ्य्र अन्तरिक्ष्याः परवत्वन्तः पर्वता जीरदानवः ||
5.54.e: Free for the Maruts is the earth with sloping ways, free for the rushing Ones is heaven with steep descents.  The paths of air's mid-region are precipitous, precipitous the mountains with their running streams.

5.54.d: यन मरुतः सभरसः सवर्णरः सूर्य उदिते मदथा दिवो नरः | न वो ऽशवाः शरथयन्ताह सिस्रतः सद्यो अस्याध्वनः पारम अश्नुथ ||
5.54.e: When, as the Sun hath risen up, ye take delight, O bounteous radiant Maruts, Heroes of the sky,  Your coursers weary not when speeding onṭheir way, and rapidly ye reach the end of this your path.

5.54.d: अंसेषु व रष्टयः पत्सु खादयो वक्षस्सु रुक्मा मरुतो रथे शुभः | अग्निभ्राजसो विद्युतो गभस्त्योः शिप्राः शीर्षसु वितता हिरण्ययीः ||
5.54.e: Lances are on your shoulders, anklets on your feet, gold chains are on your breasts, gems, Maruts, on your car.  Lightnings aglow with flame are flashing in your hands, and visors wroughtof gold are laid upon your heads.

5.54.d: तं नाकम अर्यो अग्र्भीतशोचिषं रुशत पिप्पलम मरुतो वि धूनुथ | सम अच्यन्त वर्जनातित्विषन्त यत सवरन्ति घोषं विततम रतायवः ||
5.54.e: Maruts, in eager stir ye shake the vault of heaven, splendid beyond conception, for its shining fruit.  They gathered when they let their deeds of might flash forth. The Pious Ones send forth a far-resounding shout.

5.54.d: युष्मादत्तस्य मरुतो विचेतसो रायः सयाम रथ्यो वयस्वतः | न यो युछति तिष्यो यथा दिवो ऽसमे रारन्त मरुतः सहस्रिणम ||
5.54.e: Sage Maruts, may we be the drivers of the car of riches ful I of life that have been given by you.  O Maruts, let that wealth in thousands dwell with us which never vanishes like Tisya from the sky.

5.54.d: यूयं रयिम मरुत सपार्हवीरं यूयम रषिम अवथ सामविप्रम | यूयम अर्वन्तम भरताय वाजं यूयं धत्थ राजानं शरुष्टिमन्तम ||
5.54.e: Maruts, ye further wealth with longedfor heroes, further the Ṛṣi skilled in chanted verses.  Ye give the Bhārata as his strength, a charger, and ye bestow a king who quickly listens.

5.54.d: तद वो यामि दरविणं सद्यूतयो येना सवर ण ततनाम नॄंर अभि | इदं सु मे मरुतो हर्यता वचो यस्य तरेम तरसा शतं हिमाः ||
5.54.e: Of you, most swift to succour! I solicit wealth wherewith we may spread forth mid men like as the Sun.  Accept, O Maruts, graciously this hymn of mine that we may live a hundred winters through its power.

5.55.d: परयज्यवो मरुतो भराजद्र्ष्टयो बर्हद वयो दधिरे रुक्मवक्षसः | ईयन्ते अश्वैः सुयमेभिर आशुभिः शुभं याताम अनु रथा अव्र्त्सत ||
5.55.e: WITH gleaming lances, with their breasts adorned with gold, the Maruts, rushing onward, hold high power of life.  They hasten with swift steeds easy to be controlled. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: सवयं दधिध्वे तविषीं यथा विद बर्हन महान्त उर्विया वि राजथ | उतान्तरिक्षम ममिरे वय ओजसा शुभं याताम अनु रथा अव्र्त्सत ||
5.55.e: Ye, as ye wist, have gained of your own selves your power: high, O ye Mighty Ones, and wide ye shine abroad.  They with their strength have even measured out the sky.  Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: साकं जाताः सुभ्वः साकम उक्षिताः शरिये चिद आ परतरं वाव्र्धुर नरः | विरोकिणः सूर्यस्येव रश्मयः शुभं याताम अनु रथा अव्र्त्सत ||
5.55.e: Strong, born together, they together have waxed great: the Heroes more and more have grown to majesty  Resplendent as the Sun's beams in their light are they. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: आभूषेण्यं वो मरुतो महित्वनं दिद्र्क्षेण्यं सूर्यस्येव चक्षणम | उतो अस्मां अम्र्तत्वे दधातन शुभं याताम अनु रथा अव्र्त्सत ||
5.55.e: Maruts, your mightiness deserves to be adored, sight to be longed for like the shining of the Sun.  So lead us with your aid to immortality.  Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: उद ईरयथा मरुतः समुद्रतो यूयं वर्ष्टिं वर्षयथा पुरीषिणः | न वो दस्रा उप दस्यन्ति धेनवः शुभं याताम अनु रथा अव्र्त्सत ||
5.55.e: O Maruts, from the Ocean ye uplift the rain, and fraught with vaporous moisture pour the torrents down.  Never, ye Wonder-Workers, are your Milch-kine dry. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: यद अश्वान धूर्षु पर्षतीर अयुग्ध्वं हिरण्ययान परत्य अत्कां अमुग्ध्वम | विश्वा इत सप्र्धो मरुतो वय अस्यथ शुभं याताम अनु रथा अव्र्त्सत ||
5.55.e: When to your car-poles ye have yoked your spotted deer to be your steeds, and put your golden mantles on,  O Maruts, ye disperse all enemies abroad. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: न पर्वता न नद्यो वरन्त वो यत्राचिध्वम मरुतो गछथेद उ तत | उत दयावाप्र्थिवी याथना परि शुभं याताम अनु रथा अव्र्त्सत ||
5.55.e: Neither the mountains nor the rivers keep you back: whither ye have resolved thither ye, Maruts, go.  Ye compass round about even the heaven and earth. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.  Whate’er is ancient, Maruts, what of recent time, whate’er is spoken, Vasus, what is chanted forth,  They who take cognizance of all of this are ye. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: यत पूर्व्यम मरुतो यच च नूतनं यद उद्यते वसवो यच च शस्यते | विश्वस्य तस्य भवथा नवेदसः शुभं याताम अनु रथा अव्र्त्सत ||
5.55.e: Be gracious unto us, ye Maruts, slay us not extend ye unto us shelter of many a sort.  Pay due regard unto our friendship and our praise. Their cars moved onward as they went to victory.

5.55.d: मर्ळत नो मरुतो मा वधिष्टनास्मभ्यं शर्म बहुलं वि यन्तन | अधि सतोत्रस्य सख्यस्य गातन शुभं याताम अनु रथा अव्र्त्सत ||
5.55.e: O Maruts, lead us on to higher fortune deliver us, when lauded, from afflictions.  Accept, ye Holy Ones, the gifts we bring you. May we be masters of abundant riches.

5.55.d: यूयम अस्मान नयत वस्यो अछा निर अंहतिभ्यो मरुतो गर्णानाः | जुषध्वं नो हव्यदातिं यजत्रा वयं सयाम पतयो रयीणाम ||

5.56.d: अग्ने शर्धन्तम आ गणम पिष्टं रुक्मेभिर अञ्जिभिः | विशो अद्य मरुताम अव हवये दिवश चिद रोचनाद अधि ||
5.56.e: AGNI, that valorous company adorned with ornaments of gold,  The people of the Maruts, I call down to-day even from the luminous realm of heaven.

5.56.d: यथा चिन मन्यसे हर्दा तद इन मे जग्मुर आशसः | ये ते नेदिष्ठं हवनान्य आगमन तान वर्ध भीमसंद्र्शः ||
5.56.e: Even as thou thinkest in thy heart, thither my wishes also tend.  Those who have come most near to thine invoking calls, strengthen them fearful to behold.

5.56.d: मीळ्हुष्मतीव पर्थिवी पराहता मदन्त्य एत्य अस्मद आ | रक्षो न वो मरुतः शिमीवां अमो दुध्रो गौर इव भीमयुः ||
5.56.e: Earth, like a bounteous lady, liberal of her gifts, struck down and shaken, yet exultant, comes to us.  Impetuous as a bear, O Maruts, is youi rush terrible as a dreadful bull..

5.56.d: नि ये रिणन्त्य ओजसा वर्था गावो न दुर्धुरः | अश्मानं चित सवर्यम पर्वतं गिरिम पर चयावयन्ति यामभिः ||
5.56.e: They who with mighty strength o’erthrow like oxen difficult to yoke,  Cause e’en the heavenly stone to shake ' yea, shake the rocky mountain as they race along.

5.56.d: उत तिष्ठ नूनम एषां सतोमैः समुक्षितानाम | मरुताम पुरुतमम अपूर्व्यं गवां सर्गम इव हवये ||
5.56.e: Rise up! even now with lauds I call the very numerous company,  Unequalled, of these Maruts, like a herd of kine, grown up together in their strength.

5.56.d: युङगध्वं हय अरुषी रथे युङगध्वं रथेषु रोहितः | युङगध्वं हरी अजिरा धुरि वोळ्हवे वहिष्ठा धुरि वोळ्हवे ||
5.56.e: Bind to your car the bright red mares, yoke the red coursers to your car.  Bind to the pole, to draw, the fleet-foot tawny steeds, the best at drawing, to the pole.

5.56.d: उत सय वाज्य अरुषस तुविष्वणिर इह सम धायि दर्शतः | मा वो यामेषु मरुतश चिरं करत पर तं रथेषु चोदत ||
5.56.e: Yea, and this loudly-neighing bright red vigorous horse who hath been sutioned, fair to see,  Let him not cause delay, O Maruts,, in your course, urge ye him onward in your cars.

5.56.d: रथं नु मारुतं वयं शरवस्युम आ हुवामहे | आ यस्मिन तस्थौ सुरणानि बिभ्रती सचा मरुत्सु रोदसी ||
5.56.e: The Maruts’ chariot, ever fain to gather glory, we invoke,  Which Rodasī hath mounted, bringing pleasant gifts, with Maruts in her company.

5.56.d: तं वः शर्धं रथेशुभं तवेषम पनस्युम आ हुवे | यस्मिन सुजाता सुभगा महीयते सचा मरुत्सु मीळ्हुषी ||
5.56.e: I call that brilliant band of yours, adorable, rapid on the car  Whereon the bounteous Dame, auspicious, nobly born, shows glorious with the Marut host.

5.57.d: आ रुद्रास इन्द्रवन्तः सजोषसो हिरण्यरथाः सुविताय गन्तन | इयं वो अस्मत परति हर्यते मतिस तर्ष्णजे न दिव उत्सा उदन्यवे ||
5.57.e: OF one accord, with Indra, O ye Rudras, come borne on your golden car for our prosperity.  An offering from us, this hymn is brought to you, as, unto one who th irsts for water, heavenly springs.

5.57.d: वाशीमन्त रष्टिमन्तो मनीषिणः सुधन्वान इषुमन्तो निषङगिणः | सवश्वा सथ सुरथाः पर्श्निमातरः सवायुधा मरुतो याथना शुभम ||
5.57.e: Armed with your daggers, full of wisdom, armed with spears, armed with your quivers, armed with arrows, with good bows,  Good horses and good cars have ye, O Pṛśni's Sons: ye, Maruts, with good weapons go to victory.

5.57.d: धूनुथ दयाम पर्वतान दाशुषे वसु नि वो वना जिहते यामनो भिया | कोपयथ पर्थिवीम पर्श्निमातरः शुभे यद उग्राः पर्षतीर अयुग्ध्वम ||
5.57.e: From hills and heaven ye shake wealth for the worshipper: in terror at your coming low the woods bow down.  Ye make the earth to tremble, Sons of Pṛśni, when for victory ye have yoked, fierce Ones! your spotted deer.

5.57.d: वातत्विषो मरुतो वर्षनिर्णिजो यमा इव सुसद्र्शः सुपेशसः | पिशङगाश्वा अरुणाश्वा अरेपसः परत्वक्षसो महिना दयौर इवोरवः ||
5.57.e: Bright with the blasts of wind, wrapped in their robes of rain, like twins of noble aspect and of lovely form,  The Maruts, spotless, with steeds tawnyhued and red, strong in their mightiness and spreading wide like heaven.

5.57.d: पुरुद्रप्सा अञ्जिमन्तः सुदानवस तवेषसंद्र्शो अनवभ्रराधसः | सुजातासो जनुषा रुक्मवक्षसो दिवो अर्का अम्र्तं नाम भेजिरे ||
5.57.e: Rich in adornment, rich in drops, munificent, bright in their aspect, yielding bounties that endure,  Noble by birth, adorned with gold upon their breasts, the Singers of the sky have won immortal fame.

5.57.d: रष्टयो वो मरुतो अंसयोर अधि सह ओजो बाह्वोर वो बलं हितम | नर्म्णा शीर्षस्व आयुधा रथेषु वो विश्वा वः शरीर अधि तनूषु पिपिशे ||
5.57.e: Borne on both shoulders, O ye Maruts, are your spears: within your arms is laid your energy and 3trength.  Bold thoughts are in your heads, your weapons in your cars, all glorious majesty is moulded on your forms.

5.57.d: गोमद अश्वावद रथवत सुवीरं चन्द्रवद राधो मरुतो ददा नः | परशस्तिं नः कर्णुत रुद्रियासो भक्षीय वो ऽवसो दैव्यस्य ||
5.57.e: Vouchsafe to us, O Maruts, splendid bounty in cattle and in steeds, in cars and heroes.  Children of Rudra, give us high distinction: may I enjoy your Godlike help and favour.

5.57.d: हये नरो मरुतो मर्ळता नस तुवीमघासो अम्र्ता रतज्ञाः | सत्यश्रुतः कवयो युवानो बर्हद्गिरयो बर्हद उक्षमाणाः ||
5.57.e: Ho! Maruts, Heroes, skilled in Law, immortal, be gracious unto us, ye rich in treasures,  Ye hearers of the truth, ye sage and youthful, grown mighty, dwelling on the lofty mountains.

5.58.d: तम उ नूनं तविषीमन्तम एषां सतुषे गणम मारुतं नव्यसीनाम | य आश्वश्वा अमवद वहन्त उतेशिरे अम्र्तस्य सवराजः ||
5.58.e: Now do I glorify their mighty cohort, the company of these the youthful Maruts,  Who ride impetuous on with rapid horses, and radiant in themselves, are Lords of Amṛta.

5.58.d: तवेषं गणं तवसं खादिहस्तं धुनिव्रतम मायिनं दातिवारम | मयोभुवो ये अमिता महित्वा वन्दस्व विप्र तुविराधसो नॄन ||
5.58.e: The mighty glittering band, arm-bound with bracelets, givers of bliss, unmeasured in their greatness,  With magical powers, bountiful, ever-roaring,—these, liberal Heroes, venerate thou singer.

5.58.d: आ वो यन्तूदवाहासो अद्य वर्ष्टिं ये विश्वे मरुतो जुनन्ति | अयं यो अग्निर मरुतः समिद्ध एतं जुषध्वं कवयो युवानः ||
5.58.e: This day may all your water-bringers, Maruts, they who impel the falling rain, approach us.  This fire, O Maruts, hath been duly kindled; let it find favour with you, youthful Sages.

5.58.d: यूयं राजानम इर्यं जनाय विभ्वतष्टं जनयथा यजत्राः | युष्मद एति मुष्टिहा बाहुजूतो युष्मद सदश्वो मरुतः सुवीरः ||
5.58.e: Ye raise up for the folk an active ruler whom, Holy Ones! a Master's hand hath fashioned.  Ye send the fighter hand to hand, armmighty, and the brave hero, Maruts with good horses.

5.58.d: अरा इवेद अचरमा अहेव पर-पर जायन्ते अकवा महोभिः | पर्श्नेः पुत्रा उपमासो रभिष्ठाः सवया मत्या मरुतः सम मिमिक्षुः ||
5.58.e: They spring forth more and more, strong in their glories, like days, like spokes where none are last in order.  Highest and mightiest are the Sons of Pṛśni. Firm to their own intention cling the Maruts.

5.58.d: यत परायासिष्ट पर्षतीभिर अश्वैर वीळुपविभिर मरुतो रथेभिः | कषोदन्त आपो रिणते वनान्य अवोस्रियो वर्षभः करन्दतु दयौः ||
5.58.e: When ye have hastened on with spotted coursers, O Maruts, on your cars with strong-wrought fellies,  The waters are disturbed, the woods are shattered. Let Dyaus the Red Steer send his thunder downward.

5.58.d: परथिष्ट यामन पर्थिवी चिद एषाम भर्तेव गर्भं सवम इच छवो धुः | वातान हय अश्वान धुर्य रयुयुज्रे वर्षं सवेदं चक्रिरे रुद्रियासः ||
5.58.e: Even Earth hath spread herself wide at their coming, and they as husbands have with power impregned her.  They to the pole have yoked the winds for coursers: their sweat have they made rain, these Sons of Rudra.

5.58.d: हये नरो मरुतो मर्ळता नस तुवीमघासो अम्र्ता रतज्ञाः | सत्यश्रुतः कवयो युवानो बर्हद्गिरयो बर्हद उक्षमाणाः ||
5.58.e: Ho! Maruts, Heroes, skilled in Law, immortal, be gracious unto us, ye rich in treasures,  Ye hearers of the truth, ye sage and youthful, grown mighty, dwelling on the lofty mountains.

5.59.d: पर व सपळ अक्रन सुविताय दावने ऽरचा दिवे पर पर्थिव्या रतम भरे | उक्षन्ते अश्वान तरुषन्त आ रजो ऽनु सवम भानुं शरथयन्ते अर्णवैः ||
5.59.e: YOUR spy hath called to you to give prosperity. I sing to Heaven and Earth and offer sacrifice.  They bathe their steeds and hasten through the firmament: they spread abroad their radiance through the sea of cloud.

5.59.d: अमाद एषाम भियसा भूमिर एजति नौर न पूर्णा कषरति वयथिर यती | दूरेद्र्शो ये चितयन्त एमभिर अन्तर महे विदथे येतिरे नरः ||
5.59.e: Earth shakes and reels in terror at their onward rush, like a full ship which, quivering, lets the water in.  Marked on their ways are they, visible from afar: the Heroes press between in mighty armament.

5.59.d: गवाम इव शरियसे शर्ङगम उत्तमं सूर्यो न चक्षू रजसो विसर्जने | अत्या इव सुभ्वश चारव सथन मर्या इव शरियसे चेतथा नरः ||
5.59.e: As the exalted horn of bulls for splendid might, as the Sun's eye set in the firmament's expanse,  Like vigorous horses ye are beauteous to behold, and for your glory show like bridegrooms, O ye Men.

5.59.d: को वो महान्ति महताम उद अश्नवत कस काव्या मरुतः को ह पौंस्या | यूयं ह भूमिं किरणं न रेजथ पर यद भरध्वे सुविताय दावने ||
5.59.e: Who, O ye Maruts, may attain the mighty lore of you the mighty, who may reach your manly deeds?  Ye, verily, make earth tremble like a ray of light what time ye bring your boons to give prosperity,

5.59.d: अश्वा इवेद अरुषासः सबन्धवः शूरा इव परयुधः परोत युयुधुः | मर्या इव सुव्र्धो वाव्र्धुर नरः सूर्यस्य चक्षुः पर मिनन्ति वर्ष्टिभिः ||
5.59.e: Like steeds of ruddy colour, scions of one race, as foremost champions they have battled in the van.  The Heroes have waxed strong like we.1grown manly youths; with floods of rain they make the Sun's eye fade away,

5.59.d: ते अज्येष्ठा अकनिष्ठास उद्भिदो ऽमध्यमासो महसा वि वाव्र्धुः | सुजातासो जनुषा पर्श्निमातरो दिवो मर्या आ नो अछा जिगातन ||
5.59.e: Having no eldest and no youngest in their band, no middlomost, preeminent they have waxed in might,  These Sons of Pṛśni, sprung of noble ancestry: come hitberward to us, ye bridegrooms of the sky.

5.59.d: वयो न ये शरेणीः पप्तुर ओजसान्तान दिवो बर्हतः सानुनस परि | अश्वास एषाम उभये यथा विदुः पर पर्वतस्य नभनूंर अचुच्यवुः ||
5.59.e: Like birds of air they flew with might in lengthened lines from heaven's high ridges to the borders of the sky.  The steeds who carry them, as Gods and mortals know, have caused the waters of the mounuains to desGend.

5.59.d: मिमातु दयौर अदितिर वीतये नः सं दानुचित्रा उषसो यतन्ताम | आचुच्यवुर दिव्यं कोशम एत रषे रुद्रस्य मरुतो गर्णानाः ||
5.59.e: May Dyaus, the Infinite, roar for our banquet: may Dawns toil for us, glittering with moisture.  Lauded by thee, these Maruts, Sons o Rudra, O Ṛṣi, have sent down the heavenly treasure.

5.60.d: ईळे अग्निं सववसं नमोभिर इह परसत्तो वि चयत कर्तं नः | रथैर इव पर भरे वाजयद्भिः परदक्षिणिन मरुतां सतोमम रध्याम ||
5.60.e: I LAUD with reverence the gracious Agni: here may he sit and part our meed among us.  As with spoil-seeking cars I bring oblation: turned rightward I will swell the Marut's, praise-song.

5.60.d: आ ये तस्थुः पर्षतीषु शरुतासु सुखेषु रुद्रा मरुतो रथेषु | वना चिद उग्रा जिहते नि वो भिया पर्थिवी चिद रेजते पर्वतश चित ||
5.60.e: The Maruts, yea, the Rudras, who have mounted their famous spotted deer and cars swift-moving,—  Before you, fierce Ones! woods bow down in terror: Earth, even the mountain, trembles at your coming.

5.60.d: पर्वतश चिन महि वर्द्धो बिभाय दिवश चित सानु रेजत सवने वः | यत करीळथ मरुत रष्टिमन्त आप इव सध्र्यञ्चो धवध्वे ||
5.60.e: Though vast and tall, the mountain is affrighted, the height of heaven is shaken at your roaring  When, armed with lances, ye are sporting, Maruts, and rush along together like the waters.

5.60.d: वरा इवेद रैवतासो हिरण्यैर अभि सवधाभिस तन्वः पिपिश्रे | शरिये शरेयांसस तवसो रथेषु सत्रा महांसि चक्रिरे तनूषु ||
5.60.e: They, like young suitors, sons of wealthy houses, have with their golden natures decked their bodies.  Strong on their cars, the lordly Ones, for glory, have set their splendours on their forms for ever.

5.60.d: अज्येष्ठासो अकनिष्ठास एते सम भरातरो वाव्र्धुः सौभगाय | युवा पिता सवपा रुद्र एषां सुदुघा पर्श्निः सुदिना मरुद्भ्यः ||
5.60.e: None being eldest, none among them youngest, as brothers they have grown to happy fortune.  May their Sire Rudra, young and deft, and Pṛśni pouring much milk, bring fair days to the Maruts.

5.60.d: यद उत्तमे मरुतो मध्यमे वा यद वावमे सुभगासो दिवि षठ | अतो नो रुद्रा उत वा नव अस्याग्ने वित्ताद धविषो यद यजाम ||
5.60.e: Whether, O blessed Maruts, ye be dwelling in highest, midmost, or in lowest heaven,  Thence, O ye Rudras, and thou also, Agni, notice the sacrificial food we offer.

5.60.d: अग्निश च यन मरुतो विश्ववेदसो दिवो वहध्व उत्तराद अधि षणुभिः | ते मन्दसाना धुनयो रिशादसो वामं धत्त यजमानाय सुन्वते ||
5.60.e: O Maruts, Lords of all, when Agni and when ye drive downward from sublimest heaven along the heights,  Shakers of all, rejoicing, slayers of the foe, give riches to the Soma-pressing worshipper.

5.60.d: अग्ने मरुद्भिः शुभयद्भिर रक्वभिः सोमम पिब मन्दसानो गणश्रिभिः | पावकेभिर विश्वमिन्वेभिर आयुभिर वैश्वानर परदिवा केतुना सजूः ||
5.60.e: O Agni, with the Maruts as they gleam and sing, gathered in troop, rejoicing drink the Soma juice;  With these the living ones who cleanse and further all, joined with thy banner, O Vaiśvānara, from of old.

5.61.d: के षठा नरः शरेष्ठतमा य एक-एक आयय | परमस्याः परावतः ||
5.61.e: O HEROES lordliest of all, who are ye that have singly come  Forth from a region most remote?

5.61.d: कव वो ऽशवाः कव्र्भीशवः कथं शेक कथा यय | पर्ष्ठे सदो नसोर यमः ||
5.61.e: Where are your horses, where the reins? How came ye? how had ye the power?  Rein was on nose and seat on back.

5.61.d: जघने चोद एषां वि सक्थानि नरो यमुः | पुत्रक्र्थे न जनयः ||
5.61.e: The whip is laid upon the flank. The heroes stretch their thighs apart,  Like women when the babe is born.

5.61.d: परा वीरास एतन मर्यासो भद्रजानयः | अग्नितपो यथासथ ||
5.61.e: Go ye, O Heroes, far away, ye bridegrooms with a lovely Spouse  That ye may warm you at the fire.

5.61.d: सनत साश्व्यम पशुम उत गव्यं शतावयम | शयावाश्वस्तुताय या दोर वीरायोपबर्ब्र्हत ||
5.61.e: May she gain cattle for her meed, hundreds of sheep and steeds and kine,  Who threw embracing arms around the hero whom gyavaiva praised.

5.61.d: उत तवा सत्री शशीयसी पुंसो भवति वस्यसी | अदेवत्राद अराधसः ||
5.61.e: Yea, many a woman is more firm and better than the man who turns  Away from Gods, andoffers not.

5.61.d: वि या जानाति जसुरिं वि तर्ष्यन्तं वि कामिनम | देवत्रा कर्णुते मनः ||
5.61.e: She who discerns the weak and worn, the man who thirsts and is in want  She sets her mind upon the Gods.

5.61.d: उत घा नेमो अस्तुतः पुमां इति बरुवे पणिः | स वैरदेय इत समः ||
5.61.e: And yet full many a one, unpraised, mean niggard, is entitled man:  Only in weregild is he such.

5.61.d: उत मे ऽरपद युवतिर ममन्दुषी परति शयावाय वर्तनिम | वि रोहिता पुरुमीळ्हाय येमतुर विप्राय दीर्घयशसे ||
5.61.e: And she, the young, the joyous-spirited, divulged the path to Śyāva, yea, to me.  Two red steeds carried me to Purumīlha's side, that sage of far-extended fame,

5.61.d: यो मे धेनूनां शतं वैददश्विर यथा ददत | तरन्त इव मंहना ||
5.61.e: Him who, like Vaidadasvi, like Taranta, hath bestowed on me  A hundred cows in liberal gift.

5.61.d: य ईं वहन्त आशुभिः पिबन्तो मदिरम मधु | अत्र शरवांसि दधिरे ||
5.61.e: They who are borne by rapid steeds, drinking the meath that gives delight,  They have attained high glories here.

5.61.d: येषां शरियाधि रोदसी विभ्राजन्ते रथेष्व आ | दिवि रुक्म इवोपरि ||
5.61.e: They by whose splendour both the worlds are over-spread they shine on cars  As the gold gleams above in heaven.

5.61.d: युवा स मारुतो गणस तवेषरथो अनेद्यः | शुभंयावाप्रतिष्कुतः ||
5.61.e: That Marut band is ever young, borne on bright cars, unblamable,  Moving to victory, checked by none.

5.61.d: को वेद नूनम एषां यत्रा मदन्ति धूतयः | रतजाता अरेपसः ||
5.61.e: Who knoweth, verily, of these where the All-shakers take delight,  Born, spotless, after sacred Law?

5.61.d: यूयम मर्तं विपन्यवः परणेतार इत्था धिया | शरोतारो यामहूतिषु ||
5.61.e: Guides are ye, lovers of the song to mortal man through holy hymn,  And hearers when he cries for help.

5.61.d: ते नो वसूनि काम्या पुरुश्चन्द्रा रिशादसः | आ यज्ञियासो वव्र्त्तन ||
5.61.e: Do ye, destroyers of the foe, worshipful and exceeding bright,  Send down the treasures that we crave.

5.61.d: एतम मे सतोमम ऊर्म्ये दार्भ्याय परा वह | गिरो देवि रथीर इव ||
5.61.e: OUrmya, bear thou far away to Darbhya this my hymn of praise,  Songs, Goddess, as if chariot-borne.

5.61.d: उत मे वोचताद इति सुतसोमे रथवीतौ | न कामो अप वेति मे ||
5.61.e: From me to Rathaviti say, when he hath pressed the Soma juice,  The wish I had departeth not.

5.61.d: एष कषेति रथवीतिर मघवा गोमतीर अनु | पर्वतेष्व अपश्रितः ||
5.61.e: This wealthy Rathaviti dwells among the people rich in kine,  Among the mountains, far withdrawn.

5.62.d: रतेन रतम अपिहितं धरुवं वां सूर्यस्य यत्र विमुचन्त्य अश्वान | दश शता सह तस्थुस तद एकं देवानां शरेष्ठं वपुषाम अपश्यम ||
5.62.e: BY your high Law firm order is established there where they loose for travel Sūrya's horses.  Ten hundred stood together: there I looked on this the most marvellous Deities' one chief glory.

5.62.d: तत सु वाम मित्रावरुणा महित्वम ईर्मा तस्थुषीर अहभिर दुदुह्रे | विश्वाः पिन्वथः सवसरस्य धेना अनु वाम एकः पविर आ ववर्त ||
5.62.e: This, Mitra-Varuṇa, is your special greatness: floods that stood there they with the days attracted.  Ye cause to flow all voices of the cowpen: your single chariotfelly hath rolled hither.

5.62.d: अधारयतम पर्थिवीम उत दयाम मित्रराजाना वरुणा महोभिः | वर्धयतम ओषधीः पिन्वतं गा अव वर्ष्टिं सर्जतं जीरदानू ||
5.62.e: O Mitra-Varuṇa, ye by your greatness, both Kings, have firmly stablished earth and heaven,  Ye caused the cows to stream, the plants to flourish, and, scattering swift drops, sent down the rain-flood.

5.62.d: आ वाम अश्वासः सुयुजो वहन्तु यतरश्मय उप यन्त्व अर्वाक | घर्तस्य निर्णिग अनु वर्तते वाम उप सिन्धवः परदिवि कषरन्ति ||
5.62.e: Let your well-harnessed horses bear you hither: hitherward let them come with reins drawn tightly.  A covering cloud of sacred oil attends you, and your streams flow to us from days aforetime.

5.62.d: अनु शरुताम अमतिं वर्धद उर्वीम बर्हिर इव यजुषा रक्षमाणा | नमस्वन्ता धर्तदक्षाधि गर्ते मित्रासाथे वरुणेळास्व अन्तः ||
5.62.e: To make the lustre wider and more famous, guarding the sacred grass with veneration,  Ye, Mitra-Varuṇa, firm, strong, awe-inspiring, are seated on a throne amid oblations.

5.62.d: अक्रविहस्ता सुक्र्ते परस्पा यं तरासाथे वरुणेळास्व अन्तः | राजाना कषत्रम अह्र्णीयमाना सहस्रस्थूणम बिभ्र्थः सह दवौ ||
5.62.e: With hands that shed no blood, guarding the pious, whom, Varuni3, ye save amid oblations.  Ye Twain, together, Kings of willing spirit, uphold dominion based on thousand pillars.

5.62.d: हिरण्यनिर्णिग अयो अस्य सथूणा वि भराजते दिव्य अश्वाजनीव | भद्रे कषेत्रे निमिता तिल्विले वा सनेम मध्वो अधिगर्त्यस्य ||
5.62.e: Adorned with gold, its columns are of iron. in heaven it glitters like a whip for horses;  Or stablished on a field deep-spoiled and fruitful. So may we share the meath that loads your car-seat.

5.62.d: हिरण्यरूपम उषसो वयुष्टाव अयस्थूणम उदिता सूर्यस्य | आ रोहथो वरुण मित्र गर्तम अतश चक्षाथे अदितिं दितिं च ||
5.62.e: Ye mount your car gold-hued at break of morning, and iron-pillared when the Sun is setting,  And from that place, O Varuṇa and Mitra, behold infinity and limit~tion.

5.62.d: यद बंहिष्ठं नातिविधे सुदानू अछिद्रं शर्म भुवनस्य गोपा | तेन नो मित्रावरुणाव अविष्टं सिषासन्तो जिगीवांसः सयाम ||
5.62.e: Bountiful guardians of the world! the shelter that is impenetrable, strongest, flawless,  Aid us with that, O Varuṇa and Mitra, and when we long to win may we be victors.

5.63.d: रतस्य गोपाव अधि तिष्ठथो रथं सत्यधर्माणा परमे वयोमनि | यम अत्र मित्रावरुणावथो युवं तस्मै वर्ष्टिर मधुमत पिन्वते दिवः ||
5.63.e: GUARDIANS of Order, ye whose Laws are ever true, in the sublimest heaven your chariot ye ascend.  O Mitra-Varuṇa whomsoe’er ye: favour, here, to him the rain with sweetness streameth down from heaven.

5.63.d: सम्राजाव अस्य भुवनस्य राजथो मित्रावरुणा विदथे सवर्द्र्शा | वर्ष्टिं वां राधो अम्र्तत्वम ईमहे दयावाप्र्थिवी वि चरन्ति तन्यवः ||
5.63.e: This world's imperial Kings, O Mitra-Varuṇa, ye rule in holy synod, looking on the light.  We pray for rain, your boon, and immortality. Through heaven and over earth the thunderers take their way.

5.63.d: सम्राजा उग्रा वर्षभा दिवस पती पर्थिव्या मित्रावरुणा विचर्षणी | चित्रेभिर अभ्रैर उप तिष्ठथो रवं दयां वर्षयथो असुरस्य मायया ||
5.63.e: Imperial Kings, strong, Heroes, Lords of earth and heaven, Mitra and Varuṇa, ye ever active Ones,  Ye wait on thunder with the many-tinted clouds, and by the Asura's magic power cause Heaven to rain.

5.63.d: माया वाम मित्रावरुणा दिवि शरिता सूर्यो जयोतिश चरति चित्रम आयुधम | तम अभ्रेण वर्ष्ट्या गूहथो दिवि पर्जन्य दरप्सा मधुमन्त ईरते ||
5.63.e: Your magic, Mitra-Varuṇa, resteth in the heaven. The Sun, the wondrous weapon, cometh forth as light.  Ye hide him in the sky with cloud and flood of rain, and water-drops, Parjanya! full of sweetness flow.

5.63.d: रथं युञ्जते मरुतः शुभे सुखं शूरो न मित्रावरुणा गविष्टिषु | रजांसि चित्रा वि चरन्ति तन्यवो दिवः सम्राजा पयसा न उक्षतम ||
5.63.e: The Maruts yoke their easy car for victory, O Mitra-Varuṇa, as a hero in the wars.  The thunderers roam through regions varied in their hues. Imperial Kings, bedew us with the milk of heaven.

5.63.d: वाचं सु मित्रावरुणाव इरावतीम पर्जन्यश चित्रां वदति तविषीमतीम | अभ्रा वसत मरुतः सु मायया दयां वर्षयतम अरुणाम अरेपसम ||
5.63.e: Refreshing is your voice, O Mitra-Varuṇa: Parjanya sendeth out a wondrous mighty voice.  With magic power the Maruts clothe them with the clouds. Ye Two cause Heaven to rain, the red, the spotless One.

5.63.d: धर्मणा मित्रावरुणा विपश्चिता वरता रक्षेथे असुरस्य मायया | रतेन विश्वम भुवनं वि राजथः सूर्यम आ धत्थो दिवि चित्र्यं रथम ||
5.63.e: Wise, with your Law and through the Asura's magic power ye guard the ordinances, Mitra-Varuṇa.  Ye by eternal Order govern all the world. Ye set the Sun in heaven as a refulgent car.

5.64.d: वरुणं वो रिशादसम रचा मित्रं हवामहे | परि वरजेव बाह्वोर जगन्वांसा सवर्णरम ||
5.64.e: You, foeman-slaying Varuṇa and Mitra, we invoke with song,  Who, as with penfold of your arms, encompass round the realm of light.

5.64.d: ता बाहवा सुचेतुना पर यन्तम अस्मा अर्चते | शेवं हि जार्यं वां विश्वासु कषासु जोगुवे ||
5.64.e: Stretch out your arms with favouring love unto this man who singeth hymns,  For in all places is sung forth your evergracious friendliness.

5.64.d: यन नूनम अश्यां गतिम मित्रस्य यायाम पथा | अस्य परियस्य शर्मण्य अहिंसानस्य सश्चिरे ||
5.64.e: That I may gain a refuge now, may my steps be on Mitra's path.  Men go protected in the charge of this dear Friend who harms us not.

5.64.d: युवाभ्याम मित्रावरुणोपमं धेयाम रचा | यद ध कषये मघोनां सतोत्णां च सपूर्धसे ||
5.64.e: Mitra and Varuṇa, from you may I, by song, win noblest meed.  That shall stir envy in the homes of wealthy chiefs and those who praise.

5.64.d: आ नो मित्र सुदीतिभिर वरुणश च सधस्थ आ | सवे कषये मघोनां सखीनां च वर्धसे ||
5.64.e: With your fair splendours, Varuṇa and Mitra, to our gathering come,  That in their homes the wealthy chiefs and they who are your friends may thrive.

5.64.d: युवं नो येषु वरुण कषत्रम बर्हच च बिभ्र्थः | उरु णो वाजसातये कर्तं राये सवस्तये ||
5.64.e: With those, moreover, among whom ye hold your high supremacy,  Vouchsafe us room that we may win strength for prosperity and wealth.

5.64.d: उछन्त्याम मे यजता देवक्षत्रे रुशद्गवि | सुतं सोमं न हस्तिभिर आ पड्भिर धावतं नरा बिभ्रताव अर्चनानसम ||
5.64.e: When morning flushes, Holy Ones! in the Gods’ realm where white Cows shine,  Supporting Arcananas, speed, ye Heroes, with your active feet hither to my pressed Soma juice.

5.65.d: यश चिकेत स सुक्रतुर देवत्रा स बरवीतु नः | वरुणो यस्य दर्शतो मित्रो वा वनते गिरः ||
5.65.e: FULL wise is he who hath discerned: let him speak to us of the Gods,—  The man whose praise-songs Varuṇa the beautiful, or Mitra, loves.

5.65.d: ता हि शरेष्ठवर्चसा राजाना दीर्घश्रुत्तमा | ता सत्पती रताव्र्ध रतावाना जने-जने ||
5.65.e: For they are Kings of noblest might, of glorious fame most widely spread;  Lords of the brave, who strengthen Law, the Holy Ones with every race.

5.65.d: ता वाम इयानो ऽवसे पूर्वा उप बरुवे सचा | सवश्वासः सु चेतुना वाजां अभि पर दावने ||
5.65.e: Approaching you with prayer for aid, together I address you first  We who have good steeds call on you, Most Sage, to give us strength besides.

5.65.d: मित्रो अंहोश चिद आद उरु कषयाय गातुं वनते | मित्रस्य हि परतूर्वतः सुमतिर अस्ति विधतः ||
5.65.e: E’en out of misery Mitra gives a way to dwelling at our case,  For he who worships hath the grace of Mitra, fighter in the van. '

5.65.d: वयम मित्रस्यावसि सयाम सप्रथस्तमे | अनेहसस तवोतयः सत्रा वरुणशेषसः ||
5.65.e: In Mitra's shelter that extends to utmost distance may we dwell,  Unmenaced, guarded by the care, ever as sons of Varuṇa.

5.65.d: युवम मित्रेमं जनं यतथः सं च नयथः | मा मघोनः परि खयतम मो अस्माकम रषीणां गोपीथे न उरुष्यतम ||
5.65.e: Ye, Mitra, urge this people on, and to one end direct their ways.  Neglect not ye the wealthy chiefs, neglect not us the Ṛṣis: be our guardians when ye quaff the milk.

5.66.d: आ चिकितान सुक्रतू देवौ मर्त रिशादसा | वरुणाय रतपेशसे दधीत परयसे महे ||
5.66.e: O SAPIENT man, call the Two Gods, the very wise, who slay the foe.  For Varuṇa, whose form is Law, place offerings for his great delight.

5.66.d: ता हि कषत्रम अविह्रुतं सम्यग असुर्यम आशाते | अध वरतेव मानुषं सवर ण धायि दर्शतम ||
5.66.e: For they have won unbroken sway in full perfection, power divine.  And, like high laws, the world of man hath been made beautiful as light.

5.66.d: ता वाम एषे रथानाम उर्वीं गव्यूतिम एषाम | रातहव्यस्य सुष्टुतिं दध्र्क सतोमैर मनामहे ||
5.66.e: Therefore we praise you that your cars may travel far in front of ours-  You who accept the eulogy of Ratahavya with his hymns.

5.66.d: अधा हि काव्या युवं दक्षस्य पूर्भिर अद्भुता | नि केतुना जनानां चिकेथे पूतदक्षसा ||
5.66.e: And ye show wMom, Wondrous Gods with fulness of intellIgence.  By men's discernment are Ve marked, O ye whose might is purified.

5.66.d: तद रतम पर्थिवि बर्हच छरवेष रषीणाम | जरयसानाव अरम पर्थ्व अति कषरन्ति यामभिः ||
5.66.e: This is the Law sublime, O Earth: to aid the Ṛṣis’ toil for fame  The Two, wide-spreading, are prepared. They come with ample overflow.

5.66.d: आ यद वाम ईयचक्षसा मित्र वयं च सूरयः | वयचिष्ठे बहुपाय्ये यतेमहि सवराज्ये ||
5.66.e: Mitra, ye Gods with wandering eyes, would that the worshippers and we  Might strive to reach the realm ye rule, most spacious and protected well,

5.67.d: बळ इत्था देव निष्क्र्तम आदित्या यजतम बर्हत | वरुण मित्रार्यमन वर्षिष्ठं कषत्रम आशाथे ||
5.67.e: YE Gods, Ādityas, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Mitra, verily  Have here obtained supremest sway, high, holy, set apart for you.

5.67.d: आ यद योनिं हिरण्ययं वरुण मित्र सदथः | धर्तारा चर्षणीनां यन्तं सुम्नं रिशादसा ||
5.67.e: When, Varuṇa and Mitra, ye sit in your golden dwelling-place,  Ye Twain, supporters of mankind, foeslayers, give felicity.

5.67.d: विश्वे हि विश्ववेदसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा | वरता पदेव सश्चिरे पान्ति मर्त्यं रिषः ||
5.67.e: All these, possessors of all wealth, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,  Follow their ways, as if with feet, and guard from injury mortal man.

5.67.d: ते हि सत्या रतस्प्र्श रतावानो जने-जने | सुनीथासः सुदानवो ऽंहोश चिद उरुचक्रयः ||
5.67.e: For they are true, they cleave to Law, held holy among every race,  Good leaders, bounteous in their gifts, deliverers even from distress.

5.67.d: को नु वाम मित्रास्तुतो वरुणो वा तनूनाम | तत सु वाम एषते मतिर अत्रिभ्य एषते मतिः ||
5.67.e: Which of your persons, Varuṇa or Mitra, merits not our praise?  Therefore our thought is turned to you, the Atris' thought is turned to you.

5.68.d: पर वो मित्राय गायत वरुणाय विपा गिरा | महिक्षत्राव रतम बर्हत ||
5.68.e: SING forth unto your Varuṇa and Mitra with a song inspired.  They, Mighty Lords, are lofty Law

5.68.d: सम्राजा या घर्तयोनी मित्रश चोभा वरुणश च | देवा देवेषु परशस्ता ||
5.68.e: Full springs of fatness, Sovran Kings, Mitra. and Varuṇa, the Twain,  Gods glorified among the Gods.

5.68.d: ता नः शक्तम पार्थिवस्य महो रायो दिव्यस्य | महि वां कषत्रं देवेषु ||
5.68.e: So help ye us to riches, great terrestrial and celestial wealth:  Vast is your sway among the Gods.

5.68.d: रतम रतेन सपन्तेषिरं दक्षम आशाते | अद्रुहा देवौ वर्धेते ||
5.68.e: Carefully tending Law with Law they have attained their vigorous might.  The two Gods wax devoid of guile.

5.68.d: वर्ष्टिद्यावा रीत्य्र्पेषस पती दानुमत्याः | बर्हन्तं गर्तम आशाते ||
5.68.e: With rainy skies and streaming floods, Lords of the strength that bringeth gifts,  A lofty seat have they attained.

5.69.d: तरी रोचना वरुण तरींर उत दयून तरीणि मित्र धारयथो रजांसि | वाव्र्धानाव अमतिं कषत्रियस्यानु वरतं रक्षमाणाव अजुर्यम ||
5.69.e: THREE spheres of light, O Varuṇa, three heavens, three firmaments ye comprehend, O Mitra:  Waxed strong, ye keep the splendour of dominion, guarding the Ordinance that lasts for ever.

5.69.d: इरावतीर वरुण धेनवो वाम मधुमद वां सिन्धवो मित्र दुह्रे | तरयस तस्थुर वर्षभासस तिस्र्णां धिषणानां रेतोधा वि दयुमन्तः ||
5.69.e: Ye, Varuṇa, have kine who yield refreshment; Mitra, your floods pour water full of sweetness.  There stand the Three Steers, splendid in their brightness, who fill the three world-bowls with genial moisture.

5.69.d: परातर देवीम अदितिं जोहवीमि मध्यंदिन उदिता सूर्यस्य | राये मित्रावरुणा सर्वतातेळे तोकाय तनयाय शं योः ||
5.69.e: I call at dawn on Aditi the Goddess, I call at noon and when the Sun is setting.  I pray, O Mitra-Varuṇa, for safety, for wealth and progeny, in rest and trouble.

5.69.d: या धर्तारा रजसो रोचनस्योतादित्या दिव्या पार्थिवस्य | न वां देवा अम्र्ता आ मिनन्ति वरतानि मित्रावरुणा धरुवाणि ||
5.69.e: Ye who uphold the region, sphere of brightness, ye who support earth's realm Divine Ādityas,  The Immortal Gods, O Varuṇa and Mitra, never impair your everlasting statutes.

5.70.d: पुरूरुणा चिद धय अस्त्य अवो नूनं वां वरुण | मित्र वंसि वां सुमतिम ||
5.70.e: EVEN far and wide, O Varuṇa and Mitra, doth your grace extend.  May I obtain your kind good-will.

5.70.d: ता वां सम्यग अद्रुह्वाणेषम अश्याम धायसे | वयं ते रुद्रा सयाम ||
5.70.e: From you, benignant Gods, may we gain fully food for sustenance.  Such, O ye Rudras, my we be.

5.70.d: पातं नो रुद्रा पायुभिर उत तरायेथां सुत्रात्रा | तुर्याम दस्यून तनूभिः ||
5.70.e: Guard us, O Rudras. with your guar4 save us, ye skilled to save, my we  Subdue the Dasyus, we ourselves,

5.70.d: मा कस्याद्भुतक्रतू यक्षम भुजेमा तनूभिः | मा शेषसा मा तनसा ||
5.70.e: Or ne’er may we, O Wondrous Strong, enjoy another's solemn feast,  Ourselves, our sons, or progeny.

5.71.d: आ नो गन्तं रिशादसा वरुण मित्र बर्हणा | उपेमं चारुम अध्वरम ||
5.71.e: O Varuṇa and Mitra, ye who slay the foemen, come with might  To this our goodly sacrifice.

5.71.d: विश्वस्य हि परचेतसा वरुण मित्र राजथः | ईशाना पिप्यतं धियः ||
5.71.e: For, Varuṇa and Mitra, ye Sages are Rulers over all. Fill full our songs, for this ye can.

5.71.d: उप नः सुतम आ गतं वरुण मित्र दाशुषः | अस्य सोमस्य पीतये ||
5.71.e: Come to the juice that we have pressed. Varuṇa, Mitra, come to drink  This Soma of the worshipper.

5.72.d: आ मित्रे वरुणे वयं गीर्भिर जुहुमो अत्रिवत | नि बर्हिषि सदतं सोमपीतये ||
5.72.e: To Varuṇa and Mitra we offer with songs, as Atri did. Sit on the sacred grass to drink the Soma juice.

5.72.d: वरतेन सथो धरुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातयज्जना | नि बर्हिषि सदतं सोमपीतये ||
5.72.e: By Ordinance and Law ye dwell in peace secure, bestirring men.  Sit on the sacred grass to drink the Soma juice.

5.72.d: मित्रश च नो वरुणश च जुषेतां यज्ञम इष्टये | नि बर्हिषि सदतां सोमपीतये ||
5.72.e: May Varuṇa and Mitra, for our help, accept the sacrifice.  Sit on the sacred grass to drink the Soma juice.

5.73.d: यद अद्य सथः परावति यद अर्वावत्य अश्विना | यद वा पुरू पुरुभुजा यद अन्तरिक्ष आ गतम ||
5.73.e: WHETHER, O Aśvins, ye this day be far remote or near at hand,  In many spots or in mid-air, come hither, Lords of ample wealth.

5.73.d: इह तया पुरुभूतमा पुरू दंसांसि बिभ्रता | वरस्या याम्य अध्रिगू हुवे तुविष्टमा भुजे ||
5.73.e: These here, who show o’er widest space, bringing full many a wondrous act,  Resistless, lovingly I seek, I call the Mightiest to enjoy.

5.73.d: ईर्मान्यद वपुषे वपुश चक्रं रथस्य येमथुः | पर्य अन्या नाहुषा युगा मह्ना रजांसि दीयथः ||
5.73.e: Another beauteous wheel have ye fixed there to decorate your car.  With others through the realms ye roam in might unto the neighbouring tribes.

5.73.d: तद ऊ षु वाम एना कर्तं विश्वा यद वाम अनु षटवे | नाना जाताव अरेपसा सम अस्मे बन्धुम एयथुः ||
5.73.e: That deed of yours that is extolled, Visvas! hath all been done with this.  Born otherwise, and spotless, ye have entered kinship's bonds with us.

5.73.d: आ यद वां सूर्या रथं तिष्ठद रघुष्यदं सदा | परि वाम अरुषा वयो घर्णा वरन्त आतपः ||
5.73.e: When Sūrya mounted on your car that rolls for ever rapidly,  Birds of red hue were round about and burning splendours compassed you.

5.73.d: युवोर अत्रिश चिकेतति नरा सुम्नेन चेतसा | घर्मं यद वाम अरेपसं नासत्यास्ना भुरण्यति ||
5.73.e: Atri bethinks himself of you, O Heroes, with a friendly mind,  What time, Nāsatyas, with his mouth he stirs the spotless flame for you.

5.73.d: उग्रो वां ककुहो ययिः शर्ण्वे यामेषु संतनिः | यद वां दंसोभिर अश्विनात्रिर नराववर्तति ||
5.73.e: Strong is your swiftly moving steed, famed his exertion in the course  When by your great deeds, Aśvins, Chiefs, Atri is brought to us again.

5.73.d: मध्व ऊ षु मधूयुवा रुद्रा सिषक्ति पिप्युषी | यत समुद्राति पर्षथः पक्वाः पर्क्षो भरन्त वाम ||
5.73.e: Lovers of sweetness, Rudras, she who streams with sweetness waits on you.  When ye have travelled through the seas men bring you gifts of well-dressed food.

5.73.d: सत्यम इद वा उ अश्विना युवाम आहुर मयोभुवा | ता यामन यामहूतमा यामन्न आ मर्ळयत्तमा ||
5.73.e: Aśvins, with truth they call you Twain bestowers of felicity;  At sacrifice most prompt to hear, most gracious ye at sacrifice.

5.73.d: इमा बरह्माणि वर्धनाश्विभ्यां सन्तु शंतमा | या तक्षाम रथां इवावोचाम बर्हन नमः ||
5.73.e: Most pleasing to the Aśvins be these prayers which magnify their might,  Which we have fashioned, even as cars high reverence have we spoken forth.

5.74.d: कूष्ठो देवाव अश्विनाद्या दिवो मनावसू | तच छरवथो वर्षण्वसू अत्रिर वाम आ विवासति ||
5.74.e: WHERE in the heavens are ye to-day, Gods, Aśvins, rich in constancy?  Hear this, ye excellent as Steers: Atri inviteth you to come.

5.74.d: कुह तया कुह नु शरुता दिवि देवा नासत्या | कस्मिन्न आ यतथो जने को वां नदीनां सचा ||
5.74.e: Where are they now? Where are the Twain, the famed Nāsatyas, Gods in heaven?  Who is the man ye strive to reach? Who of your suppliants is with you?

5.74.d: कं याथः कं ह गछथः कम अछा युञ्जाथे रथम | कस्य बरह्माणि रण्यथो वयं वाम उश्मसीष्टये ||
5.74.e: Whom do ye visit, whom approach? to whom direct your harnessed car?  With whose devotions are ye pleased? We long for you to further us.

5.74.d: पौरं चिद धय उदप्रुतम पौर पौराय जिन्वथः | यद ईं गर्भीततातये सिंहम इव दरुहस पदे ||
5.74.e: Ye, Strengtheners, for Paura stir the filler swimming in the flood,  Advancing to be captured like a lion to the ambuscade.

5.74.d: पर चयवानाज जुजुरुषो वव्रिम अत्कं न मुञ्चथः | युवा यदी कर्थः पुनर आ कामम रण्वे वध्वः ||
5.74.e: Ye from cyavana worn with age removed his skin as ’twere a robe.  So, when ye made him young again, he stirred the longing of a dame.

5.74.d: अस्ति हि वाम इह सतोता समसि वां संद्र्शि शरिये | नू शरुतम म आ गतम अवोभिर वाजिनीवसू ||
5.74.e: Here is the man who lauds you both: to see your glory are we here.  Now bear me, come with saving help, ye who are rich in store of wealth.

5.74.d: को वाम अद्य पुरूणाम आ वव्ने मर्त्यानाम | को विप्रो विप्रवाहसा को यज्ञैर वाजिनीवसू ||
5.74.e: Who among many mortal men this day hath won you to himself?  What bard, accepters of the bard? Who, rich in wealth! with sacrifice?

5.74.d: आ वां रथो रथानां येष्ठो यात्व अश्विना | पुरू चिद अस्मयुस तिर आङगूषो मर्त्येष्व आ ||
5.74.e: O Aśvins, may your car approach, most excellent of cars for speed.  Through many regions may our praise pass onward among mortal men.

5.74.d: शम ऊ षु वाम मधूयुवास्माकम अस्तु चर्क्र्तिः | अर्वाचीना विचेतसा विभिः शयेनेव दीयतम ||
5.74.e: May our laudation of you Twain, lovers of meath! be sweet to you.  Fly hitherward, ye wise of heart, like falcons with your winged steeds.

5.74.d: अश्विना यद ध कर्हि चिच छुश्रूयातम इमं हवम | वस्वीर ऊ षु वाम भुजः पर्ञ्चन्ति सु वाम पर्चः ||
5.74.e: O Aśvins, when at any time ye listen to this call of mine,  For you is dainty food prepared: they mix refreshing food for you.

5.75.d: परति परियतमं रथं वर्षणं वसुवाहनम | सतोता वाम अश्विनाव रषि सतोमेन परति भूषति माध्वी मम शरुतं हवम ||
5.75.e: To meet your treasure-bringing car, the mighty car most dear to us,  Aśvins, the Ṛṣi is prepared, your raiser, with his song of praise. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: अत्यायातम अश्विना तिरो विश्वा अहं सना | दस्रा हिरण्यवर्तनी सुषुम्ना सिन्धुवाहसा माध्वी मम शरुतं हवम ||
5.75.e: Pass, O ye Aśvins, pass away beyond all tribes of selfish men,  Wonderful, with your golden paths, most gracious, bringers of the flood. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: आ नो रत्नानि बिभ्रताव अश्विना गछतं युवम | रुद्रा हिरण्यवर्तनी जुषाणा वाजिनीवसू माध्वी मम शरुतं हवम ||
5.75.e: Come to us, O ye Aśvin Pair, bringing your precious treasures, come  Ye Rudras, on your paths of gold, rejoicing, rich in store of wealth. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: सुष्टुभो वां वर्षण्वसू रथे वाणीच्य आहिता | उत वां ककुहो मर्गः पर्क्षः कर्णोति वापुषो माध्वी मम शरुतं हवम ||
5.75.e: O strong and Good, the voice of him who lauds you well cleaves to your car.  And that great beast, your chariot-steed, fair, wonderful, makes dainty food. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: बोधिन्मनसा रथ्येषिरा हवनश्रुता | विभिश चयवानम अश्विना नि याथो अद्वयाविनम माध्वी मम शरुतं हवम ||
5.75.e: Watchful in spirit, born on cars, impetuous, listing to his cry,  Aśvins, with winged steeds ye speed down to cyavana void of guile. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: आ वां नरा मनोयुजो ऽशवासः परुषितप्सवः | वयो वहन्तु पीतये सह सुम्नेभिर अश्विना माध्वी मम शरुतं हवम ||
5.75.e: Hither, O Heroes, let your steeds, of dappled hue, yoked at the thought,  Your flying steeds, O Aśvins, bring you hitherward, with bliss, to drink. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: अश्विनाव एह गछतं नासत्या मा वि वेनतम | तिरश चिद अर्यया परि वर्तिर यातम अदाभ्या माध्वी मम शरुतं हवम ||
5.75.e: O Aśvins, hither come to us; Nāsatyas, be not disinclined.  Through longing for the pious turn out of the way to reach our home. Lovers of sweetness, bear my call.

5.75.d: अस्मिन यज्ञे अदाभ्या जरितारं शुभस पती | अवस्युम अश्विना युवं गर्णन्तम उप भूषथो माध्वी मम शरुतं हवम ||
5.75.e: Ye Lords of Splendour, free from guile, come, stand at this our sacrifice.  Beside the singer, Aśvins, who longs for your grace and lauds you both. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: अभूद उषा रुशत्पशुर आग्निर अधाय्य रत्वियः | अयोजि वां वर्षण्वसू रथो दस्राव अमर्त्यो माध्वी मम शरुतं हवम ||
5.75.e: Dawn with her white herd hath appeared, and in due time hath fire been placed.  Harnessed is your immortal car, O WonderWorkers, strong and kind. Lovers of sweetness, bear my call.

5.76.d: आ भात्य अग्निर उषसाम अनीकम उद विप्राणां देवया वाचो अस्थुः | अर्वाञ्चा नूनं रथ्येह यातम पीपिवांसम अश्विना घर्मम अछ ||
5.76.e: AGNI, the bright face of the Dawns, is shining; the singers' pious voices have ascended.  Borne on your chariot, Aśvins, turn you hither and come unto our full and rich libation.

5.76.d: न संस्क्र्तम पर मिमीतो गमिष्ठान्ति नूनम अश्विनोपस्तुतेह | दिवाभिपित्वे ऽवसागमिष्ठा परत्य अवर्तिं दाशुषे शम्भविष्ठा ||
5.76.e: Most frequent guests, they scorn not what is ready: even now the lauded Aśvins are beside us.  With promptest aid they come at morn and evening, the worshipper's most blessed guards from trouble.

5.76.d: उता यातं संगवे परातर अह्नो मध्यंदिन उदिता सूर्यस्य | दिवा नक्तम अवसा शंतमेन नेदानीम पीतिर अश्विना ततान ||
5.76.e: Yea, come at milking-time, at early morning, at noon of day and when the Sun is setting,  By day, by night, with favour most auspicious. Not only now the draught hath drawn the Aśvins.

5.76.d: इदं हि वाम परदिवि सथानम ओक इमे गर्हा अश्विनेदं दुरोणम | आ नो दिवो बर्हतः पर्वताद आद्भ्यो यातम इषम ऊर्जं वहन्ता ||
5.76.e: For this place, Aśvins, was of old your dwelling, these were your houses, this your habitation.  Come to us from high heaven and from the mountain. Come from the waters bringing food and vigour.

5.76.d: सम अश्विनोर अवसा नूतनेन मयोभुवा सुप्रणीती गमेम | आ नो रयिं वहतम ओत वीरान आ विश्वान्य अम्र्ता सौभगानि ||
5.76.e: May we obtain the Aśvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance.  Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!

5.77.d: परातर्यावाणा परथमा यजध्वम पुरा गर्ध्राद अररुषः पिबातः | परातर हि यज्ञम अश्विना दधाते पर शंसन्ति कवयः पूर्वभाजः ||
5.77.e: FIRST worship those who come at early morning: let the Twain drink before the giftless niggard.  The Aśvins claim the sacrifice at daybreak: the sages yielding the first share extol them.

5.77.d: परातर यजध्वम अश्विना हिनोत न सायम अस्ति देवया अजुष्टम | उतान्यो अस्मद यजते वि चावः पूर्वः-पूर्वो यजमानो वनीयान ||
5.77.e: Worship at dawn and instigate the Aśvins: nor is the worshipper at eve rejected.  Besides ourselves another craves and worships: each first in worship is most highly favoured.

5.77.d: हिरण्यत्वङ मधुवर्णो घर्तस्नुः पर्क्षो वहन्न आ रथो वर्तते वाम | मनोजवा अश्विना वातरंहा येनातियाथो दुरितानि विश्वा ||
5.77.e: Covered with gold, meath-tinted, dropping fatness, your chariot with its freight of food comes hither,  Swift as thought, Aśvins, rapid as the tempest, wherewith ye travel over all obstructions.

5.77.d: यो भूयिष्ठं नासत्याभ्यां विवेष चनिष्ठम पित्वो ररते विभागे | स तोकम अस्य पीपरच छमीभिर अनूर्ध्वभासः सदम इत तुतुर्यात ||
5.77.e: He who hath served most often the Nāsatyas, and gives the sweetest food at distribution,  Furthers with his own holy works his offspring, and ever passes those whose flames ascend not.

5.77.d: सम अश्विनोर अवसा नूतनेन मयोभुवा सुप्रणीती गमेम | आ नो रयिं वहतम ओत वीरान आ विश्वान्य अम्र्ता सौभगानि ||
5.77.e: May we obtain the Aśvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance.  Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!

5.78.d: अश्विनाव एह गछतं नासत्या मा वि वेनतम | हंसाव इव पततम आ सुतां उप ||
5.78.e: YE Aśvins, hither come to us: Nāsatyas, be not disinclined.  Fly hither like two swans unto the juice we shed.

5.78.d: अश्विना हरिणाव इव गौराव इवानु यवसम | हंसाव इव पततम आ सुतां उप ||
5.78.e: O Aśvins, like a pair of deer, like two wild cattle to the mead:  Fly hither like two swans unto the juice we shed.

5.78.d: अश्विना वाजिनीवसू जुषेथां यज्ञम इष्टये | हंसाव इव पततम आ सुतां उप ||
5.78.e: O Aśvins rich in gifts, accept our sacrifice to prosper it:  Fly hither like two swans unto the juice we shed.

5.78.d: अत्रिर यद वाम अवरोहन्न रबीसम अजोहवीन नाधमानेव योषा | शयेनस्य चिज जवसा नूतनेनागछतम अश्विना शंतमेन ||
5.78.e: As Atri when descending to the cavern called on you loudly like a wailing woman.  Ye came to him, O Aśvins, with the freshest and most auspicious fleetness of a falcon.

5.78.d: वि जिहीष्व वनस्पते योनिः सूष्यन्त्या इव | शरुतम मे अश्विना हवं सप्तवध्रिं च मुञ्चतम ||
5.78.e: Tree, part asunder like the side of her who bringeth forth a child.  Ye Aśvins, listen to my call: loose Saptavadhri from his bonds.

5.78.d: भीताय नाधमानाय रषये सप्तवध्रये | मायाभिर अश्विना युवं वर्क्षं सं च वि चाचथः ||
5.78.e: For Saptavadhri, for the seer affrighted when he wept and wailed,  Ye, Aśvins, with your magic powers rent up the tree and shattered it.

5.78.d: यथा वातः पुष्करिणीं समिङगयति सर्वतः | एवा ते गर्भ एजतु निरैतु दशमास्यः ||
5.78.e: Like as the wind on every side ruffles a pool of lotuses,  So stir in thee the babe unborn, so may the ten-month babe descend.

5.78.d: यथा वातो यथा वनं यथा समुद्र एजति | एवा तवं दशमास्य सहावेहि जरायुणा ||
5.78.e: Like as the wind, like as the wood, like as the sea is set astir,  So also, ten-month babe, descend together with the after-birth.

5.78.d: दश मासाञ छशयानः कुमारो अधि मातरि | निरैतु जीवो अक्षतो जीवो जीवन्त्या अधि ||
5.78.e: The child who hath for ten months' time been lying in his mother's side,—  May he come forth alive, unharmed, yea, living from the living dame.

5.79.d: महे नो अद्य बोधयोषो राये दिवित्मती | यथा चिन नो अबोधयः सत्यश्रवसि वाय्ये सुजाते अश्वसून्र्ते ||
5.79.e: O HEAVENLY Dawn, awaken us to ample opulence to-day  Even as thou hast wakened us with Satyasravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: या सुनीथे शौचद्रथे वय औछो दुहितर दिवः | सा वय उछ सहीयसि सत्यश्रवसि वाय्ये सुजाते अश्वसून्र्ते ||
5.79.e: Daughter of Heaven, thou dawnedst on Sunitha Sucadratha's son,  So dawn thou on one mightier still, on Satyasravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: सा नो अद्याभरद्वसुर वय उछा दुहितर दिवः | यो वय औछः सहीयसि सत्यश्रवसि वाय्ये सुजाते अश्वसून्र्ते ||
5.79.e: So, bringing treasure, dawn to-day on us thou Daughter of the Sky,  As thou, O mightier yet. didst shine for Satyatravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: अभि ये तवा विभावरि सतोमैर गर्णन्ति वह्नयः | मघैर मघोनि सुश्रियो दामन्वन्तः सुरातयः सुजाते अश्वसून्र्ते ||
5.79.e: Here round about thee are the priests who laud thee, Bright One, with their hymns,  And men with gifts, O Bounteous Dame, splendid with wealth and offering much, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: यच चिद धि ते गणा इमे छदयन्ति मघत्तये | परि चिद वष्टयो दधुर ददतो राधो अह्रयं सुजाते अश्वसून्र्ते ||
5.79.e: Whatever these thy bands perform to please thee or to win them wealth,  E’en fain they gird us round and give rich gifts which ne’er are reft away, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: ऐषु धा वीरवद यश उषो मघोनि सूरिषु | ये नो राधांस्य अह्रया मघवानो अरासत सुजाते अश्वसून्र्ते ||
5.79.e: Give to these wealthy patrons fame, O affluent Dawn, with hero sons,  To these our princes who have brought rich gifts ne’er to be reft away, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: तेभ्यो दयुम्नम बर्हद यश उषो मघोन्य आ वह | ये नो राधांस्य अश्व्या गव्या भजन्त सूरयः सुजाते अश्वसून्र्ते ||
5.79.e: Bring lofty and resplendent fame, O thou munificent Dawn, to these  Our wealthy patrons who bestow rich gifts on us of steeds and kine, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: उत नो गोमतीर इष आ वहा दुहितर दिवः | साकं सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिः शुक्रैः शोचद्भिर अर्चिभिः सुजाते अश्वसून्र्ते ||
5.79.e: Bring us, O Daughter of the Sky, subsistence in our herds of kine,  Together with the sunbeams, with the shine of pure refulgent flames, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: वय उछा दुहितर दिवो मा चिरं तनुथा अपः | नेत तवा सतेनं यथा रिपुं तपाति सूरो अर्चिषा सुजाते अश्वसून्र्ते ||
5.79.e: O Daughter of the Sky, shine forth; delay not to perform thy task.  Let not the Sun with fervent heat consume thee like a robber foe, high-born! delightful with the steeds!

5.79.d: एतावद वेद उषस तवम भूयो वा दातुम अर्हसि | या सतोत्र्भ्यो विभावर्य उछन्ती न परमीयसे सुजाते अश्वसून्र्ते ||
5.79.e: So much, and more exceedingly, O Dawn, it suits thee to bestow,  Thou Radiant One who ceasest not to shine for those who sing thy praise, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!

5.80.d: दयुतद्यामानम बर्हतीम रतेन रतावरीम अरुणप्सुं विभातीम | देवीम उषसं सवर आवहन्तीम परति विप्रासो मतिभिर जरन्ते ||
5.80.e: THE singers welcome with their hymns and praises the Goddess Dawn who bringeth in the sunlight,  Sublime, by Law true to eternal Order, bright on her path, red-tinted, far-refulgent.

5.80.d: एषा जनं दर्शता बोधयन्ती सुगान पथः कर्ण्वती यात्य अग्रे | बर्हद्रथा बर्हती विश्वमिन्वोषा जयोतिर यछत्य अग्रे अह्नाम ||
5.80.e: She comes in front, fair, rousing up the people, making the pathways easy to be travelled.  High, on her lofty chariot, all-impelling, Dawn gives her splendour at the days' beginning.

5.80.d: एषा गोभिर अरुणेभिर युजानास्रेधन्ती रयिम अप्रायु चक्रे | पथो रदन्ती सुविताय देवी पुरुष्टुता विश्ववारा वि भाति ||
5.80.e: She, harnessing her car with purple oxen. injuring none, hath brought perpetual riches.  Opening paths to happiness, the Goddess shines, praised by all, giver of every blessing.

5.80.d: एषा वयेनी भवति दविबर्हा आविष्क्र्ण्वाना तन्वम पुरस्तात | रतस्य पन्थाम अन्व एति साधु परजानतीव न दिशो मिनाति ||
5.80.e: With changing tints she gleams in double splendour while from the eastward she displays her body.  She travels perfectly the path of Order, nor fails to reach, as one who knows, the quarters.

5.80.d: एषा शुभ्रा न तन्वो विदानोर्ध्वेव सनाती दर्शये नो अस्थात | अप दवेषो बाधमाना तमांस्य उषा दिवो दुहिता जयोतिषागात ||
5.80.e: As conscious that her limbs are bright with bathing, she stands, as ’twere, erect that we may see her.  Driving away malignity and darkness, Dawn, Child of Heaven, hath come to us with lustre.

5.80.d: एषा परतीची दुहिता दिवो नॄन योषेव भद्रा नि रिणीते अप्सः | वयूर्ण्वती दाशुषे वार्याणि पुनर जयोतिर युवतिः पूर्वथाकः ||
5.80.e: The Daughter of the Sky, like some chaste woman, bends, opposite to men, her forehead downward.  The Maid, disclosing boons to him who worships, hath brought again the daylight as aforetime.

5.81.d: युञ्जते मन उत युञ्जते धियो विप्रा विप्रस्य बर्हतो विपश्चितः | वि होत्रा दधे वयुनाविद एक इन मही देवस्य सवितुः परिष्टुतिः ||
5.81.e: THE priests of him the lofty Priest well-skilled in hymns harness their spirit, yea, harness their holy thoughts.  He only knowing works assigns their priestly tasks. Yea, lofty is the praise of Savitar the God.

5.81.d: विश्वा रूपाणि परति मुञ्चते कविः परासावीद भद्रं दविपदे चतुष्पदे | वि नाकम अख्यत सविता वरेण्यो ऽनु परयाणम उषसो वि राजति ||
5.81.e: The Sapient One arrays himself in every form: for quadruped and biped he hath brought forth good.  Excellent Savitar hath looked on heaven's high vault, and shineth after the outgoing of the Dawn.

5.81.d: यस्य परयाणम अन्व अन्य इद ययुर देवा देवस्य महिमानम ओजसा | यः पार्थिवानि विममे स एतशो रजांसि देवः सविता महित्वना ||
5.81.e: Even he, the God whose going-forth and majesty the other Deities have followed with their might,  He who hath measured the terrestrial regions out by his great power, he is the Courser Savitar.

5.81.d: उत यासि सवितस तरीणि रोचनोत सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिः सम उच्यसि | उत रात्रीम उभयतः परीयस उत मित्रो भवसि देव धर्मभिः ||
5.81.e: To the three spheres of light thou goest, Savitar, and with the rays of Sidrya thou combinest thee.  Around, on both sides thou encompassest the night: yea, thou, O God, art Mitra through thy righteous laws.

5.81.d: उतेशिषे परसवस्य तवम एक इद उत पूषा भवसि देव यामभिः | उतेदं विश्वम भुवनं वि राजसि शयावाश्वस ते सवित सतोमम आनशे ||
5.81.e: Over all generation thou art Lord alone: Pūṣan art thou, O God, in all thy goings-forth.  Yea, thou hast domination over all this world. Śyāvāśva hath brought praise to thee, O Savitar,

5.82.d: तत सवितुर वर्णीमहे वयं देवस्य भोजनम | शरेष्ठं सर्वधातमं तुरम भगस्य धीमहि ||
5.82.e: WE crave of Savitar the God this treasure much to be enjoyed.  The best, all-yielding, conquering gift of Bhaga we would gladly win.

5.82.d: अस्य हि सवयशस्तरं सवितुः कच चन परियम | न मिनन्ति सवराज्यम ||
5.82.e: Savitar's own supremacy, most glorious and beloved of all,  No one diminisheth in aught.

5.82.d: स हि रत्नानि दाशुषे सुवाति सविता भगः | तम भागं चित्रम ईमहे ||
